items.x: Hunter-gatherers in the Levant settle in round stone houses and harvest wild grain with flint sickles.
Caine kills Abel in the fields, is cursed, and goes into the wilderness east of Eden.
As farming begins, the Garou start to cull the growing human herds; the Impergium lasts about three thousand years (W20 pdf 71).
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: In the reckoning of the Fallen, the angels who loved humanity rebel against Heaven at the dawn of the human race and are cast down.
Hunter-gatherers in Japan make some of the world's oldest pottery.
In the lore of Ur and Babylon, Lilith is the first woman, Adam's equal, and is cast out of Eden into the unformed world (Revelations of the Dark Mother pdf 4).
The Fallen walk the young world openly and war with the loyal hosts; humans worship and fear them.
Late Ice Age hunters shelter in the caves of the Moravian Karst and follow reindeer and horse across the plain.
The cold snap called the Younger Dryas breaks; forests spread north and the great herds thin.
People settle by the spring at Jericho, one of the oldest continuously lived-in places.
Hunters raise carved stone pillars on a hill in Anatolia, a sacred place built before farming.

items.t: The carved beasts on the hill
items.x: The foxes, vultures and boars carved at Gobekli Tepe are read by Garou lorekeepers as a caern raised in honour of the Fera.
In the wilderness Caine finds Lilith, who teaches the first powers of the blood and is later betrayed.
Bound to a crone by her blood, Caine in turn gives Zillah his blood for three nights and marries her (Book of Nod pdf 12-13).
Lilith's cult, the Bahari, keep her teaching; in their telling Caine's line turns on her for thirteen generations (Revelations of the Dark Mother pdf 4-5).
Wheat, barley and lentils are first sown on purpose in the hills of the Fertile Crescent.
The dead of the first villages linger in the Shadowlands, with no city or ferryman to guide them.
Hunters with fluted spear points have spread through both Americas.
Herders in the Zagros keep the first tame goats.
Wild aurochs and mouflon are bred into cattle and sheep in Anatolia and the upper Euphrates.

items.t: The laws of the First City
items.x: Caine forbids the Second Generation to make more childer; the command is broken.
After the Time of Atrocities and the Long March, the war of Heaven and the Fallen calms into the Time of Babel (Houses of the Fallen pdf 19, 73).

items.t: The wall and tower of Jericho
items.x: Jericho's people build a stone wall and round tower, among the first public works anywhere.
The Second Generation Embrace the thirteen who will be remembered as the Antediluvians.
Caine founds Enoch and Embraces the Second Generation; mortals and the childer live under one ruler.
Rice is first farmed along the middle Yangtze in China.

items.t: Squash and gourds in the Americas
items.x: People in the Americas begin to grow squash and gourds.

items.t: The Fallen cast into the Abyss
items.x: The rebel angels are locked away in the Abyss; a few escape the binding as the Earthbound.

items.t: The antler masks of Star Carr
items.x: Hunters by a lake in Yorkshire wear red-deer antler headdresses, perhaps for rites.
In some tellings the Third Generation kill their own sires after the Flood; in others the Second simply vanish.
A town of mud-brick houses entered through the roofs grows on the Konya plain, home to several thousand.
Some Noddists claim the bull horns and vulture paintings of Catalhoyuk mark a town that fed the First City.
Villagers near Amman shape tall plaster figures with staring eyes.
Farming families cross from Anatolia into Greece and the Balkans.
A farming village rises at Mehrgarh below the Bolan Pass, ancestor of the Indus cities.
Villagers at Jiahu in China play flutes of crane bone and scratch signs on tortoise shell.
Sixteen tribes meet and agree to end the Impergium, nearly nine thousand years before the modern nights (W20 pdf 40-41, 71).
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Garou lorekeepers tell that the Wyld, the Weaver and the Wyrm once kept the balance, before the Weaver went mad and bound the Wyrm.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.t: The rock paintings of the Sahara
items.x: Herders paint cattle, giraffes and dancers on the rocks of a green Sahara.
The people of Jericho keep their dead's skulls, rebuilt in plaster with shell eyes.
Wraith lore holds that the plastered skulls of Jericho were Fetters, keeping the first dead close to the living.
Caught in the Weaver's web, the Wyrm goes mad and splits into Beast-of-War, Eater-of-Souls and the Defiler (W20 Book of the Wyrm pdf 12-14).
After the Impergium the Fera rise against the Garou, and the Garou turn on the changing breeds; many lines are hunted near to their end (Tribebook Silent Striders pdf 16).
Mages remember the Mythic Age as a time before consensus, when gods and spirits answered common people.
The rising sea covers the low land between Britain and the continent.
In Kithain legend the fae live beside mortals, and the Dreaming touches every field.
A sudden cooling lasting two centuries strains the first farms of Europe and the Near East.
Farmers in southern Mesopotamia dig canals from the rivers to water their fields.
A great flood destroys Enoch; the Second Generation die or vanish, and their childer rule the ruins.
The Kuei-jin speak of the oldest age, when the courts of Heaven and the Yomi kept the Great Cycle turning.
Bands of hunters and fishers still live by the rivers of Moravia before the farmers come.
Fishers by the Danube's Iron Gates carve river-stone heads with fish faces.
After the Flood, Brujah Embraces Troile, who will later destroy the sire (V20 Dark Ages pdf 45).
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: Some scholars hold that the Black Sea filled quickly from the Mediterranean about now, drowning its shore villages.
Linear Pottery farmers settle the loess plains of southern Moravia in long timber houses.
The first fields cut into the Moravian woods; Garou of the region mark where the farmers may go and where they may not.

items.t: The long houses and their dead
items.x: The Linear Pottery farmers of Moravia bury their dead beside the villages, crouched with pots and adzes.
The Baali begin in the Second City; their leader leads them against it and is beaten back (V20 pdf 402).
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: At Talheim in Germany a whole farming community is killed and buried in one pit.
The Third Generation raise a new city after the Flood, each ruling a quarter with their own childer.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: Eridu, held by later Sumerians to be the first city of kings, builds its first temple to the water god Enki.
Painted-pottery villages spread along the Yellow River.
Farmers in Mexico breed maize from the wild grass teosinte.
The Ratkin say they were made to keep the human herds small, and took to the first cities when the Impergium ended.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Villagers at Hemudu near the Yangtze mouth build timber houses on stilts and grow rice.
Potters of the Vinca culture scratch signs on clay that some take for an early script.
Farmers of central Europe build great round ditched enclosures, some of them in Moravia, perhaps for gatherings and rites.
Stone tombs and standing stones rise in Brittany.
The Encyclopaedia records a War of Rage fought across Siberia.
Farmers of southern Moravia make clay figurines of women for their homes and shrines.
A grave at Varna on the Black Sea holds the oldest worked gold yet found.
The tales of the Kithain place the Mythic Age in the time when the long stone rows of Carnac were raised.
Smiths in the Balkans smelt copper; the Copper Age begins.
The Bastet keep courts among the city kings of Sumer, as their tales hold.
Each rebuilding raises Eridu's temple higher, toward the later ziggurat.

items.t: The oldest leaf of the Book of Nod
items.x: By the reckoning of the book's own scholar, its oldest fragment was written just before Sumer (Book of Nod pdf 19).

items.t: The quarrels of the Third Generation
items.x: The rulers of the Second City feud over power and their childer, and the city's peace frays.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: Ubaid culture spreads from southern Mesopotamia up the rivers and along the Gulf.
Thousands of standing stones are set in rows at Carnac.
Saulot, founder of the Salubri, studies in the Second City and travels east to seek the end of the Beast.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: The Brujah say their founder Troile prized the Second City above all and fought its fall.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: The first wheels turn in Mesopotamia and on the steppe.
Steppe people north of the Black Sea begin to keep and ride horses.

items.t: The fall of the Second City
items.x: The Second City falls to war and the childer's revolt; the Antediluvians scatter across the world.
lk: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

items.x: The green Sahara turns to desert; herders move toward the Nile and the south.
Farmers of the Lengyel culture build fortified villages in southern Moravia.
The Botai people of the Kazakh steppe keep herds of horses.
After the Second City, the Third Generation go their ways: some to the mountains, some to the rivers, some into the sea of mortal peoples.
The founder of the Tzimisce leaves the ruins for the mountains to the north, toward the Carpathians.

items.t: The hill folk of the Alps
items.x: Herders cross the high passes of the Alps with copper axes and flint.
Nosferatu tales tell how their founder was made monstrous by Caine's anger for the deeds of the Second City.
Copper tools reach Moravian farmers through trade from the Balkans.
Uruk becomes the largest city in the world, with tens of thousands living inside its walls.
The Silent Striders are cursed by Sutekh and can no longer rest in Egypt, as the Encyclopaedia records.
Islanders on Malta build great stone temples.
Farmers in Ireland raise passage tombs in the Boyne valley.

items.t: The potter's wheel and the plough
items.x: Sumerians use the fast potter's wheel and the ox-drawn plough.
The towns of Upper Egypt grow rich under chiefs buried with painted pots.
In the legend of the Reborn, Osiris rules the Two Lands as a god-king, with Isis beside the throne.
The Silent Striders keep their oldest home among the shrines of the Nile.
The Encyclopaedia records a council that judged quarrels among the changing breeds.
The Baden culture's villages spread through Moravia, with wheeled carts and copper.
Steppe herders bury their chiefs under earth mounds called kurgans.

items.t: The first Gangrel run with the herds
items.x: The Gangrel tell that their founder ran with the horse peoples of the steppe, far from any city.
Herders from the steppe begin to push west into central Europe.
The Get of Fenris and their kin lose a great northern hold, as the Encyclopaedia records.
A man is shot with an arrow and dies on a pass in the Alps; the ice keeps the body for five thousand years.
The bear-changers refuse to fight the Garou or to teach them; the Encyclopaedia keeps the tale.

items.t: The scattered childer reach the rivers
items.x: Deduced: Set is ruling in Egypt by about 3000 BCE (Mummy 1st pdf 64) and the Baali hold Sumerian cities, so the Antediluvians' scattering after the Second City has reached the river kingdoms by 3300 BCE.
Scribes at Uruk press signs into clay tablets to keep the temple's accounts, the start of writing.
The first hieroglyphs are written in Upper Egypt.
Set kills Osiris and scatters the body across Egypt, and takes the throne.
Isis gathers the pieces of Osiris and, with the help of the gods, works the Spell of Life; Osiris rises.
The Followers of Set tell that their founder walked among the first kings of Egypt and was worshipped as a god.
A dishonour of the War of Rage the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The passage tomb at Newgrange is built so the midwinter sunrise lights its inner chamber.
Kithain call the Boyne tombs the first hollow hills, doors of the sidhe long before the Sundering.

items.t: The War of Rage ends in Egypt
items.x: Deduced: Rage Across Egypt has Egypt united only after the War of Rage (pdf 25), so the killing is over along the Nile before Narmer, about 3200 BCE.
The king of Upper Egypt takes the Delta; the Narmer Palette shows the first king of a single Egypt.
Horus, son of Osiris and Isis, wars with Set for the throne of Egypt.
Farmers on Orkney build the stone village of Skara Brae, with stone beds and dressers.
A carved alabaster vase from Uruk shows a procession bringing offerings to Inanna.
A circular bank and ditch is dug on Salisbury Plain; the stones come later.
Ur, Uruk, Lagash, Kish and Nippur grow into rival city-states, each with its own god.
Osiris shares the Spell of Life with chosen followers, the first of the Reborn who serve Horus.
In the reckoning of the Fallen, the gods the Sumerians worship are half-remembered faces of angels from before the Fall.
Towns of the Indus valley begin building with baked brick.
The Akashic Brotherhood counts its oldest roots among hermits in the mountains above the Indus.
Garou and Fera together bind great Banes in this age, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Scribes at Susa write in their own signs.
People of the Copper Age bury some of their dead in the caves of the Moravian Karst.
As more Cainites come to Egypt, Set's rule of the land weakens (Mummy 1st pdf 64).
A deep layer of river silt at Shuruppak marks a great flood, the kind later remembered in the flood stories.
Herders who bury their dead with corded beakers and stone battle-axes settle across Moravia.
The early kings of Egypt are buried at Abydos with their servants.
Uruk's walls reach nine kilometres, later credited to Gilgamesh.
Walled towns of black polished pottery rise along the Yellow River.

items.t: The First Comers to the Amazon
items.x: The changing breeds of the great forest settle the Amazon long before the Garou, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: The First Comers to the Amazon
The Amazon War and the Balam

items.x: The Sumerian king list names Kish as the first city to hold kingship after the flood.
Gilgamesh, later the hero of the oldest written epic, rules Uruk about now.
Egypt's Old Kingdom begins, the age of the great pyramids.
The jade-working city of Liangzhu near the Yangtze mouth is abandoned, perhaps after floods.
Imhotep builds the step pyramid for King Djoser at Saqqara, the first great stone building.
Later Hermetic masters honour Imhotep as a founder of the arts of building, healing and writing.
Egypt keeps a calendar of 365 days in three seasons tied to the Nile flood.
The kings and queens of Ur are buried with gold, lyres and dozens of attendants.
The great Indus cities lay out straight streets, drains and granaries.
The ravens tell how they were scorched black in the War of Rage; the Encyclopaedia keeps the tale.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The city of Caral in the Peruvian desert raises platform mounds, the oldest city of the Americas.
The Great Pyramid of Khufu is finished at Giza, the tallest building on earth for nearly four thousand years.
The Shemsu-heru know the pyramid fields as places where the walls between the living and the dead are thin.
The Sphinx is carved from the bedrock at Giza.
The great sarsen circle and the trilithons are raised at Stonehenge.
The Fianna sing that the stone circles of Britain were raised over caerns, and that the rings still answer the moon.
Bell Beaker pottery and copper daggers spread from Iberia to Britain and central Europe.
Garou and Fera keep a truce at Lagash in Sumer for a time, before the War of Rage returns.
The great stone halls of the Ness of Brodgar stand between two stone rings on Orkney.
Bell Beaker people settle in Moravia beside the Corded Ware herders.
Mohenjo-daro's builders make a large waterproof brick bath, perhaps for rites.
Deduced: Earthbound says mortal sorcerers freed them thousands of years ago (pdf 13-18), and the oldest priest-kings are Sumer's, so the first are taken to wake about 2500 BCE.
Eannatum of Lagash defeats Umma and sets up a stone showing vultures over the dead.
Urukagina of Lagash curbs the greed of priests and officials, the first known law reform.

items.t: The War of Rage seen by ravens
items.x: The Corax's own telling of the War of Rage, as the Encyclopaedia records.
Spells for the dead king's rise to the stars are carved inside the pyramid of Unas.
The Reborn read the Pyramid Texts as a clumsy echo of the true Spell of Life.
Thousands of clay tablets at Ebla in Syria record a trading city's business.
The Sumerian king list names Kubaba, a tavern keeper, as the only woman to rule Kish.
Sargon founds the Akkadian empire, the first to rule all Mesopotamia.
Some Ventrue claim that their line advised the first kings of Akkad; the Brujah call it a boast.
Sargon's daughter Enheduanna, high priestess at Ur, writes hymns to Inanna, the first author known by name.
The Unetice culture works bronze in Bohemia and Moravia and trades tin and amber across central Europe.
Indus traders sail to Sumer with carnelian beads; Sumerians call the land Meluhha.
Pepi II rules Egypt for perhaps ninety years; the Old Kingdom weakens.
A drought lasting decades strikes from Egypt to the Indus; Akkad collapses.
The Old Kingdom breaks apart into rival provinces after low Nile floods.
The Ananasi tell of their own losses in the War of Rage.
A great stone-walled town rises on the loess at Shimao in northern China.
Mountain raiders called the Gutians overrun Akkad.
Ur-Nammu rebuilds Sumer, raises the great ziggurat of Ur and issues a law code.
The oldest surviving law code sets fines in silver for injuries.
King Shulgi of Ur sets up a road network with rest houses and standard weights.
Chinese tradition places the first dynasty, the Xia, and the flood-tamer Yu the Great about now.
The Kuei-jin say the first dynasty was founded when the dragons of the rivers were bargained with, not beaten.
Mentuhotep II reunites Egypt from Thebes.
The Minoans build the first palaces at Knossos and Phaistos.
Garou tales of the War of Rage place a hidden lair of the changing breeds under the palace hills of Crete.
Chariots with spoked wheels appear on the steppe east of the Urals.
Peoples speaking an early Greek settle the Greek mainland.
The Garou wipe out the Bunyip of the far south, a crime the Encyclopaedia records.
The Unetice dead are buried crouched on their sides with bronze pins and rings.
The fortified towns of Sintashta on the steppe bury warriors with chariots.
The Ainu people's ancestors live in the northern islands of Japan.
Kindred of the East places the Ainu in the islands by this age, with their own bond to the spirits (Kindred of the Thousand Hells pdf 44).
Merchants from Assur keep a trading colony at Kanesh in Anatolia, sending tin and cloth.
The great Indus cities shrink as rivers shift and trade fails.
Chiefs on the chalk downs of Wessex are buried with gold and amber.
Baltic amber passes through Moravia toward the south.
Hebrew tradition places the patriarch Abraham's journey from Ur to Canaan about now.
An Amorite dynasty takes Babylon, then a small town.
The Baali tell that their first sire drew power from things older than Caine in the swamps of southern Mesopotamia.
Egyptian scribes copy problems of fractions and areas, later gathered in the Rhind papyrus.
Fera who flee the War of Rage hide among human peoples, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The palace archive of King Zimri-Lim at Mari records spies, prophets and diplomacy.
Babylonian scribes work in base sixty and know Pythagoras' rule a thousand years early.
The Followers of Set grow strong in the cult centres of the Delta, as the Encyclopaedia records.
Hammurabi takes the throne of Babylon and spends thirty years making it an empire.
Hammurabi has his laws carved on a basalt stele: an eye for an eye, set by rank.
Bronze axes, rings and ingots are buried in hoards across Moravia, as offerings or savings.
Wraiths of the Unetice dead are said to linger over the hoards buried with their names.
Mari's letters record ecstatic prophets who carry messages from the gods to the king.
The Babylonian city of Mashkan-shapir is emptied, perhaps after a change in the river.
In Baali lore their city of Mashkan-shapir falls and the elder Nergal moves to Ashur (Clanbook Baali pdf 23-24).
A bronze disc inlaid with gold sun, moon and stars is buried on a hill in Germany.
Earthquakes wreck the Cretan palaces; they are rebuilt grander than before.
The Nubian city of Kerma rules the middle Nile and rivals Egypt.
Foreign kings called the Hyksos rule the Nile Delta, bringing the horse and chariot to Egypt.
The Hyksos kings honour Set at Avaris; the Followers of Set count this a high time of their cult.
The volcano of Thera blows apart, burying the town of Akrotiri in ash and sending waves across the Aegean.
Kithain tales speak of a shining island of the Mythic Age lost to fire and sea; scholars point to Thera.
The Shang dynasty rules the Yellow River plain from walled capitals.
Mycenae's kings are buried with gold masks.
A Garou moot whose vote was never counted, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Shang diviners crack ox bones and turtle shells with heat and write the questions on them, China's oldest writing.
The Kuei-jin say the Shang kings spoke with true ancestors through the cracks, and the spirits answered.
Bronze Age settlements in Moravia gain ditches and palisades.
The Hittite king Mursili I raids down the Euphrates and sacks Babylon.
Ahmose I drives out the Hyksos; Egypt's New Kingdom begins.
The Shemsu-heru are said to have fought beside Ahmose's army against the Followers of Set in the Delta.
Egyptians begin to bury spells for the afterlife on papyrus, later called the Book of the Dead.
Deduced: Mummy's sample Reborn are born about 2600 and 1273 BCE (Mummy 1st pdf 12, 69-77), so the Reborn are many by the New Kingdom.
Peoples speaking an Indo-Aryan tongue settle north India; the hymns of the Rigveda take shape.
Egypt's kings begin to be buried in hidden tombs in the Valley of the Kings.
Central Europeans bury their dead under earth mounds, the barrows of the Bronze Age.
Bronze Age barrows crown the ridges of Moravia; the Garou of the land take some for caerns and leave others well alone.
Mycenaean builders raise walls of stones so large later Greeks thought giants had moved them.
Hatshepsut takes the throne of Egypt as king and rules for about twenty years.

items.t: The Reed of Thoth and the Cupbearers of Isis
items.x: Hatshepsut and Thutmose III call a gathering that founds two lodges of magicians (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 20).
Hatshepsut's ships sail down the Red Sea to Punt and bring back incense trees and ebony.
Thutmose III defeats a league of Canaanite kings at Megiddo, the first battle recorded in detail.
Mycenaean Greeks take over the palace of Knossos and its Linear B scribes.
Some Cainite legends place an elder of the beast-blooded clans in the halls under Knossos.
The kingdom of Mitanni rules northern Mesopotamia with chariot lords.
Kings of Egypt, Babylon, Mitanni and the Hittites write to each other as brothers and trade gold for horses.
The Encyclopaedia records the Bone Gnawers' tale of being the last and lowliest tribe.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Scribes at Ugarit write an alphabet in cuneiform signs.
Within a century the two Egyptian lodges split into more than a hundred rival sects (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 20).
The Reborn remember Akhenaten's reign, which the books put at 1364 to 1347 BCE, as a time when the old rites of the dead were shut away and the Shemsu-heru hid.
Akhenaten puts the sun disc Aten above all other gods and builds a new capital at Amarna.
Ashur-uballit I makes Assyria a great power.
Thinkers of the Ganges plain begin the speculation later written in the Upanishads.
The sculptor Thutmose carves the painted bust of Queen Nefertiti.
The boy king Tutankhamun abandons Amarna and restores the old gods.
Tutankhamun dies young and is buried with a small but rich tomb that robbers miss.
Central Europeans begin to burn their dead and bury the ashes in urns in large cemeteries.
Hillforts ringed with earth and timber are built on the heights of Moravia.
Burning the dead changes nothing for the wraiths of Moravia's urnfields, who gather in the shadow of the cemeteries.
An old battle site of the Garou, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The Shang queen and general Fu Hao leads armies and is buried with hundreds of bronzes.
Ramesses II begins a reign of sixty-six years and carves his temples at Abu Simbel.
Egyptians and Hittites fight the largest chariot battle known at Kadesh; both claim victory.
Ramesses II and the Hittite king Hattusili III sign a peace treaty, copies of which survive in both tongues.
The citadel of Troy is sacked about now, the event that may lie behind the Iliad.
Thousands fight at a river crossing in northern Germany, the oldest large battle known in Europe.
A people called Israel is first named in Canaan, on a stone of Pharaoh Merneptah in 1208.
In later hunter lore the judges and prophets of Israel are the first mortals remembered for standing against the night's creatures by faith alone.
The standard version of the Epic of Gilgamesh is written down.
Hattusa is abandoned and burned; the Hittite empire breaks up.
The Olmec build their first ceremonial centre at San Lorenzo and carve colossal stone heads.
The Pure Ones tell that their tribes held the lands across the ocean long before the Garou of Europe came, with their own peace among the breeds.
lk: The Shadow Lords in the Americas

items.t: The Caern of the Fallen Star
items.x: A caern raised where a star fell, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The hymns of the Rigveda reach their final form, though still learned by heart.

items.t: Bronze hoards of the Urnfield age
items.x: Moravian smiths bury hoards of sickles, axes and scrap bronze.
The palace of Pylos burns, baking its clay records hard.
Hermetic historians trace the first Greek oracles to the oak of Dodona, older than Delphi.

items.t: Ramesses III fights the Sea Peoples
items.x: Ramesses III turns back the Sea Peoples in a battle on the Nile Delta, carved on the walls of Medinet Habu.
Ugarit, Mycenae, Pylos and many other cities fall to raiders, drought and quakes; trade and writing vanish across the region.
The fall of the Bronze Age cities sends old Cainites into long sleep; some claim the collapse was a war among them.
The Elamites sack Babylon and carry off the Code of Hammurabi and the statue of Marduk.
Tomb robbers in the Valley of the Kings are tried and confess.
Greece loses its palaces and writing; people live in small villages for three centuries.
Tyre, Sidon and Byblos rise as sea-trading cities.
Iron tools and weapons spread through the Levant and Anatolia.
An old wound to the Garou, as the Encyclopaedia records.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Tiglath-Pileser I campaigns to the Mediterranean and hunts lions and wild bulls.
The Zhou begin the divination system later written down as the Yijing.

items.t: Cold iron and the first Sundering
items.x: Deduced: cold iron is the fae's bane and the Sundering parts dream from flesh (C20 pdf 34-36), so the Sundering is taken to begin as iron spreads, about 1100 BCE in the Levant.
Egypt splits between the priest-kings of Thebes and kings in the Delta.
The Philistine cities of the coast fight Israel's tribes.
King Wu of Zhou defeats the last Shang king at Muye; the Zhou claim the Mandate of Heaven.
The Kuei-jin date their weakness to sunlight from the Chou, and tell that the Japanese spirit Mikaboshi advised the new dynasty (KotE pdf 12).
David makes Jerusalem the capital of Israel.
The Phoenicians write with an alphabet of 22 letters, the ancestor of Greek and Latin writing.
The Vedic hymns are gathered and the kingdoms of the Ganges plain grow.
The first fire-priests of the Iranian plateau tend their altars, later honoured as a root of the Celestial Chorus and the Ahl-i-Batin.
Hillforts multiply in central Europe as chiefs compete.
Kithain legend sets the great war of the Tuatha against the Fomorians in this age, long before the Sundering.
The Encyclopaedia's tale of a breed ordained by both sun and moon.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: Large urnfield cemeteries spread across southern Moravia below the Palava hills.
Camels carry frankincense and myrrh from south Arabia north to the Levant.
Many scholars place the prophet Zarathustra between 1500 and 1000 BCE on the steppe.
The Encyclopaedia's account of Zarathustra and the first Adversary belongs here.
Solomon builds the first temple in Jerusalem.
Fallen and Earthbound alike tell stories of the king who bound spirits with a ring and a name.
Shoshenq I, of Libyan descent, takes Egypt's throne and raids Judah.
The kingdom of Saba grows rich on incense in south Arabia.
Horus, with allies from the west, drives Set out of Egypt (Mummy 1st pdf 65).
After Solomon the kingdom splits into Israel in the north and Judah in the south.
Akashic and Euthanatos masters begin a war in the mountains that runs, by one count, to 300 BCE (M20 pdf 123; Sorcerers Crusade pdf 68).
Kushite kings at Napata on the upper Nile build their own kingdom.
The temple centre of Chavin draws pilgrims in the high Andes.
Iron-using villages of central Italy grow into the Etruscan cities.
An old lair at Krapina tied to the spider queen, as the Encyclopaedia records.

The Encyclopaedia's schisms among the mages begin about now.
Oldrich of Bohemia, through his son Bretislav, takes Moravia from Poland, between 1019 and 1029.
Tremere and the inner circle become Cainites in 1022 (House of Tremere pdf 23; V20 Dark Ages pdf 63).
Bretislav rules Moravia for his father.
Bretislav I becomes duke of Bohemia and Moravia.
Goratrix rules the Tremere seat from 1037 to 1133 (House of Tremere pdf 26-28).
Bretislav sacks Gniezno and carries off the relics of Adalbert.

items.t: The schism of East and West
items.x: The legates of Rome and the patriarch of Constantinople excommunicate each other.
lk: The White Howlers' War with Rome

items.x: Bretislav's rule of succession gives Bohemia to the eldest, Moravia's parts to younger sons.
Moravia is shared among Premyslid princes at Olomouc, Brno and Znojmo.
The bishopric of Olomouc is restored.
William of Normandy wins England at Hastings.
The Seljuks defeat the eastern Romans at Manzikert.
Henry IV kneels in the snow at Canossa before Pope Gregory VII.
Vratislaus II is crowned king of Bohemia for his lifetime.
The Encyclopaedia places Cainites among the taifa kingdoms of Spain.
Pope Urban II calls the First Crusade.
Crusaders passing through Prague attack its Jews.
The crusaders take Jerusalem and kill much of its people.
The Encyclopaedia's Weeks of Blood follow the fall of Jerusalem.
lk: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

items.t: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
items.x: The Encyclopaedia places Cainites in the new crusader kingdom.
lk: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

items.x: The Tremere make the first gargoyles for their war with the Tzimisce (V20 Dark Ages pdf 83).
Sobeslav I of Bohemia defeats the German king Lothar at Chlumec.
About a century before the 1230 setting of Dark Ages: Fae, the fae swear the Oath-Truce, which is near its end by that year (Dark Ages: Fae pdf 8, 25, 40).
Tremere drinks the soul of Saulot in 1133 (V20 Dark Ages pdf 41).
Ardan, of the Tremere chantry in Prague, is Embraced (House of Tremere pdf 82).
The Moravian princes rise against Duke Vladislaus II and besiege Prague.
Zengi takes Edessa; the Second Crusade follows.
Frederick Barbarossa makes Vladislaus II king of Bohemia.
Saladin takes power in Egypt.
The Lombard cities beat Barbarossa at Legnano.
Barbarossa makes Moravia a margraviate under the emperor, held by Conrad Otto.
Bohemians and Moravians fight at Loditz; Moravia returns to Bohemia's rule.
Saladin destroys the crusader army at Hattin and takes Jerusalem.
Barbarossa, Richard I and Philip II set out for the Holy Land.
Barbarossa drowns crossing the Saleph in Anatolia.
Premysl Ottokar takes the Bohemian throne, losing it again in 1193.
The Encyclopaedia's massacre at Orvieto falls here.
Henry VI plans to make the empire hereditary; he dies at Messina the next year.
Henry VI dies of fever at Messina; the empire falls into a contest between Philip of Swabia and Otto of Brunswick.
Vladislaus Henry yields Bohemia to his brother Ottokar and takes Moravia as margrave.
Lothar of Segni becomes Innocent III, the most powerful pope of the age, and soon calls a new crusade.
Rival princes elect Philip of Swabia and Otto IV; ten years of civil war follow across the German lands.
Premysl Ottokar I takes the title of king, which the Golden Bull of 1212 later confirms.
Richard I of England dies of a crossbow wound at the siege of Chalus; John takes the throne.

items.t: The Courts of Love take note
items.x: Philip II of France grows stronger against the English kings; the Toreador of the Grand Court watch the balance shift toward Paris.
The first Kamakura shogun dies after a fall from a horse; the Hojo family begin to rule for his heirs.
Philip II grants the scholars of Paris rights against the city's officers, the start of the university's privileges.
Hermetic masters take rooms among the Paris scholars, and the craftsmen who will become the Order of Reason do the same.

items.t: Venice agrees to carry the crusade
items.x: The Treaty of Venice binds the Fourth Crusade to pay for a fleet it cannot afford.
Leonardo of Pisa publishes the Liber Abaci, bringing Hindu-Arabic numerals to European merchants.

items.t: The first crusader assault on Constantinople
items.x: Crusaders storm the city's sea walls and restore Isaac II and Alexios IV; the bargain cannot be paid.
A fire set during fighting burns a broad swath of Constantinople; tens of thousands lose their homes.
Hojo Tokimasa becomes regent to the shogun, and the regents rule Japan in fact.
Alexios Doukas Mourtzouphlos strangles Alexios IV and defies the crusaders.
The crusaders break in and loot for three days; Cainites of every clan flee or burn with their havens, and the Dream ends.
Relics, books and treasures from the sack flood into Venice, Paris and the Rhineland; mages hunt for the true ones among the fakes.
Theodore Laskaris gathers Byzantine refugees at Nicaea and founds a successor state.
The Komnenos brothers found an empire on the Black Sea coast with Georgian help.
Philip II takes Rouen and Normandy from King John.
The Bulgarian tsar Kaloyan destroys the Latin army and captures Emperor Baldwin I, who dies in prison.
Henry of Flanders becomes Latin emperor and rules the conquered lands with skill.
Qutb ud-Din Aibak, a slave general, founds the Mamluk dynasty of Delhi.

items.t: The khan's oath under the Eternal Blue Sky
items.x: Temujin is proclaimed Genghis Khan; the courts of the Middle Kingdom take the omens of the steppe seriously.
The conqueror of northern India is murdered on the Indus; his generals divide the empire.
Innocent III names Stephen Langton Archbishop of Canterbury against King John's wishes.
The papal legate Peter of Castelnau is killed near Saint-Gilles; the pope calls a crusade against the Cathars.
The pope lays England under interdict: no masses, no church burials, for six years.
Simon de Montfort takes Carcassonne; inquirers ride with the army and learn which questions make people confess.
Pope Innocent approves the brotherhood of Francis; the Franciscans begin.
Scholars fleeing a riot at Oxford settle at Cambridge.

The Albigensian Crusade sacks Beziers on 22 July 1209. Southern France learns what a crusade at home means, and the Church learns how to hunt heresy by inquiry. Fits: Fits the heretical end times card of 1206.
items.ref: Real history (sack of Beziers, 1209).

items.x: A council at Paris forbids lecturing on Aristotle's natural philosophy; the ban is widely ignored.
Iltutmish takes the throne of Delhi and holds northern India against the Mongols.
Genghis Khan invades the Jin empire and wins at Badger Mouth.
King Andrew II of Hungary settles the Teutonic Order in the Burzenland to guard the passes.
Christian kings of Spain crush the Almohads; the reconquest of al-Andalus speeds up.
Bands of children and the poor march toward the sea; few come home, and some Kindred along the road grow fat.
Simon de Montfort kills Peter II of Aragon at Muret; the south loses its strongest protector.
Hungarian nobles kill Andrew II's queen for favouring her German kin.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.x: Philip II beats Otto IV and his allies; John's hopes of retaking Normandy end, and Otto's empire collapses.
The Mongols take the Jin capital (Beijing) and burn it for a month.
The council requires yearly confession, defines transubstantiation and orders Jews and Muslims to wear distinct dress.

items.t: Rabbat in the fall of Zhongdu
items.x: Genghis Khan takes the Jin capital Zhongdu in 1215. Rabbat, already old, lives through the killing and is carried off as a Mongol captive. Fits: The book places it in the Mongol sweep through the Chin Empire in the early 13th century.
items.ref: Kindred Most Wanted p. 20 (the captivity); the fall of Zhongdu, 1215, is real history; the year is a house reading.

items.x: John dies during the barons' war; the boy Henry III is crowned and William Marshal rules for him.
Pope Honorius III confirms the Order of Preachers founded by Dominic.
The great pope dies at Perugia; Kindred who shaped the Curia through him must start again.
William Marshal routs the French-backed rebels at Lincoln; Prince Louis gives up the English crown.
Crusaders gather at Acre, then turn on Egypt.
The governor of Otrar kills a Mongol trade caravan; Genghis Khan resolves on war with Khwarazm.
The crusaders take Damietta after a long siege; disease has killed most of the city.
The Mongol host enters Khwarazm; Garou of the Silk Road watch the land fill with ash and carrion spirits.
Danes conquering Estonia win at Lyndanisse; legend says the Danish flag fell from the sky.
Samarkand surrenders and is plundered; its craftsmen are carried off to Mongolia.
Pope Honorius III crowns Frederick II in Rome.
Work begins on the new cathedral at Salisbury.
Tolui's army takes Merv and kills nearly every inhabitant; chroniclers write of hundreds of thousands dead.
After a Mongol prince dies in its siege, Nishapur is razed and even its animals killed.
The crusaders, trapped by the Nile's flood, give up Damietta.
Jalal al-Din of Khwarazm escapes Genghis Khan by riding his horse into the river.
Andrew II grants the Hungarian nobles their rights, including the right to resist an unjust king.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.x: Scholars leaving Bologna found a new school at Padua.
Mongol scouts under Subutai destroy the Rus princes on the Kalka; the Rus forget the warning, and the Shadow Lords do not.
Philip II of France dies after 43 years; Louis VIII takes the throne.
The pope approves the final rule of the Franciscans.
The emperor founds a school at Naples to train lawyers and officials for his kingdom.
Francis of Assisi is said to receive the wounds of Christ; the Messianic Voices count it a sign.
The Livonian crusaders take Tartu; the Get of Fenris and the Shadow Lords of the Baltic mark the last pagan groves burning.
Henry III reissues Magna Carta in its lasting form in return for a tax.
The Tran family takes the throne of Dai Viet.
Francis dies at the Portiuncula; canonised two years later.
The king dies on his way back from the Albigensian campaign; Blanche of Castile rules for the boy Louis IX.
Frederick II grants the Teutonic Order the lands it can conquer in Prussia.
Genghis Khan dies during the war on the Xi Xia, who are destroyed; the courts of the East mark the death of the scourge.
North German princes break Danish power in the Baltic.
Ugolino of Segni becomes pope and excommunicates Frederick II within months.
Excommunicated, Frederick II sails for the Holy Land anyway.
The excommunicated emperor reaches the Holy Land.
Sultan al-Kamil hands Jerusalem to Frederick II by treaty, without a battle.
The Albigensian war ends; Toulouse submits and the Inquisition arrives in the south.
A church council at Toulouse sets out how to search out heretics and bans the Bible in the common tongue.

Frederick II gets Jerusalem back by treaty in February 1229, without a battle. Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut among the city's Cainites, watches the Franks return. Fits: Same year as Camilla and Cretheus in Rome.
items.ref: Real history (Treaty of Jaffa, 1229); Gabriel Chavez from Jerusalem by Night (Dark Ages) p. 62; the year is a house reading.

items.x: Ferdinand III unites the crowns of Castile and Leon for good.
The Teutonic Knights begin their war against the pagan Prussians from Kulm.
Gregory IX sends inquisitors answerable to the pope, most of them Dominicans.
Frederick II issues a law code for the Kingdom of Sicily.
The first of many Mongol invasions of Korea begins.
Conrad of Marburg burns suspects across Germany; the shadow Inquisition in the Empire takes note of his methods.

items.t: The Korean court flees to Ganghwa
items.x: The Goryeo court moves to Ganghwa Island and holds out there for decades.

items.t: Kaifeng and the thunder crash bombs
items.x: The Jin defend Kaifeng with gunpowder bombs and fire lances; plague kills hundreds of thousands in the city.
Knights kill the inquisitor on the road; his terror ends.
The Mongols and the Song take the last Jin city; the last Jin emperor dies.
Ogedei Khan builds walls and a palace at Karakorum, the Mongol capital.
Ferdinand III takes Cordoba; the great mosque becomes a cathedral.
Batu and Subutai destroy Volga Bulgaria.
Razia becomes Sultan of Delhi, the only woman to rule it.
The first Rus city falls to Batu's host.
The Sword Brothers, beaten by the Lithuanians, join the Teutonic Order as its Livonian branch.
Word of the riders in the Rus lands reaches the voivodes of the Carpathians; most do not believe it.
The Mongols take Vladimir and burn the grand prince's family in the cathedral.
Grand Prince Yuri II is killed and his army destroyed.
James I of Aragon takes Valencia.
Muhammad I founds the Nasrid kingdom of Granada, the last Muslim state in Spain.
Pope and emperor go to open war in Italy.
The Mongols take Chernigov and Pereyaslavl.
Prince Alexander of Novgorod beats a Swedish force and is called Nevsky.
Batu's army storms Kiev; the mother of Rus cities is ruined, and Cainites who held it scatter.
The Rus princes submit to the Golden Horde; the Shadow Lords' quiet backing of the Mongols begins.
A Mongol column burns Krakow; legend says a trumpeter was shot mid-call from the church tower.
The Mongols destroy Duke Henry II of Silesia's army, Teutonic and Templar knights among it.
Batu and Subutai destroy the Hungarian army; King Bela IV flees to the Adriatic.

items.t: Ogedei dies and the horde turns back
items.x: Word of the great khan's death reaches the army in Hungary; the Mongols withdraw, and the Tzimisce and the Garou of the plains count their dead.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.x: The two cities agree to guard the road between them, the seed of the Hanseatic League.
After Mohi the Mongols burn Pest and range across Hungary all summer.
A Mongol column crosses Moravia, burning villages and failing before Olomouc.

items.t: Mohi and the burning of Pest
items.x: The Mongols beat the Hungarian army at Mohi on 11 April 1241 and burn Pest. Vencel Rikard's plan to make Buda-Pest the greatest city of the region goes up with it, for a time. Fits: Fits the Mongol invasion card of 1241.
items.ref: Real history (Battle of Mohi, 1241); Vencel Rikard from Transylvania by Night (Dark Ages) p. 105; the setback is a house reading.

items.x: Alexander Nevsky beats the Livonian Knights on frozen Lake Peipus.
Batu sets his capital at Sarai on the Volga; the Rus princes must travel there for leave to rule.
Mongol riders chase King Bela to the coast at Trogir.
The Mongols break the Seljuk sultanate of Rum.
The new pope flees to Lyon to escape Frederick II.
More than two hundred Cathars are burned below the mountain fortress; the Inquisition calls it victory, and the Inquisition is wrong to call it the end.
Khwarazmian horsemen take and wreck Jerusalem.
lk: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

items.x: An Egyptian and Khwarazmian army destroys the crusader host near Gaza.
The Council of Lyon declares the emperor deposed.
John of Plano Carpini sets out for the Mongol court as the pope's envoy.

items.t: The friars' mission to the Mongols
items.x: The Council of Lyon sends friars east to learn what the Mongols want.
Guyuk becomes great khan with Carpini watching.
Duke Frederick of Austria dies in battle; Austria is left without a lord.

items.t: The Sakya lama and the Mongols
items.x: Sakya Pandita submits Tibet to Godan Khan, the first tie between Tibet and the Mongols.
Ferdinand III takes Seville after a long siege.
The foundation stone of the new cathedral is laid; it will not be finished for six hundred years.
Louis IX consecrates his glass chapel for the Crown of Thorns; the Celestial Chorus calls it a true house of the One.
The Akashic Brotherhood in Tibet watches the lamas bargain with the khans and keeps its own counsel.
Louis IX takes Damietta again.
The silver town of Jihlava writes down its mining code.
The crusaders break into Mansourah and are cut down in its streets by the Mamluks under Baibars.
The French king is taken prisoner and ransomed.
Mamluk officers kill the last Ayyubid sultan of Egypt.
The stupor mundi dies in Apulia; Hohenstaufen power soon collapses.
Bela IV orders stone castles built across Hungary against the Mongols' return.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.x: In February 1250 the army of Louis IX is trapped at Mansourah and broken. Tariq fights in the city's defence; later Tariq serves the Old Man of the Mountain. Fits: The book ties it to the Seventh Crusade.
items.ref: Kindred Most Wanted p. 68; the battle of Mansourah, 1250, is real history.

items.x: After a bitter assembly Mongke is raised as great khan and purges Ogedei's line.
Ottokar of Bohemia takes Austria and marries the Babenberg heiress.
Florence strikes the gold florin, soon the standard coin of European trade.
Mindaugas of Lithuania is baptised and crowned, though Lithuania stays pagan.
The Flemish friar reaches the great khan's court and debates Buddhists, Muslims and Nestorians there.
Kublai conquers the kingdom of Dali in Yunnan.
Premysl Ottokar II becomes King of Bohemia, the iron and golden king.
With Conrad IV dead, the empire has no accepted ruler for almost twenty years.
The Teutonic Knights found Konigsberg, named for Ottokar of Bohemia.
The monk Nichiren preaches that the Lotus Sutra alone can save Japan.
Hulegu takes Alamut and the Nizari strongholds; Kindred in the east say the Assamites did not stir, because their Alamut is not this one.
lk: Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

items.x: Rhineland towns band together to keep the peace on the river roads.

Hulegu's Mongols take the Nizari castle of Alamut in December 1256. Kindred in the east note that the Assamites did not stir: whatever their Alamut is, it is not this one. Fits: Leaves the Assamite Alamut of the books untouched.
items.ref: Real history (fall of Alamut, 1256); the Kindred reading is a house rule.

items.x: Robert de Sorbon founds a college for poor theology students in Paris.
The electors choose both Richard of Cornwall and Alfonso X of Castile.
The Mongols take Baghdad, kill the caliph and throw the libraries into the Tigris; Batini carry out what they can.
English barons force Henry III to share power with a council.
Jalal ad-Din Rumi begins the Masnavi at Konya.
Hulegu has the last Abbasid caliph rolled in a carpet and trampled; the Cainites of Baghdad who lived through the sack go into the desert.
The Mongols sack Baghdad in February 1258; the libraries go into the Tigris. Batini carry out what they can before the walls fall. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (sack of Baghdad, 1258); the Batini are a house reading.

items.x: Henry III gives up his claims to Normandy and Anjou and keeps Gascony as Louis IX's vassal.
The great khan dies besieging a Song fortress; the Mongol armies in Syria and China pause.
The Goryeo crown prince submits to the Mongols.
Hulegu takes Aleppo and Damascus; the Mamluks are next.
The Mamluks under Qutuz and Baibars beat the Mongols in Galilee; the mummies of Egypt call it a reprieve for the river.
Baibars murders Qutuz on the road home and takes the throne.
Ottokar II of Bohemia beats the Hungarians and takes Styria.
Bands of penitents whip themselves through the towns of Italy; the Church is unsure whether to bless them or hunt them.
Kublai and his brother Ariq Boke are both proclaimed great khan; civil war splits the empire.

items.t: The Byzantines take back the city
items.x: Michael VIII Palaiologos's general walks into Constantinople almost without a fight; Latin rule ends, but the Dream does not return.
Baibars sets up an Abbasid survivor as caliph in Cairo to bless Mamluk rule.
The Icelandic chieftains accept the Norwegian king.
Scots and storms drive off a Norwegian fleet; the Hebrides pass to Scotland three years later.
The prince dies returning from the Horde.
Simon de Montfort captures Henry III and his son Edward.
Urban IV makes the feast of Corpus Christi a feast of the whole Church.
Simon de Montfort calls knights and burgesses from towns to parliament.
Prince Edward kills Simon de Montfort and cuts the body to pieces.
Baibars takes the crusader towns of the coast one by one.
Charles of Anjou kills King Manfred and takes Sicily and Naples.

items.t: Roger Bacon writes for the pope
items.x: Roger Bacon sends Clement IV his great work on experiment and optics; the craftsmen of the future Order of Reason study it.
Baibars takes Safed from the Templars and kills the garrison.
The painter Giotto di Bondone is born near Florence.
Charles of Anjou defeats Conradin, then beheads the sixteen-year-old in Naples.
Baibars takes Antioch and kills or enslaves its people; the crusader principality ends.
Kublai adopts a new script for all the empire's languages.
The Eighth Crusade ends when the French king dies of dysentery outside Tunis.
Kublai Khan proclaims the Great Yuan and builds a new capital at Khanbaliq (Beijing).
Marco Polo leaves Venice with his father and uncle for the court of Kublai.
The Hospitallers give up their great castle to Baibars.
Korean soldiers who will not submit to the Mongols hold out on Jeju until 1273.
Edward I becomes king of England while still on crusade.
The German princes choose Rudolf of Habsburg as king, ending the interregnum.
The poet dies at Konya; the whirling dervishes of the Mevlevi order grow from his followers.
Persian engineers' counterweight trebuchets end a five-year siege; the road into southern China is open.
Aquinas dies on the way to the Council of Lyon, his Summa unfinished.

items.t: The first Mongol fleet against Japan
items.x: A Mongol and Korean fleet lands at Hakata and then sails off in a storm; the kami are said to have answered.
The Greek envoys accept union with Rome; their church at home does not.
Bonaventure dies during the council; the Messianic Voices lose a friend in the Church's councils.
The Song capital surrenders to the Mongol general Bayan.
Rudolf of Habsburg forces Ottokar II to surrender Austria and Styria.
Bishop Tempier condemns 219 philosophical propositions, many drawn from Aristotle and Averroes.
Llywelyn ap Gruffudd is forced to terms.
Rudolf of Habsburg kills Ottokar II of Bohemia; Austria passes to the Habsburgs.
The last Song fleet is destroyed at Yamen and the boy emperor drowns; Kuei-jin speak of a turning of the age.
Dinis of Portugal plants pine forests and founds the university at Lisbon.

items.t: Black Earth Boy and the end of the Song
items.x: The last Song fleet is lost at Yamen in 1279. In those years Black Earth Boy rises to the Hundred Clouds, as the Fourth Age turns. Fits: Before the Treaty of the Quincunx, 1304.
items.ref: Dharma Book: Thrashing Dragons p. 18 (the rise); the year is a house reading; the battle of Yamen, 1279, is real history.

items.x: The Dominican master of natural philosophy dies at Cologne.
Guo Shoujing's astronomers produce the most exact calendar yet made.
A typhoon wrecks the second, far larger Mongol invasion of Japan; priests and spirits both claim the storm.
The Mamluks beat the Mongols and their Armenian and Georgian allies.
Two Mongol fleets sent against Japan, in 1274 and 1281, are wrecked by storms. Japan's priests and its spirits both claim the victory. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1274, 1281); the claim is a house reading.

items.x: Palermo rises against the French at vespers on Easter Monday; Sicily passes to Aragon.
The last native Prince of Wales dies in a skirmish; Wales is conquered.
Edward I begins Caernarfon, Conwy and Harlech to hold Wales.
The Teutonic Knights finish the conquest of the Prussians.

items.t: The stolen children are not found
items.x: No one finds Hamelin's children; changelings in the German lands keep the tale close.
One hundred and thirty children vanish from Hamelin; the town's records blame a piper, and the fae say nothing.
Genoa destroys the Pisan fleet; Pisa never recovers.
Philip IV becomes King of France.

items.t: Venice and Genoa fight at Acre
items.x: The Italian quarters of Acre are at war with each other.
The king of Scots falls from his horse in a storm; Scotland is left with a child queen in Norway.
A storm surge drowns tens of thousands along the Dutch and German coast.
A Mongol army ends the kingdom of Pagan in Burma.
The burghers of Cologne and their allies break the archbishop's power.
Tran Hung Dao destroys a Mongol fleet on staked river beds in Vietnam.
The Mamluks take Tripoli in Lebanon.
Edward I orders all Jews out of England; they will not be readmitted for over three centuries.
The child queen of Scotland dies on her way from Norway; Edward I is asked to judge between the claimants.
The Mamluks storm Acre and the crusader kingdom ends; Kindred of the Military Orders sail for Cyprus with the survivors.
Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swear to defend each other, the start of the Swiss Confederation.
A Mongol fleet lands in Java; the Majapahit state rises from the fighting.
Edward I picks John Balliol as King of Scots.
Raden Wijaya uses the Mongols to destroy a rival, then drives them out and founds Majapahit.
The hermit pope resigns after five months; Boniface VIII follows him.
The great khan dies; his empire no longer obeys one ruler.
The Ilkhan Ghazan becomes Muslim, and the Mongols of Persia follow.
The Polos come home to Venice after twenty-four years.
Edward I takes Berwick and kills many of its people; Scotland is conquered.
Alauddin Khalji murders his uncle and takes Delhi; he will beat back several Mongol invasions.
William Wallace and Andrew Moray destroy an English army.
Francesco Grimaldi, disguised as a monk, seizes the rock of Monaco.
Edward I breaks Wallace's army.
A prisoner of Genoa, Marco Polo tells his travels to the writer Rustichello.
Ghazan's Mongols beat the Mamluks near Homs and briefly take Damascus.
Osman's frontier state in Bithynia grows; the Ottomans take their name from him.
Osman's beylik grows on the Byzantine border; Kindred of the Bosporus do not yet think it worth watching.
Boniface VIII proclaims a holy year; pilgrims crowd Rome for full pardon of sins.
Wenceslas II reforms the Bohemian coinage on Kutna Hora silver.
Andrew III dies; the Arpad kings of Hungary are gone.
lk: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

items.x: Dante Alighieri is banished from Florence and begins the Divine Comedy in exile.
Flemish townsmen kill the French garrison of Bruges at dawn.
Flemish militia destroy the French knights at Courtrai.
Boniface VIII declares that every creature must be subject to the pope.
Osman beats a Byzantine army, his first great victory.
Philip the Fair's men seize Boniface VIII; the pope dies weeks later.
The Mamluks beat Ghazan's last invasion of Syria.
Alauddin Khalji takes the Rajput fortress of Chittor.
In the year the Quincunx is signed, mortal China lies quiet under the Yuan; the courts take it as proof the treaty works.
William Wallace is hanged, drawn and quartered at Smithfield.
Bertrand de Got becomes Clement V and never goes to Rome.
Robert Bruce kills a rival and is crowned King of Scots.
Philip IV expels the Jews from France and takes their goods.
Wenceslas III is murdered at Olomouc; the Bohemian royal line ends.
On Friday 13 October Philip IV has every Templar in France seized; some say Cainite counsellors or Batini with grudges guided the king.
Edward I dies on his way north to fight Bruce; Edward II takes the throne.
The Teutonic Knights seize Danzig and kill many of its people.
Albert of Habsburg is killed by his nephew.
Clement V settles in Avignon; the popes will stay for nearly seventy years, and the Kindred of Rome lose their nearest grip on the Church.
The Teutonic grand master moves to Marienburg, the largest brick castle in Europe.
The Knights of St John make Rhodes their island base.
John of Luxembourg marries the Premyslid heiress and is chosen King of Bohemia.
The council meets to decide the fate of the Templars.
Clement V dissolves the Order of the Temple and gives its lands to the Hospitallers.
The Mamluk sultan's third reign begins; Cairo reaches its height.
The emperor dies of fever, ending hopes of restoring imperial rule in Italy.
The last Grand Master is burned on an island in the Seine; the tale of a curse on king and pope spreads when both die that year.
Robert Bruce routs Edward II's army.
The king dies after a hunting fall, months after de Molay's death.

Jacques de Molay is burned in Paris on 18 March 1314. The tale that the Grand Master cursed king and pope from the fire, and that both died within the year, runs through Europe. Fits: Follows the fall of the Temple, 1307.
items.ref: Real history (1314); the curse is a legend.

items.x: Swiss peasants ambush and destroy a Habsburg army.
Years of rain ruin the harvests of northern Europe; as many as one in ten die by 1317.
De Varre founds the Solificati, the alchemists who will break away from the Order of Reason.
The Avignon pope who will condemn magic and the Spiritual Franciscans takes office.
John XXII believes enemies tried to kill him with wax images; trials for sorcery follow.
With the herds starving, Kindred across the north feed on the dying and the Masquerade frays in the poorhouses.
Four Spiritual Franciscans who would not give up their poverty are burned at Marseille.
Magnus Eriksson inherits both crowns as a child.
Scottish nobles ask the pope to recognise their independence.
Bands of young shepherds march south and massacre Jews; the authorities crush them.
Wladyslaw is crowned King of Poland at Krakow, reuniting the kingdom.
Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq takes Delhi.
Dante dies in exile at Ravenna, the Comedy complete.
Rumour claims lepers poisoned the wells for the Jews and the king of Granada; lepers are burned across France.
Louis of Bavaria captures his rival Frederick of Austria.
Coastal Flanders rises against taxes and lords for five years.
Grand Duke Gediminas invites merchants and craftsmen to Vilnius, his new capital.
Mansa Musa passes through Cairo with so much gold that its price falls for years.
The first witch trial in Ireland; Alice Kyteler escapes to England and a servant is burned in her place. Verbena in Ireland grow careful.
Ibn Battuta leaves Tangier on pilgrimage and travels for nearly thirty years.
In the year the Convention of the White Tower meets, the Order of Reason takes its name.
Orhan takes Bursa and makes it the Ottoman capital.
John XXII declares that sorcery is heresy, giving inquisitors power over it.
The deposed king dies in prison; Edward III, fourteen, takes the throne.
John of Luxembourg brings the Silesian dukes under the Bohemian crown.
Charles IV dies without a son; Philip VI of Valois takes the crown, and Edward III's claim waits.
Philip VI crushes the Flemish rising.

items.t: Louis of Bavaria crowned in Rome
items.x: Louis IV is crowned emperor by the Roman people and sets up an antipope.
Ivan Kalita becomes Grand Prince with the Horde's blessing, and the metropolitan moves to Moscow.
Orhan beats the Byzantine emperor in Bithynia.
Mages die and the Hermetic covenant of Le Ictus is destroyed in the purge of 1330; the scholars of the city never learn why their colleagues vanished.
The Wallachians under Basarab ambush and destroy a Hungarian army in the Carpathians.
The Ottomans take Nicaea.
An epidemic kills many in Hebei; some historians see the first sign of the Black Death.
Stefan Dusan takes the Serbian throne and builds the greatest Serbian state.
Emperor Go-Daigo rises against the Kamakura shogunate.
Nitta Yoshisada takes Kamakura; the Hojo regents kill themselves and the shogunate ends.
Edward III's archers destroy a Scottish army.
The Arno sweeps away Florence's bridges.
Casimir III becomes King of Poland and builds the country in stone.
Giotto begins the campanile of Florence cathedral.
The governor of Madurai breaks from Delhi.
Abu Said dies without an heir; Mongol Persia falls apart.
The kings of Hungary, Poland and Bohemia meet at Visegrad and agree on trade and borders.
Ashikaga Takauji takes Kyoto; Go-Daigo flees to Yoshino, and the Northern and Southern courts begin.
Harihara and Bukka found the empire of Vijayanagara in southern India.
Philip VI confiscates Gascony; Edward III claims the French crown.
The painter who changed Italian art dies in Florence.
Ashikaga Takauji becomes shogun.
The electors declare that the man they choose is king without the pope's leave.
Graves of Christian merchants near Lake Issyk-Kul record a pestilence; Garou far to the west smell something coming.
Venice expands on the mainland at Verona's cost.
The English destroy the French fleet off Flanders.
Castile and Portugal beat the last great Marinid invasion of Spain.
Poland begins to take Galicia-Volhynia.
A civil war between John Kantakouzenos and the regency of John V begins; both sides hire Turks.
England and France fight over Brittany through rival dukes.
The traveller serves Muhammad bin Tughluq as a judge.
The worst recorded flood in central Europe sweeps the Rhine, Main and Danube.
The great Florentine banks begin to fail after Edward III defaults on his loans.
Estonian peasants rise against German lords and are crushed.
Charles of Luxembourg, already ruling Bohemia for his father, plans to make Prague a capital; the Ventrue of the Empire take interest.
A crusader league takes the harbour of Smyrna from the Turks.
Work begins on the new cathedral of St. Vitus in Prague.
The Bardi bank collapses, taking much of Florence's wealth with it.
The Bahmani nobles break the Deccan away from Delhi; the Bahmani sultanate is founded in 1347.
The leader of Ghent is murdered by a mob.
English longbowmen cut down the French knights; the blind King John of Bohemia dies in the charge.
The English capture David II of Scotland.
The Mongol army besieging Caffa in the Crimea is struck by plague; Genoese ships will carry it west.
Edward III begins an eleven-month siege of Calais.
Charles of Luxembourg is chosen King of the Romans against Louis of Bavaria.
Stefan Dusan is crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks.

appr.x: In September 1212 Frederick II confirms Bohemia as a hereditary kingdom under the Premyslids, with Moravia as its margraviate. The valley answers to a king in Prague, a margrave and, at night, to whoever holds Kranzfels.
Ventrue of the Empire send envoys east to learn who holds the Moravian march. The Tzimisce of the hills receive them coldly and send them home with gifts that are also warnings.
In the spring and summer of 1241 Mongol riders cross Moravia, burning villages and failing before walled places. The valley's families hide their own, and their Kindred, in the hills and the mine.

appr.t: The hill sept fights the riders' spirits
appr.x: The Garou of the Moravian hills meet the spirits riding with the Mongol host. They hold their caern but lose half their number, and their Kinfolk among the old families grow fewer.
The silver town of Jihlava (Iglau) sets down its mining law, which becomes the rule for workings across Moravia and Bohemia. Rothenstein's German council claims the Adit under it.

appr.t: The king falls on the Marchfeld
appr.x: On 26 August 1278 King Premysl Otakar II dies fighting Rudolf of Habsburg. Bad years follow: regents plunder the land and famine reaches the margraviate.

appr.t: Kutna Hora silver and the Prague groschen
appr.x: The great strike at Kutna Hora and the new Prague groschen of 1300 pull miners away from smaller workings. The Adit's silver is worth less and its miners drift away.
On 4 August 1306 the young King Wenceslas III is stabbed in Olomouc and the Premyslid line ends. Kindred of the march whisper that a Cainite hand guided the knife; no one proves it.
John of Luxembourg takes the Bohemian crown. German settlers keep arriving, and the towns and the old Moravian villages grow further apart.

appr.t: A citadel in the Moravian Shadowlands
appr.x: A legion of the Hierarchy raises a citadel in the Shadowlands of Moravia to hold the restless dead of the mines. It will outlast nearly every other in the east.
Dominican inquisitors work the Bohemian crown lands against Waldensian heretics. One passes through the valley, asks the parish many questions, and writes down the answers.
On 30 April 1344 Prague is raised to an archbishopric over the bishops of Olomouc and Litomysl. The parish of St. Aegidius now answers to a church of its own crown.
The last trod near the valley, at the old crossroads, opens on fewer nights each year. The fae who use it feel the cold coming.
Around 1197 the city stands at the edge of ruin, threatening to drag the Dream down with it.
The mechanical clock began with Benedictine monks around 1200 to time prayers; some say it also served Time magick.
The crusaders took Byzantium in 1204 and set up a feudal Latin Empire, also called Romania, with the emperor above vassals such as the King of Thessalonica and the Prince of Achaia.
The Toreador Methuselah Michael, the Patriarch of Constantinople, met Final Death in 1204, but that influence lingers.
Ghouls abandoned when the Trinity families burned or fled in 1204 now hunt Cainites from the Grand Bazaar.
Most Heretics expect the Third Caine to appear in 1206 and dwell on earth for thirty-three years, like Christ.
Bramber Castle in Sussex is said to hold the ghosts of three de Braose children starved by King John and of Lady Maud de Hurst, murdered in 1210.
The Hermetic sanctum at Mistridge fell in 1210, brought down by mortals led by a group calling itself the Craftmasons.
Mages have already used magic to build such weapons, and several cannon were fired in the destruction of the Mistridge Covenant in 1210.
The Craftmasons destroyed Mistridge in the winter of 1210, and the Convention of the White Tower met on 25 March 1325.
Roger Bacon's influence among the High Artisans remains immense; the Craftmasons showed their strength in 1210 when they brought down Mistridge with cannon.
A moderate Ventrue faction, the Antasians, watched over the crowning of Frederick II at Frankfurt in 1212.

After the Children's Crusade of 1212, Giselher, Ventrue prince of Cologne, barred Clan Lasombra from the city. Giselher never proved the Magisters were behind it, but used the charge against rivals anyway.
Before 1215 the vial was widely believed to have reached Cistercian monks near the start of the 12th century, though how it got there is unclear.
Given as a child to a Benedictine priory in the twelfth century, Marc ran away at sixteen and was Embraced in 1216 by Megan of Bristol, a Gangrel of the 10th Generation.

appr.t: Eye for the Weakness of Steel
appr.x: It began among the Fellowship of Our Lady, a company of Toreador and Ventrue, and it passed to their successors after the Fellowship broke apart in 1218 through infighting.
Paris is the seat of the joint Toreador and Ventrue Grand Court. Geoffrey, a Ventrue, has led it as Prince of Paris since 1222, after overthrowing Alexander, Geoffrey's own sire.
A Toreador of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1229 by Maiselle of Rochester, born in the village of Strood.

Cretheus, Fifth Generation Ventrue and childe of Mithras, ruled Rome in fact for nearly 300 years and is the only public member of the Ignoti; bending the knee to Camilla in 1229 was read as the hidden ones' blessing.
It began in AD 1130 and so will end around 1230.
In 1230 common superstition supports belief in magic, which helps mages cast with impunity; only in later ages does belief turn against them.
A few great diseases cause most deaths in 1230; some can empty a village in weeks, others leave victims wasted husks.
In May of 1230 an eclipse darkens the sky so deeply that workers go home thinking night has come.
The Garou of 1230 count Ten Tribes.
They see this era as a time to feed on the spreading chaos and fear and to prepare for the Golden Horde, which turns west in 1235 and pulls back in 1242.
Counting from a creation date of 3761 B.C.E. and five stages of a thousand years each, Heretics expect the material world to end in 1239.
With Kin of their own among the Mongol clans, the Shadow Lords quietly backed the Tatar Yoke over Russia from about 1240 to 1480.
By the 1240s Italy is only a name on the map; loyalty comes from the cities, swollen by migrants from the countryside.

appr.t: Kupala's Eve and the Tzimisce revolt
appr.x: The Mongol invasion of 1241 broke Tzimisce holdings in the east and nearly destroyed the elder known as the Butcher of Rus. Elders tightened their grip on their thralls in response.
A diary of 1242 tells of a coterie sent by an unnamed powerful patron, chasing clues through Dublin, Edinburgh and Norwich toward London.
Most of its men-at-arms die at Gaza in 1244, and its time in the Holy Land is ending during the 13th century.
A Ventrue of the 7th Generation, Embraced in 1263 by Palamon the Copt; a few childhood memories of the mountains are all that remain from before Egypt.
Roger Bacon's London Accord of 1268 ended the war among England's artisan guilds; de Varre founded the Solificati in 1315, and they broke away from the Order of Reason in 1335.

appr.t: The Hospitallers and the Teutonic Knights
appr.x: Large endowments in Western Europe fund the Hospitallers' work in the East, a structure that lets the order outlast the loss of the Holy Land in 1291.
Around 1300 the wandering Caern of Long Voyages was thrown into an attack on a Zmei's servants in southern Russia and lost with its whole sept.
The last reliable account dates to about 1300, back when the tribe still kept its alliance with Helios and the Mound Builder Dreamspeakers.

In 1304, ten years after Kublai Khan died, ancestors from three courts (Yellow Emperor, White Tiger and Black Tortoise) met at the Shaolin monastery near Changan and signed the Treaty of the Quincunx.
King Philip the Fair had the French Templars seized in 1307 on heresy charges, with papal leave, and is widely thought to have wanted their wealth.
In 1307 Philip the Fair had the French Templars arrested for heresy; some say vampire advisors or Batini with grudges pushed the king.

appr.t: The Way of the Ancient Lawgivers
appr.x: Founded in 1312, it holds that all Kindred must return to the ways of the First City, when mortals and lesser vampires honoured the Antediluvians.
Ten years on they wrote that purpose down as the Chodona, the Wheel of the Law with eight spokes; by 1314 the Wheel stretched from Nepal to Ireland.
Pagans gathered there as a refuge from persecution, and in 1317 Sir Garland declared the land a fief named Baerwald, an open insult to Rome and the Empire.
In 1325, as that Order formally began, mathematicians made a sub-lodge, the Arithmeticians, never strong enough to be a Convention.
A Ventrue antitribu of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1327 by Leander Phipps, once a Templar in the Crusades.
The Paris University Purge of 1330 killed many mages and destroyed the Hermetic covenant of Le Ictus.
The War of the Dust Witch near Great Zimbabwe, 1345 to 1350, split the Ngoma and the Madzimbabwe into separate groups; plague in 1420 set them at war, each blaming the other.

items.x: Calais yields to Edward III after eleven months; the burghers offer their lives and are spared.
Genoese galleys bring the plague to Sicily; the Second Great Maelstrom gathers as the dead cross in numbers no one has seen.
The pestilence reaches Constantinople; the emperor's son is among the dead.
lk: The great schism and the Paladins

items.x: The notary Cola di Rienzo takes power in Rome as tribune of the people.
The Deccan nobles found the Bahmani sultanate at Gulbarga.
Charles IV is crowned King of Bohemia with the new crown of St. Wenceslas.
Charles IV founds Prague New Town, one of the largest town plans in Europe.
The plague comes ashore in Provence and moves up the Rhone.
Perhaps half of Florence dies; Boccaccio sets the Decameron among young people fleeing it.
Charles IV founds the first university north of the Alps in Prague.
The plague lands at a Dorset port and reaches London by autumn.
The plague reaches Cairo; at its height thousands die a day.
The people of Damascus fast and pray together, Muslims, Christians and Jews.
Clement VI's physician keeps the pope between two great fires; the pope survives and buys Avignon outright.
The Hierarchy cannot ferry the dead fast enough; whole towns' worth of wraiths wander the Shadowlands unclaimed.
Kindred who feed on the sick sicken their herds and sometimes the Masquerade; some princes forbid feeding in plague houses.
An earthquake shakes the eastern Alps; preachers say it opened the earth for the plague.
Prague becomes the emperor's city; Kindred from the west come to court it.
Charles IV begins Karlstejn castle to keep the crown jewels and relics.
A ship drifts into Bergen with its crew dead of plague; the town soon follows.
Hundreds of Jews are burned in Strasbourg on the charge of poisoning wells, before the plague even arrives.
Processions of flagellants cross Germany; the pope condemns them in October.
The Jewish communities of the Rhineland are destroyed.
A ship brings the plague to Bergen; Norway loses perhaps half its people.
The plague reaches Moravia, lighter than in the west but bad in the towns.
Edward III forbids wages above the old rates; there are too few hands left to obey.
Hermetic healers and Chorus monks die tending the sick; the young Order of Reason studies the plague's spread.
The Jews of Basel are burned on an island in the Rhine.
Banality closes the trods to Arcadia; fae who stay must hide in mortal bodies.
The king of Castile dies of plague at the siege of Gibraltar.
Pilgrims crowd Rome despite the plague.
King Ramathibodi founds Ayutthaya in Siam.
The English beat a Castilian fleet in the Channel.
With half the people dead, landlords in Tuscany cannot find tenants; wages climb.
With villages emptied, wolves come into the fields; Garou Kinfolk families are among the few still farming.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The Red Turban rebellion against the Yuan begins in the Huai valley.
Parliament defines high treason.
The Delhi sultan who moved his capital and made copper coins worth silver dies on campaign.
The Second Great Maelstrom begins to ease; Stygia counts its lost Legions.
The Ottomans take the fortress of Tzympe on the Gallipoli peninsula, their first foothold in Europe.
The Hierarchy gathers the plague dead into new Legions as the storm passes.
Boccaccio finishes the Decameron.
John Kantakouzenos gives up the throne and becomes a monk.
An earthquake shatters Gallipoli's walls; the Ottomans move in and settle the town.
In the plague years Cairo's Kindred shift and shuffle; newcomers find room where the dead left gaps.
The returned tribune is killed by a Roman mob.
Charles IV is crowned in Rome and leaves the same day, as promised.
A tavern brawl at Oxford becomes a two-day battle; dozens of students die.
The doge of Venice is beheaded for plotting to make himself lord of the city.
Stefan Dusan dies on the way to attack Constantinople; his empire breaks up.
Charles IV fixes the seven electors and the rules for choosing a king.
The Black Prince captures King John II of France.
The war between Dalou'laoshi, the Wu Lung and the Akashics begins; it will drive the Brotherhood back into Tibet by 1360.
The strongest recorded earthquake in central Europe wrecks Basel.
Another wave of plague strikes the city.
The provost of Paris merchants forces reforms on the dauphin.
The foundation stone of the stone bridge over the Vltava is laid.
The peasants of northern France rise against the nobles and are crushed within weeks.
The Paris leader is killed as he tries to open the city to Charles of Navarre.
Charles IV plans a new stone bridge across the Vltava; it is begun in 1357.
Venice runs convoys of galleys to Alexandria and Beirut each year for spices.
England gives up its claim to France in return for Aquitaine and Calais.
The Screaming Ghost Purge ends; the Akashics withdraw into Tibet.
Japanese pirates raid Korea and China throughout the 1360s.
The plague returns, killing many children born since 1348.
Murad I takes Adrianople; as Edirne it becomes the Ottoman capital.
Lithuania beats the Golden Horde and takes Kiev.
Zhu Yuanzhang destroys his chief rival's fleet in one of the largest naval battles ever fought.
John II gives Burgundy to his son Philip; the Valois dukes of Burgundy begin.

items.t: The papal court in the plague years
items.x: The Avignon popes' court thrives as plague returns; Lasombra in the Curia grow richer with each death.
Casimir the Great founds a university at Krakow.
The French king dies in London, having returned to captivity.
Rudolf IV founds a university at Vienna.
Peter I of Cyprus sacks Alexandria for a week.
The English lords of Ireland are forbidden to marry, speak or dress as the Irish do.
Astronomy is taught at Prague's new university.
The Black Prince wins for Pedro the Cruel in Castile.
Zhu Yuanzhang founds the Ming and drives the Mongols out of Khanbaliq.
The courts of the Middle Kingdom hold that the Quincunx kept their quarrels from spoiling the change of dynasty.
The Yuan court flees north to the steppe; Garou of Mongolia see the old horde come back broken.

Zhu Yuanzhang drives the Mongols from Beijing and founds the Ming in 1368. The courts of the Middle Kingdom hold that the Quincunx kept their quarrels from spoiling the change. Fits: After the Treaty of the Quincunx, 1304.
items.ref: Real history (1368); the courts' reading is a house rule.

items.x: Pedro of Castile is stabbed by his half-brother Henry, who takes the throne.
Charles V of France restarts the war and slowly takes back Aquitaine.
Timur becomes master of Transoxiana.
The Black Prince storms Limoges; chroniclers tell of thousands killed.
The Hanseatic towns force Denmark to yield; the League is at its height.
The Ottomans destroy the Serbian lords of Macedonia.
