A British army returns to Kabul, blows up its great bazaar and leaves again.
Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol, three spirits and a miser's change of heart.
Charles Napier defeats the emirs of Sindh at Miani and takes the province for the Company.
A young merchant of Shiraz declares the gate to a coming prophet, and the Babi movement spreads across Persia.
Starving handloom weavers in Silesia smash the houses of the merchants, and Prussian troops shoot them down.
Daniel O'Connell is jailed for conspiracy after the monster meetings for repeal of the union with Britain.
Blight rots Ireland's potato crop; over the next five years a million die and another million leave.
The house reading has Fianna caerns in the west cry out as the famine dead crowd the Shadowlands of Ireland.
Two Royal Navy ships seek the Northwest Passage and vanish; searches over decades find bones and tales of cannibalism.
Blight takes the Irish potato from 1845; a million die and a million leave. The Fianna lose Kinfolk to the ships. Fits: Fits the Bone Gnawer Kin card on Irish families.
items.ref: Real history (1845 to 1849); the Fianna are a house reading.

items.x: Peel ends the tariffs on grain and splits his party; cheap bread wins over the landlords.
A Polish noble rising in Galicia is turned when peasants kill hundreds of their lords, and Austria swallows Krakow.
Galle finds the planet Neptune where mathematics said it would be.
The Company fights the Sikh kingdom of the Punjab and takes its eastern lands.
The house reading has Silent Striders carry word west that the Company's wars have broken caerns along the Indus.
The Bronte sisters publish Jane Eyre, Wuthering Heights and Agnes Grey within months.
Semmelweis shows that doctors washing their hands save mothers, and the profession mocks the idea.
The emir of Algeria surrenders to France after fifteen years of war.
Paris overthrows Louis Philippe and declares a republic; revolution spreads across Europe within weeks.
Vienna rises in March, and the old chancellor flees to England in a laundry cart.
The Austrian imperial parliament meets in the archbishop's palace at Kromeriz and drafts a liberal constitution.
Czech students and workers rise in Prague; Windischgratz shells the city and ends the Slav Congress.
Hungary declares its laws its own under Kossuth and fights Vienna for a year.
Marx and Engels publish their manifesto: a spectre is haunting Europe.
The house reading has mediums across London drawing real ghosts to their tables, and the Hierarchy watches every seance.
The house reading puts young Brujah at the Paris barricades, hoping the republic of 1848 can be the one that lasts.
The imperial parliament abolishes the labour dues of the peasants, and Moravian villages are free of the robot.
Revolution breaks out in Paris in February 1848 and spreads to Vienna, Berlin, Milan and Budapest. Most of it is put down within a year. Fits: Round 1 has the Moravian side.
items.ref: Real history (1848).

items.x: Soldiers close the Kromeriz parliament and the young emperor imposes a constitution from above.
With Russian help, Austria crushes Hungary; the Hungarian army lays down its arms at Vilagos and thirteen generals are hanged.
French troops end Mazzini's Roman Republic and restore the pope; Garibaldi escapes.
The second Sikh war ends with the Punjab annexed and the Koh-i-Noor sent to the queen.
Hong Xiuquan, who believes himself Christ's younger brother, raises the Taiping; the war kills twenty million or more.

items.t: The Taiping and the Middle Kingdom
items.x: The house reading has the Kuei-jin courts of the south shaken as the Taiping burn temples and shrines across their lands.
The Bab is executed by firing squad at Tabriz; the first volley leaves the prisoner unhurt, and the faith grows.
Brno is made a statutory city and swallows its suburbs.
The Crystal Palace in Hyde Park shows the world's machines, and six million people come to see.
Louis Napoleon closes the assembly and makes himself master of France; within a year he is emperor.
An American medium holds paid seances in London, and table rapping becomes the fashion of the drawing rooms.
Napoleon III is proclaimed emperor of the French.
Commodore Perry's steamships anchor off Edo and demand that Japan open its ports.
Russia destroys an Ottoman squadron at Sinope with shell guns, and Britain and France move toward war.
The house reading has the Kindred who held the Spilberk prison as a feeding ground leave when it closes as a jail.
Britain and France land in the Crimea to besiege Sevastopol.
A misread order sends British light cavalry into the Russian guns at Balaclava.
Florence Nightingale's nurses reach the barracks hospital, where disease kills far more than Russian shot.
John Snow maps cholera deaths in Soho to a single pump and has its handle taken off.
Christian socialists open a college in London for working men.
After eleven months the Russians leave Sevastopol in flames.
Nicholas I dies; the new tsar Alexander II will free the serfs.
Paris answers London with its own Universal Exposition.
The Crimean War ends; the Black Sea is closed to warships.
Britain and France fight China again over a seized ship, the Second Opium War.
The sultan promises full equality to Christians and Jews, and the Muslim notables resent it.
Sepoys at Meerut mutiny over cartridges and march on Delhi; north India rises against Company rule.
British women and children held at Kanpur are killed; British vengeance across the north is terrible.
The house reading has the Ventrue of Calcutta and the Kuei-jin of the Ganges both feeding on the war while blaming each other.
Flaubert is tried for offending public morals with Madame Bovary and acquitted.
The emperor orders the old walls of Vienna pulled down for a grand boulevard.
The last Mughal emperor is tried and exiled to Rangoon, and the crown takes India from the Company.
A miller's daughter sees a lady in a grotto at Lourdes; the spring becomes a place of pilgrimage.
A hot summer makes the sewage in the Thames unbearable, and Parliament funds Bazalgette's sewers.
Darwin publishes the theory of natural selection and sets science against Genesis.
The house reading has the Union's men of science seize on Darwin as proof that the world runs by law, not spirit.
France and Piedmont beat Austria in a bloody day; a Swiss witness, Henri Dunant, will found the Red Cross.
A great solar storm sets telegraph lines sparking and lights auroras as far south as the Caribbean.
Ferdinand de Lesseps breaks ground on a canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
Garibaldi lands in Sicily with a thousand volunteers and conquers the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
Druze and Christian fighting in Mount Lebanon spreads to Damascus, where thousands of Christians die.
British and French troops loot and burn the Qing emperor's Summer Palace.
The house reading has the Inquisition's Society of Leopold shrunk to a few priests in Rome, keeping files no bishop reads.
Victor Emmanuel becomes king of Italy.
Alexander II frees twenty-three million serfs, though they must buy their land in debt.
The prince consort dies of typhoid, and the queen wears black for the rest of her life.
Bismarck becomes minister-president of Prussia and promises iron and blood.
Victor Hugo publishes Les Miserables from exile.
Tyrs and Fugner found the Sokol gymnastic movement, and halls rise in every Czech and Moravian town.
Poland rises against Russia again and fights for over a year in the forests.
The first underground railway opens between Paddington and Farringdon.
The house reading has London's Nosferatu furious as the Underground cuts through warrens they have held since the Romans.
A British squadron shells Kagoshima after a Satsuma samurai kills an English merchant.
Prussia and Austria take Schleswig and Holstein from Denmark.
Twelve states agree to protect the wounded and those who care for them.
Workers' leaders found the International Workingmen's Association in London.
Qing armies take the Taiping capital and kill over a hundred thousand; Hong Xiuquan is already dead.
Russia ends its war in the Caucasus by driving hundreds of thousands of Circassians to Ottoman lands; many die on the shore.
Gregor Mendel reads the laws of heredity to the Brno natural history society; no one understands them for thirty-five years.
The house reading has a Technocrat visitor to the Brno monastery mark Mendel's work as a future paradigm and leave it unknown.
Russian troops take Tashkent and the conquest of Central Asia begins.
Prussia crushes Austria in Bohemia in a single day, and the German question is settled.
Prussian troops occupy Brno after the Bohemian defeat; cholera follows the armies.
Austria and Prussia sign the preliminary peace at Mikulov castle; Austria is shut out of Germany.
The Austrian fleet rams and sinks Italian ironclads off Lissa in the Adriatic.
Crete rises against the Ottomans; the monks of Arkadi blow up their monastery rather than surrender.
The compromise makes the Habsburg lands a dual monarchy; Hungary rules itself and the Czechs get nothing.
The first volume of Marx's Capital is published.
The last Tokugawa shogun returns power to the emperor.
Paris holds another world fair, with Japanese prints that change European art.
The house reading has Irish Kithain hoping the Fenians win; a few eshu carry their letters across the sea.
The emperor's government defeats the shogun's last loyalists and moves to Edo, renamed Tokyo.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin of Japan split over the Meiji reforms; some court the new ministries, others retreat to the mountains.
Foundation stones from Czech mountains, Radhost among them, are laid for the National Theatre in Prague.
The last shogunate loyalists hold out at Hakodate under their Republic of Ezo and surrender the next spring.

In the Meiji Restoration of 1868 the emperor moves to Edo, now Tokyo. Hakari, oldest of the undead in Japan, keeps court in the Imperial Palace from then on. Fits: Fits House Genji's rise with Japan in the late 1800s.
items.ref: Real history (1868); Hakari from Encyclopaedia Vampirica p. 89; the timing is a house reading.

items.x: The canal opens to shipping and the route to India is shortened by weeks.
The bishops meet in Rome and declare the pope infallible on faith and morals.
Mendeleev arranges the elements in a table that predicts ones not yet found.
The emir of Bukhara accepts Russian protection after defeat.
The French emperor surrenders at Sedan with his army, and the Second Empire falls.
The Prussians ring Paris; the city eats its horses, its rats and the zoo animals.

items.t: The Toreador starve with the city
items.x: The house reading has the Toreador of Paris feeding thin as the siege drags on and blood grows as scarce as bread.
Italian troops break into Rome through the Porta Pia, and the Papal States end.
The king of Prussia is proclaimed German emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.
Paris rules itself for ten weeks; in the bloody week of May the army kills thousands of Communards.
The house reading has the Camarilla let the Commune burn to purge Brujah radicals, then blame the Sabbat for the fires.
Italy makes Rome its capital, and the pope shuts himself in the Vatican as a prisoner.
Bismarck fights the Catholic Church over schools and priests.
Sheridan Le Fanu publishes Carmilla, a vampire tale of a countess and a lonely girl in Styria.
The exiled Algerian emir, who saved thousands of Christians in 1860, lives on as a scholar in Damascus.
The Vienna stock exchange collapses days after the World's Fair opens, and a long depression follows.
Cholera kills thousands in Vienna during the exhibition, and visitors stay away.
Russia takes the khanate of Khiva and frees its slaves.
Painters refused by the Salon show their work together, and a critic mocks it as impressions.
Blavatsky and Olcott found the Theosophical Society, and Eastern wisdom becomes a fashion in Europe.
The house reading has the Cult of Ecstasy and the Chakravanti watching the Theosophists closely, for some of what they teach is true.
Christian peasants rise against Ottoman tax collectors, and the Great Eastern Crisis begins.
Ottoman irregulars crush a Bulgarian rising and kill thousands at Batak; Gladstone writes of Bulgarian horrors.
The Ottomans proclaim a constitution and a parliament, which the sultan suspends within two years.
Wagner's whole Ring cycle opens in a theatre built to stage it.
Leos Janacek becomes a teacher and choirmaster in Brno; the town's music will carry Moravian folk song to the world.
The Ottomans hold Plevna against the Russians for five months before hunger breaks them.
Victoria is proclaimed Empress of India at a great durbar while famine kills millions in the south.
Saigo Takamori leads the last samurai rising against the new Japan and dies at Shiroyama.
Drought and grain exports kill five million or more in south and west India.
The house reading has the Stygian Hierarchy struggle to collect the souls from Plevna, and Renegades take many.
The powers redraw the Balkans: Serbia, Montenegro and Romania are free and Austria takes Bosnia to govern.
Austro-Hungarian troops occupy Bosnia and Herzegovina against fierce resistance.
Drought across north China kills nine million or more.
The house reading has Tzimisce of the Balkans see the Austrian occupation as a chance to push Camarilla influence south.
Swan and Edison light carbon filament lamps; the night changes.
The house reading has the night shrinking for the Kindred as electric light spreads, and the Weaver grows stronger in every lit street.
The British envoy at Kabul is murdered, and British troops occupy the city again.
An Afghan army wins at Maiwand, and Roberts marches three hundred miles to relieve Kandahar.
Brno opens horse trams, among the first in the Czech lands.
Revolutionaries of the People's Will kill the tsar with bombs on the Catherine Canal.
After the tsar's murder, mobs attack Jewish towns across the south of the empire, and emigration to America begins.
The new National Theatre in Prague burns before its formal opening; the nation pays to rebuild it in two years.
France occupies Tunisia.
The Royal Navy shells Alexandria, and a British army defeats Urabi at Tel el-Kebir.
The house reading has Egypt's mummies watching as British collectors empty tombs, and some go to London after their own bodies.
Prague's university is split into Czech and German halves.
Scholars found a society to test mediums, ghosts and thought transference.
The volcano blows apart, the sound is heard across the Indian Ocean, and sunsets turn red worldwide.
Some four hundred people die when the Ringtheater burns in Vienna during an opera.
France fights China and the Black Flags for northern Vietnam.
The European powers meet to share out Africa among themselves.
An international conference fixes the prime meridian at Greenwich and the world's time zones follow.
Britain takes Mandalay in weeks and annexes Upper Burma.
Pasteur saves a boy bitten by a rabid dog with a new vaccine.
The house reading places the founding of the Arcanum in London, scholars sworn to study the hidden world without becoming part of it.
Serbia attacks Bulgaria and is beaten at Slivnitsa within two weeks.
The Mahdi's army storms Khartoum after a ten-month siege, and Gordon is killed two days before relief.
Stevenson publishes The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.
Ludwig II of Bavaria is declared insane and found dead in Lake Starnberg with the doctor who certified him.
Masaryk and others show that the medieval Czech manuscripts of Dvur Kralove and Zelena Hora are forgeries.
Victoria marks fifty years on the throne, and kings come to London.
The Yellow River breaks its dykes and floods the plain; perhaps a million die.
The house reading has a mummy unwrapped before a London audience wake that night; the house rule notes the Reborn remember such things.
Three Freemasons found the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn in London.

items.t: The Golden Dawn and the Order
items.x: The house reading has the Order of Hermes recruit from the Golden Dawn, and a few of its members Awaken.
An unknown killer murders at least five women in Whitechapel, and the press calls the killer Jack the Ripper.
The house reading has London's Kindred fear a Masquerade breach in Whitechapel; the prince sends hounds after the killer.
Wilhelm I dies, Frederick III reigns ninety-nine days, and Wilhelm II takes the German throne.
The house reading has an Arcanum scholar keep notes on the Ripper that point away from the Kindred and toward a mortal doctor.
Crown Prince Rudolf of Austria and Mary Vetsera are found dead at the hunting lodge of Mayerling.
The tower is finished for the World's Fair, the tallest structure on earth.
Japan becomes a constitutional monarchy with a parliament on the Prussian model.
An influenza pandemic spreads by rail from Russia and kills about a million.
The young emperor drops the old chancellor.
Oscar Wilde publishes the tale of a portrait that ages while its sitter does not.
Japan's schools are bound to loyalty to the emperor.
Prague holds a great exhibition and builds the Petrin lookout tower and a funicular.
Work begins on a railway across Siberia to the Pacific.
A great earthquake in central Japan kills seven thousand.
Persians stop smoking when the shah sells the tobacco trade to a British company; the shah backs down.
Unfiltered water spreads cholera through Hamburg and kills eight thousand, while Altona next door is spared.
The house reading has a Brno doctor's notes on a patient with no pulse who walks at night; the Arcanum buys them.
The Indian Councils Act lets Indians sit on the legislative councils.
A canal cut through rock opens across the isthmus of Corinth.
Young Czech radicals are tried and jailed, and Prague is placed under emergency law.
Dvorak writes his symphony From the New World far from home.
A Jewish army captain is falsely convicted of spying and sent to Devil's Island; France splits for twelve years.
Japan defeats China in Korea and at sea, and takes Taiwan.
The sultan's irregulars kill Armenians in eastern Anatolia; over two years perhaps two hundred thousand die.
Bubonic plague reaches Hong Kong; Yersin finds its bacillus, and the disease spreads by ship to every continent.
The house reading has the fae of Brittany and Ireland feed on the poets of the Celtic revival, and the Dreaming grows brighter there.
The Lumiere brothers show moving pictures to a paying audience in a Paris cafe.
Rontgen finds rays that pass through flesh and show the bones.
Oscar Wilde is sentenced to two years' hard labour for gross indecency.
Prague shows peasant life from every Czech land, Moravian Wallachia and Slovacko among them.
Japanese agents murder Queen Min in the palace at Seoul and burn the body.
The Olympic Games return in Athens.
Becquerel finds that uranium salts fog photographic plates in the dark.
A tsunami strikes the coast of northern Japan and kills over twenty thousand.
Plague reaches Bombay and kills millions across India over the next two decades.

items.t: The Akashic Brotherhood shut the doors
items.x: The house reading has the Akashics close Tibetan monasteries to Western seekers after Theosophists come asking.
Victoria celebrates sixty years with troops from every corner of the empire.
Bram Stoker publishes Dracula: a Transylvanian count, his voyage to Whitby and the hunters who stop him.
The house reading has the Tzimisce furious at the book, the Tremere amused, and every hunter in England reading it twice.
The house reading follows Mage canon: the Order of Reason takes the name Technocratic Union at its 1897 convocation.
Herzl gathers the first Zionist Congress in Basel.
Vienna orders officials in Bohemia and Moravia to know Czech; German riots force the minister out.
One of the strongest earthquakes recorded strikes Assam and Shillong.
Greece fights the Ottomans over Crete and loses in a month.
An anarchist stabs the empress of Austria with a file by the lake at Geneva.
The Guangxu emperor orders sweeping reforms; the empress dowager stops them and holds the emperor prisoner.
Kitchener's machine guns destroy the Mahdist army outside Omdurman.
Wilhelm II rides into Jerusalem through a gap cut in the wall.
Alfons Mucha of Ivancice, in Moravia, is the rage of Paris for his posters of Sarah Bernhardt.
A Jewish vagrant is convicted of ritual murder at Polna; Masaryk defends Hilsner and is called a traitor.
The Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists attacks missionaries and Chinese Christians in Shandong.
The powers agree rules of war and found a court of arbitration.
Freud publishes the book that founds psychoanalysis.
The house reading has the Dreamspeakers and the fae both uneasy as Freud teaches the waking world to pick dreams apart.
The house reading has the Toreador of Vienna patron the Secession painters while the Ventrue fund their critics.

Don Cerro brings the childe Theo Bell to Victorian London to learn to read Kindred society. In London Bell meets Angus Abranson, a friendship that lasts a century. Fits: The book has them meet about a hundred years before the late 1990s.
items.ref: Clan Novel Trilogy: Brujah 1, Slave Ring p. 35, and Brujah 2, The Overseer; the year is a house reading.

items.x: The Boxers and Qing troops besiege the foreign legations in Beijing for fifty-five days until an eight-nation army arrives.
The relief armies loot Beijing and punish the north China countryside; the court flees to Xi'an.
The house reading has some Kuei-jin courts feed the Boxer fury against foreign Kindred, and pay when the foreign armies arrive.
Paris holds the century's greatest fair, with moving walkways and the first Metro line.
Three botanists find Mendel's forgotten paper from Brno within months of each other.
Trade unions and socialists form a committee to send workers to Parliament.
Max Planck proposes that energy comes in small packets, and physics begins to change.
The Golden Dawn tears itself apart over Mathers and Crowley, and rival temples form.
The house reading has a Technocrat in Brno quietly delighted as Mendel's laws return; the Progenitors claim them.
The queen dies at Osborne after sixty-three years, and Edward VII takes the throne.
Marconi receives a radio signal sent from Cornwall across the Atlantic.
Persia grants a British prospector the right to drill for oil across most of the country.
The Czech technical university opens in Brno.
Britain ends its splendid isolation in an alliance with Japan.
The bell tower of St Mark's in Venice collapses into a heap of rubble.
King Chulalongkorn's reforms keep Siam independent between British and French empires.
Emmeline Pankhurst founds the Women's Social and Political Union: deeds, not words.
Officers murder King Alexander and Queen Draga of Serbia and throw their bodies from a window.
A mob kills forty-nine Jews over two days in Bessarabia while police watch.
Macedonian revolutionaries rise against the Ottomans and are crushed with village burnings.
Russian socialists split at their London congress, and Lenin's faction calls itself the majority.
The house reading follows canon: the Electrodyne Engineers' break with the Technocracy hardens, and they will join the Traditions.
Japan attacks the Russian fleet at Port Arthur without warning and lays siege to the port.
Britain and France settle their colonial quarrels and draw together against Germany.
Work presses on the railway from Damascus to Medina, built for the hajj.
Troops fire on workers marching to petition the tsar, and revolution spreads across Russia.
Japan destroys the Russian Baltic fleet after its voyage around the world.
Over half a million men fight for three weeks outside Mukden, the largest battle the world has yet seen.
Sailors on the battleship Potemkin mutiny over rotten meat and sail to Odessa.
The tsar promises a parliament and civil rights to end the general strike.
A patent clerk named Einstein publishes on light, atoms and special relativity in one year.
Germans and Czechs clash over a Czech university in Brno; a joiner, Frantisek Pavlik, is killed by troops on the steps of the House of Artists.
Merchants and clerics take sanctuary and force the shah to grant a parliament.
An earthquake in the Himalayan foothills kills twenty thousand.
Britain launches an all big-gun battleship that makes every other warship obsolete.
A coal dust explosion in northern France kills over a thousand miners.
Vesuvius erupts, kills over a hundred, and sends Rome's Olympics to London.
The first Majlis meets in Tehran.
Lord Curzon divides Bengal, and the boycott of British goods begins.
Austria gives every man the vote for the Reichsrat, and Czech and socialist members flood in.
Britain and Russia divide Persia into spheres and settle Afghanistan and Tibet.
Picasso paints the canvas that opens the way to cubism.
Bolsheviks led by Kamo and organised by a young Stalin rob a bank convoy with bombs.
Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina outright, and Serbia and Russia are humiliated.
Ottoman officers in Macedonia force the sultan to bring back the constitution.
Something explodes over the Siberian forest and flattens eighty million trees.
The house reading has the blast felt across the Umbra; Garou of Siberia and Mages argue over whether it was a falling star or a failed working.
An earthquake and tsunami destroy Messina and Reggio and kill some eighty thousand.
Riots between Czechs and Germans bring martial law to Prague during the emperor's jubilee.
D'Arcy's drillers strike oil at Masjed Soleyman, and the Anglo-Persian Oil Company follows.
Something bursts over the Siberian forest at Tunguska on 30 June 1908 and flattens it for miles. Every faction of mages has a theory. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1908); the theories are a house reading.

items.x: Louis Bleriot flies across the English Channel.
A counter-coup fails and the Young Turks depose Sultan Abdulhamid II.
Mobs and soldiers kill some twenty thousand Armenians in Adana.
The house reading has the Shadowlands of Messina flooded with the earthquake dead, and Spectres gather.
Edward VII dies and George V becomes king; nine kings ride in the funeral.
Japan annexes Korea.
A revolution ends the monarchy in Portugal.
Pneumonic plague kills sixty thousand in Manchuria until a Malayan doctor's masks and quarantines stop it.
The earth passes through the comet's tail, and people buy comet pills against poison gas.
The house reading has an Olomouc priest send the archbishop a report of a parish where the dead do not stay buried.
Army units rise at Wuchang, the provinces follow, and the Qing dynasty falls within months.
George V and Queen Mary are crowned emperor and empress of India in Delhi, and the capital moves from Calcutta.
Italy attacks the Ottoman provinces of Libya; aircraft drop bombs in war for the first time.
The Mona Lisa vanishes from the Louvre; it turns up two years later in Florence.
A German gunboat at Agadir nearly brings war with France over Morocco.
Great fires burn thousands of wooden houses in Istanbul.
Revolution breaks out at Wuchang in October 1911; the last emperor gives up the throne in February 1912. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1911, 1912).

items.x: The liner strikes an iceberg on its first voyage; over fifteen hundred die.
Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece and Montenegro drive the Ottomans almost out of Europe.
The Meiji emperor dies and General Nogi and his wife follow in ritual suicide.
The six-year-old Puyi gives up the throne, and China becomes a republic.
The Stockholm Games bring electric timing and a photo finish.
Brno's Czech and German artists hold rival shows, and the town's cafes argue about modern art.
Ismail Qemali proclaims an independent Albania at Vlore.
Bulgaria attacks its allies over Macedonia and loses.
Colonel Redl, chief of Austrian counter-intelligence, is found to be a Russian spy and shoots himself.
Stravinsky's ballet starts a riot in the theatre.
A suffragette runs onto the course at the Derby and is killed by the king's horse.
A failed painter and a Georgian revolutionary live in Vienna the same winter; Trotsky and Tito pass through too.
The house reading has the Tremere of Vienna advising the court; their chantry is among the oldest in the empire, and they sense the war coming.
Germany launches the largest ship in the world.
Employers lock out twenty thousand workers in Dublin for over seven months.

items.t: The raid on the Sublime Porte
items.x: Enver Pasha storms the government offices, the war minister is shot, and the Committee of Union and Progress takes power.
The ironworks at Vitkovice by Ostrava become one of the great steel and coal works of the empire.
The house reading has Glass Walkers watching a German chemical firm whose board answers to something in the Wyrm's service.

appr.x: The Emperor Ferdinand Northern Railway opens from Vienna to Brno in July 1839. News, goods and travellers now come in days, not weeks.
In 1848 the labour dues are abolished (September) and an imperial parliament meets at Kromeriz in Moravia until it is closed in March 1849.
Gregor Mendel reads his work on heredity in pea plants to the Brno society in 1865. Almost no one notices; a few Progenitors do.
Prussia beats Austria in the war of 1866 and occupies Brno; cholera follows the armies.
Coal and iron at Ostrava grow into a black country. The hill sept smells the Wyrm in the pits and the Weaver in the furnaces.
The valley's mine is worked out and closed. The miners' families leave for Ostrava and Brno, and the Adit becomes a place children are told to keep away from.
Spiritualist circles meet in Brno and Olomouc. Some reach the restless dead of the Moravian citadel, which does not like it.

In the years before the Rebellions of 1837 and 1838, Strathcona watched the city's cliquish ancillae, likened to an old boys' club, spend their nights on their wealth at the Beaver Club and the Exchange Coffee House, and judged it time for the Sabbat to act.
Victoria has ruled the Empire's living subjects since 1837, so few alive remember any other reign.
In an 1838 letter to Prince Mithras of London, Archbishop Strathcona claimed that Montreal had always belonged to the Sabbat and warned the Camarilla off, calling it the City of Black Miracles.
Strathcona wrote to Prince Mithras of London in April 1838, declaring that once-friends were now dead to each other and that Montreal would be defended against the Camarilla.

appr.t: San Francisco in the Gold Rush
appr.x: In 1849 San Francisco grew from 900 people to 26,000, with another 100,000 passing through on the way to the hills.
As the Order of Reason began turning into the Technocratic Union in the mid-1800s, several were caught in the fighting, and the survivors passed on a warning to stay out of wizards' affairs.
In 1851 the tangle of guild laws was folded into one body named the Financiers.
A Virginian Confederate officer from 1861, friend to Stonewall Jackson, shot and left for dead at the Battle of Fisher's Hill.
A Tremere of the 9th Generation, perhaps antitribu, Embraced in 1864; sire Lady Lise Paulmann is destroyed.
An Assamite of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1867 by Ma'aruf, and of the same lineage as the notorious Fatima.

Shadow Lords have been barred from the island since their treachery in 1868, and Get of Fenris of both sexes since 1967, when Get women seeking sanctuary opened a moon bridge for their kin to seize it.

From 25 December 1870 Don Sebastian governed Los Angeles as prince, a stern but fair ruler to the refugees who came south from San Francisco, caring nothing for their pasts so long as they kept the rules of the domain.
Through paid dispatchers, customs men and dock and ground crews, the Giovanni have watched what moves up the Hudson since the 1870s and through Idlewild, now Kennedy, airport since 1962.
Tammany Hall, run by Boss Tweed, keeps great power through illegal favours and vote-gathering, despite a setback in the 1870s.
A suicidal Malkavian lit the flames that swept the city in 1871. Few mortals died, but some 18,000 buildings burned and Maxwell's supporters were nearly all destroyed.

Prince Iain MacLaren, a ninth-generation Ventrue banker Embraced in London in 1874, took the city after leaving Britain in 1979; a paid arrangement with Lucian of Gary to move Kindred down the river into the States funds the post.
It began in 1877 amid Sabbat raids on Midwestern telegraph stations, when a templar saw that fast communication could offset the Camarilla's social reach.
The end of Reconstruction in 1877 eased the city's burdens but left behind a group of Kindred from the North who had tasted power there and want more.
Lodin ruled through money and force, using police and private guards to keep the workers in line, until strikes and Modius's rebellion shook that rule in the 1880s.
For the game the age runs almost two decades, from 1880 to 1897.

appr.t: The Kindred and the Occult Revival
appr.x: Mortals start the Golden Dawn in 1880, but Kindred soon infest it and use it to draw living initiates.
Holmscroft wrote the society's rituals, first held at Christmas 1885; a founder suspected they were far older than the Arcanum.
The Minneapolis conclave of 1887 tried Prince Cyril Ximenes for tyranny over the Masquerade.
A Giovanni of the Tenth Generation, Embraced in 1887 by Rosario Giovanni.

appr.t: The Fall of the Storm Eater
appr.x: The Storm Eater, a blend of Weaver and Wyrm, was destroyed in 1889 by a rite the Pure Ones and Wyrmcomers found together; the Wendigo say its exact form is now lost.
Founded in 1890 and named after a Tennyson poem, it holds that the Antediluvians sleep for lack of magic and will wake when a second Flood of magic comes.
Salvador Garcia is a Brujah, sired by Ferdinand and Embraced in 1892, who looks about 23.
In 1895 the Artificers moved their best difference engine to Autochthonia, where power was plentiful and no Sleeper could see it.

appr.t: The Order of Reason becomes the Technocratic Union
appr.x: The Order of Reason reorganizes as the Technocracy.
The common account says the engine reached full sentience in 1897 on the tenth iteration of a new algorithm, and the Machinists renamed their Convention Iteration X.
In 1897 Vlad Dracula arrives in London and whispers a story to an Irish author that strains the Masquerade to its limits.
A militant offshoot founded in 1898, the Master Edenic Groundskeepers, wants to strike first; it has drifted from the main body since the 1960s and may soon break away.
The Bunyip are hunted out as Europeans settle Australia. No living Bunyip remains.
A warrior and linguist who came to California around 1900 and served the Prince of San Francisco against the Sabbat and lawless Anarchs.
Even the Luciferian Movement, Satanism included, became widespread by the 1900s.
The Sons of Ether left the Technocracy in 1905 and took the empty Seat once held by the Solificati in 1906; in 1932 the Ahl-i-Batin quit the Council over Middle Eastern Quintessence.
The city was formally founded in 1905, and federal interest in the area began with surveys ahead of the Hoover Dam.
A 1905 symposium across Europe set down the Scientific Ethos, with the League charged to ease Etherite work into the Consensus.
The 1906 earthquake woke the torpid Nosferatu elder Fa Chen Leong amid the fires, who attacked believing assassins had come.

In 1907 Mercer played while the Ecstatic dancer Isadora Duncan performed in Paris; witnesses saw the hall flicker into a Greek temple and the light of Olympus, and some of the crowd went mad or rioted.
In 1908 Lodin warned the city's oldest Kindred that anarch actions threatened the Masquerade, and the elders allowed Lodin to end the conflict by any means.
The name was first pinned on Mathieu Hullebusch in 1909 for a flying-automaton bid to overthrow the colonial rulers of the Belgian Congo.
Former Electrodyne Engineers formed it in 1910, aiming to share research so the Masses could build their prototypes and so steal assembly-line power from the Union.
By 1913 Lodin held the city and Modius fled.

items.x: A Bosnian Serb student shoots Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo after their driver takes a wrong turn.
The archduke's estate at Konopiste in Bohemia, with its rose garden and hunting trophies, is left without a master.
Austria-Hungary sends Serbia demands written to be refused, and declares war when they are not all met.
Austrian monitors on the Danube shell Belgrade the night after war is declared.
Germany declares war on Russia and then France, and the great powers mobilise millions by rail.
Belgium's forts at Liege hold the German advance for days until giant siege howitzers crush them.
Britain declares war when Germany invades Belgium, over a treaty the German chancellor calls a scrap of paper.
The regiments of Brno, Olomouc, Kromeriz and Jihlava entrain for Galicia and Serbia amid flags and quiet dread.
German troops burn the university library of Leuven and shoot civilians; the rape of Belgium becomes a byword.
Hindenburg and Ludendorff encircle a Russian army in East Prussia; its general shoots himself.
French infantry in red trousers attack into Lorraine and the Ardennes and lose over a quarter of a million men in weeks.
The British Expeditionary Force meets the Germans at Mons and falls back; tales of the Angels of Mons follow.
The house reading lets soldiers' tale of the Angels of Mons be a real working, though no Tradition will say whose.
Serbia beats the first Austrian invasion on Cer Mountain, the first Allied victory of the war.
Japan declares war on Germany and turns on its Pacific islands and its port of Tsingtao.
Russia routs the Austro-Hungarian armies in Galicia and takes Lemberg; Austria loses four hundred thousand men in a month.
British battlecruisers sink three German cruisers in the first sea fight of the war, near Heligoland.
The French and British stop the Germans on the Marne, some reserves rushed out from Paris in taxis.
Both sides dig in on the Aisne, and the race to the sea begins.
The Russians besiege the great Austrian fortress of Przemysl in Galicia.
Germany drives a second Russian army out of East Prussia.
One German submarine sinks three British cruisers in an hour.
The Belgian army slips out of Antwerp, and the city surrenders.
German volunteer regiments of students attack at Ypres and are shot down in thousands.
Ottoman warships, two of them German, shell Russian Black Sea ports, and the empire enters the war.
Belgium opens the sluices at Nieuwpoort and floods the Yser plain to stop the Germans.
The German raider Emden slips into Penang harbour and sinks a Russian cruiser before being hunted down.
Japanese and British troops take Germany's Chinese port after a siege.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin of Shandong drive out the German Kindred who came with the colony.
The Ottoman sheikh ul-Islam calls Muslims everywhere to holy war against the Allies.
An Indian army lands at the head of the Gulf to guard the oil and takes Basra.
Austria takes Belgrade.
Indian troops land at Fao on the Shatt al-Arab to protect the Abadan refinery.
Serbia counterattacks at the Kolubara and drives the Austrians out of the country.
Enver Pasha marches an Ottoman army through the Caucasus snows; most of the army freezes or dies.
Soldiers along parts of the Western Front stop fighting for Christmas, sing carols and meet in no man's land.
The house reading has the Christmas truce blaze with Glamour, and changelings in uniform remember it all their lives.
German battlecruisers shell Scarborough, Hartlepool and Whitby.
Austria wins its last unaided victory against Russia south of Krakow.
Professor Masaryk leaves Austria for exile to work for Czech independence.
Britain makes Hussein Kamel sultan of Egypt in place of the deposed khedive.
Hospital trains fill Olomouc and Brno; schools become wards and cholera comes from the Galician front.
The house reading has Brno's Kindred lose half their ghouls to the call-up and quarrel over who may take the wounded.
The house reading follows canon: the war dead swamp the Shadowlands of Flanders, and the Hierarchy cannot reap them fast enough.
Typhus spreads from prisoner camps across Serbia and kills hundreds of thousands, doctors among them.
The house reading has the Garou of the Ardennes torn between fighting the Wyrm in the trenches and guarding caerns being shelled to splinters.
India sends over a million men to fight; Indian corps hold the line at Ypres in their first winter.
The house reading has the Iteration X and the New World Order working both sides, testing new guns on whichever army will take them.
Censorship closes Czech papers, and suspected Russophiles are arrested.
German professors sign a manifesto defending the army in Belgium.

items.t: The Defence of the Realm Act
items.x: Britain gives its government wide powers over press, pubs and land.
Britain declares a protectorate over Egypt and deposes the khedive.
The house reading has Egypt's Reborn see the war as the outsiders' quarrel, while Set's followers grow bold in Cairo.
War closes the pilgrim roads, and few pilgrims reach Mecca.
Russian troops in Galicia attack Jewish towns; hundreds of thousands flee to Vienna and Budapest.
Austria interns thousands of suspect Ruthenians in a camp near Graz, where many die.
The Afghan emir keeps out of the war despite Ottoman and German pleading.
Austria attacks through the Carpathian passes in winter to relieve Przemysl and loses six hundred thousand men to battle and frost.
An Ottoman force crosses Sinai and tries to cross the canal; it is beaten off.
British and German battlecruisers fight off the Dogger Bank; the Blucher sinks.
Germany fires gas shells at the Russians at Bolimow; the cold stops the gas from working.
Ottoman and Russian forces fight over Tabriz in neutral Persia.
Germany declares the waters round Britain a war zone where any ship may be sunk.
British and French battleships begin shelling the forts at the mouth of the Dardanelles.
Mines sink three Allied battleships in the narrows in an afternoon, and the fleet withdraws.
The starving garrison of Przemysl blows up its forts and surrenders: over a hundred thousand prisoners.
The British break into the German line at Neuve Chapelle and cannot go further.
Czech politicians at home form a secret network, called the Maffie, to send news to Masaryk abroad.
Germany releases chlorine gas from cylinders at Ypres; French colonial troops break and the Canadians hold.
British, Australian, New Zealand and French troops land on Gallipoli; Mustafa Kemal holds the heights.
Armenian leaders in Istanbul are arrested and killed, and the deportations of the Armenian people begin; about a million die.
The house reading has the Armenian dead rise in the Shadowlands in such numbers that the Dark Kingdom of Jade sends envoys to see.
The Armenians of Van hold their quarter against Ottoman troops for a month until the Russians come.
The Prague 28th infantry regiment goes over to the Russians nearly whole in the Carpathians, and the army disbands it in disgrace.
German and Austrian armies break the Russian front at Gorlice, and the great retreat begins.
A German submarine sinks the liner Lusitania off Ireland; nearly twelve hundred die.
Italy joins the Allies on promises of Austrian land.
Second Ypres ends with the salient smaller and poisoned.
Italy attacks across the Isonzo river, the first of twelve battles there.
Austria takes back Lemberg.
The Czech politician Karel Kramar is arrested for treason and later sentenced to death; the sentence is commuted.
Masaryk in Geneva declares war on Austria on the five hundredth anniversary of Jan Hus's burning.
Italy attacks again on the Carso and loses forty thousand men.
The Germans take Warsaw as the Russians retreat, burning crops and driving civilians east.
A new British landing at Suvla Bay stalls on the beach.
Millions of refugees flee eastward ahead of the Russian armies through the summer.
Britain uses gas for the first time at Loos; the wind blows some of it back.
France attacks in Champagne with huge losses for a few miles.
Austria's autumn attack in Volhynia fails and costs it a quarter of a million men.
Germany, Austria and Bulgaria invade Serbia from three sides.
The Germans shoot the British nurse Edith Cavell for helping Allied soldiers escape.
British and French troops land at Salonika in neutral Greece too late to save Serbia.
The British march on Baghdad is stopped at Ctesiphon, and the army falls back on Kut.
Serbian civilians and soldiers stream across the Kosovo plain toward the mountains.
The Serbian army and King Peter retreat through the Albanian mountains in winter; tens of thousands die.
The Ottomans surround the British at Kut.
The Allies slip away from Gallipoli at night without losing a man, after eight months and half a million casualties.
The house reading has the Assamites of Anatolia refuse the sultan's holy war, while Ventrue in Istanbul profit from the deportations.
The house reading has a Reborn in Cairo dream of Troy's old dead stirring under the guns at Gallipoli.
The house reading has the Arcanum in London lend scholars to naval intelligence and lose track of half its own members.
Japan demands control over much of China, and Chinese students boycott Japanese goods.
Indian troops in Singapore mutiny and kill Europeans before they are put down.
Sharif Hussein of Mecca and the British high commissioner in Cairo begin letters on an Arab rising.
An Allied blockade, locusts and Ottoman requisitions starve Mount Lebanon; perhaps half the people die.
The house reading has the Shadow Lords of the Carpathians wage their own war, using the armies to drive rival septs from caerns.
Bread is rationed in Vienna, and queues begin outside every bakery.
Jamal Pasha hangs Arab nationalists in Beirut and Damascus.
German airships bomb London and English towns by night.
The house reading has London's Kindred find the blackout a gift for hunting, and the prince orders discretion.

items.t: The Good Soldier Svejk is born
items.x: In Prague cells and barracks Jaroslav Hasek gathers the material for the soldier who survives by seeming a fool.
A German and Ottoman mission reaches Kabul to raise Afghanistan against India and fails.
A German agent called Wassmuss raises the southern Persian tribes against Britain.
Bulgaria joins the Central Powers.
A blizzard and floods kill soldiers in the trenches at Suvla.
Austria takes Mount Lovcen and Montenegro surrenders.
Yudenich's Russians storm the fortress of Erzurum in the winter snows.
The survivors of the Serbian army are shipped to Corfu, where thousands die of disease on Vido island.
Germany attacks Verdun to bleed France white; the battle lasts ten months and costs some seven hundred thousand casualties.
The house reading has the Shadowlands of Verdun turn to a sea of mud and ghosts where Spectres hunt the newly dead.
The house reading has Kindred haunt the dressing stations behind Verdun, and the Camarilla struggles to stop Masquerade breaches among the dying.
Italy attacks again on the Isonzo with little gain.
French and German troops fight for months over a hill called Dead Man.
Irish republicans seize the Dublin General Post Office and proclaim a republic; the leaders are shot after the surrender.
The house reading has the Irish Kithain see the Rising as a poem made real, and the Unseelie mourn its poets.
The starving British at Kut surrender; many of the prisoners die on the march into Anatolia.
Austria attacks Italy from the Trentino and is held on the Asiago plateau.
The British and German fleets meet off Jutland; Britain loses more ships but keeps command of the sea.
Britain and France secretly agree how to divide the Ottoman Arab lands.
Brusilov breaks the Austrian line on a wide front, taking hundreds of thousands of prisoners.
Sharif Hussein proclaims the Arab revolt against the Ottomans at Mecca.
The war minister Lord Kitchener drowns when HMS Hampshire hits a mine off Orkney.
Germany fires diphosgene shells at Verdun in its last push for Fort Souville.
Britain attacks on the Somme and loses nearly sixty thousand men on the first day.
The house reading has Black Spiral Dancers move freely in the Somme mud, and the Garou find the Wyrm grown fat on the battle.
Italy takes Gorizia in the sixth Isonzo battle.
Romania declares war on Austria-Hungary and invades Transylvania.
The British beat an Ottoman attack on the canal at Romani in the Sinai.
Britain sends tanks into battle for the first time on the Somme.
German and Austrian armies drive the Romanians out of Transylvania.
Friedrich Adler shoots Austria's prime minister Sturgkh at dinner in a Vienna hotel.
French troops take back Fort Douaumont.
The old emperor dies at Schonbrunn after sixty-eight years on the throne; young Karl succeeds.
The house reading has Vienna's Tremere hold a vigil for the old emperor and begin preparing for an empire that may not last.
The Somme ends in mud and snow; over a million men are dead or wounded for six miles.
German troops enter Bucharest.
Russian aristocrats poison, shoot and drown the healer Rasputin.
Lloyd George becomes Britain's prime minister.
A failed potato crop and the blockade leave Germans eating turnips; hundreds of thousands die of hunger and cold.
Brno's workers queue for bread; the mills switch to army cloth, and women replace men in the factories.
Kazakhs and Kyrgyz rise against conscription for labour; Russian reprisals drive hundreds of thousands into China.
The house reading has the steppe Garou ride with the rebels against the tsar's labour draft.
Yuan Shikai declares himself emperor of China, the provinces revolt, and Yuan dies within months.
Refugee artists open the Cabaret Voltaire in Zurich and start Dada.
The house reading has a Marauder loose among the Dadaists, and the Cult of Ecstasy work to keep the cabaret from going mad entirely.
Masaryk, Benes and Stefanik form the Czechoslovak National Council in Paris.
A single road from Bar-le-Duc carries a lorry every few seconds to keep Verdun supplied.
Ostrava's pits and Vitkovice work round the clock for the army, with prisoners of war in the mines.
The house reading has Iteration X take a quiet interest in the Vitkovice works, and a Brno Hermetic sees the Weaver tighten.
Arab forces besiege Medina, whose Ottoman commander holds it beyond the end of the war.
Surgeons at Aldershot and Paris rebuild soldiers' faces; Harold Gillies's work founds modern plastic surgery.
Some hundred and forty thousand Chinese labourers sail to France to dig trenches and unload ships.
A British officer named T. E. Lawrence joins Faisal's army in the Hejaz.
The house reading has the Reborn of Egypt wary of Lawrence's band crossing old roads that hide old tombs.
The house reading has a Moravian soldier home from Galicia tell an Olomouc priest of something that drank from the dead.
Germany offers Mexico an alliance against America; British codebreakers read the telegram and publish it.
Germany sinks any ship near Britain without warning, wagering on starving Britain before America arrives.
Bread riots in Petrograd become revolution; the soldiers join the crowds and the tsar abdicates.
The British take Baghdad.
The British attack Gaza and fall back.
The United States declares war on Germany, and American troops begin to cross the Atlantic to France.
Canadian troops take Vimy Ridge.
France's offensive on the Chemin des Dames fails, and French divisions refuse to attack.
Germany sends Lenin home from Zurich in a sealed train.
Three shepherd children see a lady at Fatima in Portugal; in October a crowd sees the sun dance.
The house reading has the Celestial Chorus claim Fatima, the Technocracy dismiss it, and Inquisitors arrive to see for themselves.
The Austrian parliament meets again, and the Czech deputies demand a state of their own.
British miners blow up nineteen great mines under Messines Ridge; the sound is heard in London.
King Constantine is forced out and Greece joins the war under Venizelos.
German bombers raid London by day and kill over a hundred and sixty people, many of them schoolchildren.
The Czechoslovak brigade in Russia fights at Zborov against Austrian troops, many of them fellow Czechs.
Britain attacks at Ypres again; the rains turn the field into a swamp where men drown in shell holes.
Arab irregulars with T. E. Lawrence take Aqaba from the land side.
Soldiers and workers rise in Petrograd and are put down; Lenin flees to Finland.
Serbian and Yugoslav leaders agree to a kingdom of the South Slavs.
A great fire destroys the old centre of Thessaloniki and its Jewish quarter.
China declares war on Germany and sends labourers to France.
Italy takes the Bainsizza plateau at terrible cost; Austria's army is near breaking.
Germany takes Riga with new infiltration tactics.
Sun Yat-sen sets up a rival government in Canton.
German and Austrian troops break the Italian front at Caporetto; Italy loses three hundred thousand men, most as prisoners.
Australian light horsemen charge and take the wells of Beersheba.
The British break the Gaza line after taking Beersheba.
The Bolsheviks take the Winter Palace and seize power in Russia.
The house reading has Brujah in Petrograd see their dream at last, until the Ventrue and the Tremere of Moscow begin their own plans.
The house reading has the New World Order send agents to shape the new state, and Russian Mages scatter.
Britain promises a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.
Hundreds of British tanks break the line at Cambrai, but the gains are lost in a German counterattack.
The Italians hold a new line on the Piave and Monte Grappa after the rout at Caporetto.
Allenby enters Jerusalem on foot by the Jaffa Gate.
Bolshevik Russia makes an armistice with Germany.
The Bolsheviks set up a Soviet Ukraine at Kharkiv and march on Kiev.
Ukraine's Central Rada declares autonomy, then independence.
Finland declares independence from Russia.
Women riot over bread in Brno, Prostejov and Ostrava; troops fire on crowds.
Britain promises India the gradual growth of self-government.
The house reading has an Egyptian Reborn serve as a labour officer with Allenby's army, looking for an old tomb in Palestine.
A dancer called Mata Hari is shot as a spy at Vincennes; the house reading has the Arcanum note a Toreador's interest in the case.
Russian soldiers desert in millions to go home and share the land.
Siam declares war on Germany and sends a force to France.
The house reading has changelings at the front lose themselves to Banality, and Kithain houses in Britain forbid their young to enlist.
The Petrograd Soviet orders the army to obey its soldiers' committees, and discipline collapses.
Emperor Karl's secret peace letters to France are made public, and Karl is forced to grovel to Berlin.
Olomouc's barracks hold prisoners of war and the sick; typhus breaks out among them.
The Russian Church elects a patriarch for the first time in two centuries.
Gandhi leads indigo farmers in Bihar in a peaceful campaign against their planters.
The house reading has Glass Walkers find a Pentex forerunner selling the army gas masks that do not work.
The house reading has the Kindred of Brno find the starving thin and their blood weak; the prince allows hunting among soldiers on leave.
Hundreds of thousands strike in Vienna and Budapest over bread cuts and the slow peace talks.
Czech deputies meet in Prague and demand a state of the Czechs and Slovaks.
President Wilson's peace terms reach Vienna; they set out peace terms, among them self-determination for the peoples of Austria-Hungary.
Sailors of the Austrian fleet in the Bay of Kotor raise red flags; the mutiny is crushed and four are shot.
The Red Army takes Kiev and kills thousands; within weeks German troops drive them out.
Russia gives up Poland, the Baltic lands, Finland and Ukraine to make peace.
Germany throws its armies from the east at the British in Picardy and gains forty miles in days.
A German gun seventy-five miles away shells Paris; one shell kills eighty worshippers in a church on Good Friday.
A mild influenza spreads through the crowded army camps in France, among them the great base at Etaples.
Germany attacks again on the Lys; Haig orders his men to fight with their backs to the wall.
The Royal Navy tries to block the submarine port at Zeebrugge with sunken ships.
Manfred von Richthofen is shot down and killed over the Somme.
Czech writers and deputies swear an oath in Prague to stand together until independence.
Czechs, Poles, Romanians and South Slavs meet in Rome to plan the breakup of Austria-Hungary.
The Czechoslovak Legion, crossing Russia to sail home from Vladivostok, fights the Bolsheviks at Chelyabinsk and seizes the railway.
Germany breaks through on the Chemin des Dames and reaches the Marne again.
Czech soldiers back from Russian captivity mutiny at Rumburk in Bohemia; the leaders are shot.
The Transcaucasian republic breaks into Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan.
Armenians beat the Ottoman army at Sardarapat and save Yerevan.
American marines fight for weeks in a hunting wood near Chateau-Thierry.
Austria's last offensive fails on the flooded Piave.
Brno and Ostrava get almost no flour in the summer of 1918; workers strike and the army is sent in.
France recognises the Czechoslovak National Council as the basis of a future government.
The Bolsheviks shoot the former tsar, his family and servants in a cellar at Ekaterinburg.
The house reading has the old Ventrue of St Petersburg lose their ruling line in a night and blame the Brujah for it.
The last German attack fails on the Marne, and the Allies strike back.
The Czech Legion takes Kazan and the Russian gold reserve.
British, Canadian and Australian troops break the German line at Amiens: the black day of the German army.
A deadly strain of influenza breaks out in Brest, Freetown and Boston within weeks of each other.
Japan, America and the Allies land troops at Vladivostok, partly to help the Czech Legion.
Fanny Kaplan shoots Lenin, and the Bolsheviks answer with mass executions.
Britain recognises the Czechoslovaks as an Allied nation.
Allenby's cavalry break the Ottoman front at Megiddo and ride for Damascus.
Serbian and French troops break the Bulgarian line, and Bulgaria asks for peace.
The American army fights its first big battle on its own.
Ottoman and Azerbaijani troops take Baku and kill thousands of Armenians.
Over a million American soldiers attack in the Argonne forest in the war's last great battle.
Arab and Australian troops enter Damascus.
Emperor Karl offers to make Austria a federation of peoples; the peoples have already decided.
The National Committee in Prague declares an independent Czechoslovakia on 28 October without a shot.
Czech officials take over Brno; German parties try to join the Moravian lands to German Austria and fail.

items.t: A new prince for a new state
items.x: The house reading has the Kindred of Brno use the new republic to settle old scores; the prince recognises Prague's claims for the first time.
Italy breaks the Austro-Hungarian army as its regiments go home by nation.
The Ottoman empire makes peace on a British warship.
Budapest rises, Count Karolyi takes power, and Hungary breaks from Austria.
The Croatian diet breaks with Austria-Hungary and declares a South Slav state.
Influenza kills thousands in Prague and Brno as the republic is born; the painter Schiele dies in Vienna.
German admirals plan a last battle; the sailors put out the boilers.
German sailors refuse a last sortie, raise the red flag at Kiel, and revolution spreads through Germany.
A republic is proclaimed in Berlin, and Wilhelm II goes into exile in the Netherlands.
Germany signs the armistice in a railway carriage at Compiegne; the guns stop at eleven on 11 November.
Emperor Karl gives up his share of power in Austria; German Austria is proclaimed a republic.
Pilsudski takes command in Warsaw, and Poland returns after a hundred and twenty-three years.
The new National Assembly elects Masaryk president of Czechoslovakia.
The house reading has the Shadowlands of the Western Front left crowded with ghosts who do not believe it is over.
The house reading has the European septs count their losses after four years, and find that some caerns have gone silent.
Kurt Eisner proclaims a Bavarian republic, and the Wittelsbach king flees.
Allied warships anchor off Istanbul, and the occupation of the Ottoman capital begins.
Soldiers die in the last minutes before eleven o'clock; the Canadians end the war where the British began it, at Mons.
Hungary is proclaimed a republic.

items.t: The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes
items.x: Prince Alexander proclaims the united South Slav kingdom.
Czechoslovak troops occupy Opava and the German districts of Silesia and northern Moravia.
Czechoslovak and Italian-led troops push Hungarian forces out of Slovakia.
Czechoslovak troops close on Bratislava, then called Pressburg, and march in on the first day of the new year.
Poles and Ukrainians fight for Lviv after the empire falls.
The Spartacist League founds the German Communist Party; the January rising comes weeks later.
The house reading has the influenza fill the Shadowlands with the young; the Hierarchy blames Spectres, and Heretic cults grow.
The house reading has the Kindred of London fall ill after feeding on the sick; the house rule calls it a taint of the blood, not a true plague.
Influenza kills perhaps twelve million in India, more than anywhere else.
Rice prices double and riots spread across Japan; the government falls.
Armies, drought and influenza kill a large part of Persia's people.
Red and White armies fight across Russia; the Czech Legion holds the Trans-Siberian Railway.
Reds and Whites fight in Finland, and the Whites win with German help.
The house reading has a Czech Hermetic in the Legion carry a talisman across Siberia, and Russian Traditions hunt for it.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin of the coast watch Allied armies pour into Vladivostok and decide to wait them out.
The house reading has an Egyptian Reborn with the Arab armies search for a scroll hidden in Damascus.
The house reading has the Arcanum send scholars to Paris, fearing that new borders will move old guarded sites.
The Allied blockade of Germany continues after the armistice, and hunger kills many more.
Foundation stones for the Hebrew University are laid on Mount Scopus.
Franz Kafka, ill with tuberculosis, writes in Prague and the countryside while the empire falls.
The German mark begins the fall that will turn into the great inflation.
Cholera and influenza strike Baghdad in the first months of British rule.
Chinese mills in Shanghai grow rich as European goods vanish from Asian markets.
Klimt dies of a stroke in February and Schiele of influenza in October.
The house reading has the Kithain of Moravia meet in a Brno cafe to choose a duke for the new republic's lands.
The house reading has the influenza and the war fill the Moravian Shadowlands; the local Hierarchy cannot ferry them all.

appr.x: Moravian regiments march to Galicia and Serbia in August 1914. The valley sends its young men, and many do not return.

appr.t: The citadel in the Fourth Maelstrom
appr.x: In the Fourth Great Maelstrom the Moravian citadel shelters the dead of the Eastern Front and holds its walls.
By 1917 the towns go hungry; there are bread riots and strikes. Feeding is easy and dangerous: everyone is out at night.
On 28 October 1918 Czechoslovakia is declared. Spanish influenza runs through the country that autumn.
Stopping Lord Vargo in 1914 led to the New World Order's founding; the Ahl-i-Batin left the Council in 1932; a short alliance with the Union beat back the Nephandi in the Second World War.
A Malkavian of the Seventh Generation, Embraced in 1915 by Trimeggian, born into wealth.
The dead of the Great War flood the Underworld. The Somme sets off a storm that ravages the Shadowlands.
The setting covers the years from Armistice Day, 11 November 1918, up to the night before the stock market crash of 1929.

items.x: The victors meet in Paris to redraw the map of Europe and the Middle East; the beaten are not invited.
Freikorps veterans crush a communist rising in Berlin and murder Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht.
Czechoslovakia and Poland fight over the coal district of Cieszyn Silesia, beside Ostrava.
Bela Kun's communists take power in Hungary for a hundred and thirty-three days.
Czech troops fire on Germans demonstrating for self-rule in the Sudeten towns; fifty-four die.
Egyptians rise against British rule when the nationalist Zaghlul is exiled.
Koreans read a declaration of independence in Seoul; Japanese troops kill thousands across the country.
General Dyer's troops fire into an unarmed crowd in the Jallianwala Bagh and kill hundreds.
Beijing students march against the treaty giving Shandong to Japan, and a new Chinese culture is born.
Greek troops land at Smyrna with Allied blessing, and the war for Anatolia begins.
Mustafa Kemal lands at Samsun and begins organising Turkish resistance.
Germany signs the treaty in the Hall of Mirrors, accepting guilt for the war and huge reparations.
The interned German fleet scuttles itself at Scapa Flow.
Austria signs away its empire and is forbidden to join Germany.
Brno gets its Czech university at last, named for the president.
Brno absorbs twenty-three villages and suburbs and becomes the second city of the republic.
The house reading has Brno's Kindred court give itself Czech names for its offices, and the German-speaking elders take offence.
Afghanistan fights Britain for a month and wins control of its own foreign affairs.
Germany's national assembly meets at Weimar and writes a democratic constitution.
Hungary loses two thirds of its land, Slovakia among it, by the Treaty of Trianon.
Pilsudski's Poles turn the Red Army back before Warsaw and stop the revolution from marching west.
The Ottoman sultan signs away most of Anatolia; the Turkish nationalists refuse it.
Czechoslovakia adopts a democratic constitution on the French model.
France defeats King Faisal's Syrian army at Maysalun and takes Damascus.
Iraq rises against British rule; the RAF bombs villages to end it.
The Allies give Syria and Lebanon to France and Iraq and Palestine to Britain.

items.t: The Reborn and the new Egypt
items.x: The house reading has the Reborn watch Egypt's nationalists with hope, for a free Egypt guards its own dead.
Priests break from Rome to found a national Czechoslovak church.
The sailors of Kronstadt rise against the Bolsheviks and are crushed.
War and requisitions bring famine to the Volga; five million die.
Churchill makes Faisal king of Iraq and Abdullah emir of Transjordan.
A dozen delegates found the Chinese Communist Party in Shanghai.
The Irish Free State is born, and the civil war follows.
The house reading has Vienna's Hermetics salvage the old court library's secret shelves as the empire's archives are split.
The Turkish army retakes Smyrna, and the Greek and Armenian quarters burn.
Mussolini's Blackshirts march on Rome and the king makes him prime minister.
Howard Carter opens the sealed tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings.
The house reading has the tomb's guardians wake, and Lord Carnarvon's death the next spring is no accident.
Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and Transcaucasia join as the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics.
The house reading has the Arcanum smile at the fairy photographs that fool Conan Doyle, and quietly visit the beck at Cottingley.
Greece and Turkey trade populations; over a million Greeks and half a million Muslims are uprooted.
Mustafa Kemal proclaims the Republic of Turkey with its capital at Ankara.
An earthquake and firestorm destroy Tokyo and Yokohama and kill over a hundred thousand; mobs murder Koreans.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin of Tokyo see the quake as a sign of the Sixth Age deepening.
The German mark collapses; a loaf of bread costs billions and the savings of the middle class vanish.
Hitler tries to seize power in Munich and is jailed.
The Turkish republic abolishes the caliphate and sends the last caliph into exile.
Lenin dies after a series of strokes, and Stalin begins to outmanoeuvre the other heirs.
Franz Kafka dies near Vienna; a friend refuses to burn the manuscripts.
The house reading has the names on the Menin Gate draw the unremembered dead of Flanders in a slow crowd.
The Druze rise against the French, and France shells Damascus.
Reza Khan ends the Qajar dynasty and crowns himself shah of Persia.
British-led police fire on protesters in Shanghai, and strikes spread across China.
Germany, France and Belgium agree their western borders; the eastern ones are left open.
Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists march north from Canton to beat the warlords and unify China.
British unions call a general strike for nine days in support of the miners.
Janacek's opera of a woman who has lived three hundred years opens in Brno.
The house reading has the Kindred of Brno attend Janacek's premiere and wonder who told the composer.
Chiang turns on his communist allies in Shanghai and kills thousands.
Oil gushes for days from the well at Baba Gurgur near Kirkuk, and Iraq's oil age begins.
Fritz Lang's film of a city of machines and workers opens in Berlin.
Brno opens its new exhibition grounds with a show of ten years of the republic; functionalist buildings rise across the city.
Hassan al-Banna, a schoolteacher, founds the Muslim Brotherhood in Ismailia to renew Egypt through Islam.
Alexander Fleming notices mould killing bacteria in a dish.
Czechoslovakia marks a thousand years since the murder of St Wenceslas, and St Vitus Cathedral is finished.
Arab rioters kill sixty-seven Jews in Hebron, ending a community that had lived there for centuries.
The Wall Street crash spreads ruin to Europe; two years later the Vienna Creditanstalt fails and the Depression deepens.
The house reading has the Syndicate allow the crash, the better to buy up the wreckage.
Mies van der Rohe finishes the Tugendhat house on a Brno hillside, a landmark of modern architecture.
Gandhi walks to the sea at Dandi to make salt against British law; tens of thousands are jailed.
Indigenous Seediq rise against Japanese rule in Taiwan and are crushed with gas.
Japanese officers blow up a railway and use it to seize Manchuria.
The Yangtze and Huai flood, and perhaps two million die.
The shoe king Tomas Bata builds Zlin into a company town of brick and glass and sells shoes across the world.
Spain's king leaves and a republic is proclaimed.
Tomas Bata dies when his plane crashes on take-off at Otrokovice.
Stalin's seizure of grain and seed starves Ukraine and the Kuban; millions die in villages sealed off by police.
Ibn Saud, master of Najd and the Hejaz, names his kingdom Saudi Arabia after his own house.
Iraq joins the League of Nations as an independent kingdom.
President Hindenburg appoints Hitler chancellor of Germany, and the Nazis take the state apart within months.
The German parliament burns, and the Nazis use it to suspend civil rights.
The house reading has German Kindred and Mages split over the Nazis; some see a tool, most see a fire that burns the hand.
The first concentration camp opens at Dachau outside Munich, for communists, socialists and other enemies of the state.
Japan walks out of the League of Nations over Manchuria.
Socialist workers fight the government in Vienna for four days; the army shells the workers' flats.

items.t: The Night of the Long Knives
items.x: Hitler has the SA leaders and other rivals murdered.
The Red Army breaks out of encirclement and marches six thousand miles to Shaanxi.
An earthquake on the Nepal border kills ten thousand.
The aged Masaryk retires, and the foreign minister Edvard Benes becomes president of Czechoslovakia.
Germany strips Jews of citizenship and forbids marriage between Jews and other Germans.
An earthquake in the night destroys Quetta in Baluchistan and kills thirty thousand.
Reza Shah asks the world to call the country Iran.
Generals rise against the Spanish republic, and Europe's armies try out their weapons in Spain.
The house reading has the Sabbat and the Camarilla both fight in the shadow of the Spanish war; the Lasombra claim Madrid.
Germany stages the Olympics as propaganda; Jesse Owens wins four gold medals.
Palestinian Arabs strike and rise against British rule and Jewish immigration.
Chiang Kai-shek is kidnapped by his own generals until he agrees to fight Japan with the communists.
Brno opens its road racing circuit, and the Czechoslovak Grand Prix draws crowds of a hundred thousand.
Fighting at the Marco Polo Bridge begins full war between China and Japan.
Japanese troops kill hundreds of thousands of civilians and prisoners in Nanjing.
The house reading has the Yomi stir beneath Nanjing, and the Kuei-jin courts of the city fall.
German and Italian bombers destroy the Basque town of Guernica on market day, and Picasso paints it.
Stalin's police shoot hundreds of thousands and send millions to the camps.
Germany annexes Austria, and Czechoslovakia is surrounded on three sides.
Britain and France agree that Germany may take the Sudetenland; Czechoslovakia is not asked.
German troops march into the borderlands, Opava and Znojmo among them, and Czechs flee inland.
Nazis burn synagogues and smash Jewish shops across Germany and Austria.
The house reading has the Kindred of Brno split after Munich; some flee to Prague, the prince goes to ground under the Spilberk.
Hahn and Strassmann split the uranium atom in Berlin.
German troops enter Prague and Brno; Bohemia and Moravia become a protectorate of the Reich and Slovakia a client state.
Germany invades Poland, the Soviets follow from the east, and Britain and France declare war.
After student protests, Czech universities are closed, nine students are shot and twelve hundred sent to camps.
The Soviet Union attacks Finland, and the Finns hold in the snow for three months.
The house reading has the Underworld shake as the war begins; the Hierarchy prepares for the worst Maelstrom in memory.
The house reading has the Technocracy's council forbid any convention to serve the Reich, though some Progenitors ignore it.
War comes in September 1939. The Ventrue Gotsdam sends Dylan Bruce, the Scot who dug the fortified havens, to France with the British Expeditionary Force. Fits: Follows the 1930 Dylan Bruce card.
items.ref: Dread Names, Red List p. 69; the year is a house reading.

items.x: Soviet police shoot over twenty thousand Polish officers and prisoners in the Katyn forest and elsewhere.
German armour breaks through the Ardennes at Sedan; France falls in six weeks.
Over three hundred thousand Allied soldiers are taken off the beaches at Dunkirk.
German bombers attack London night after night for eight months.
The house reading has London's Kindred shelter deep in the Underground with the mortals, and Masquerade breaches go unreported in the chaos.
Benes forms a government in exile in London; Czechoslovak airmen fly in the Battle of Britain.
Japanese troops enter French Indochina by agreement with Vichy, and America cuts off Japan's oil.
The house reading has the Arcanum move its London library to the country and lose a crate of Prague papers on the way.
Germany bombs Belgrade without warning and overruns Yugoslavia and Greece in a few weeks.
A pro-Axis government in Iraq fights the British and loses; a pogrom follows in Baghdad.
Germany invades the Soviet Union with three million men.
Britain and the Soviets invade Iran, and Reza Shah gives up the throne to his son.
German units shoot nearly thirty-four thousand Jews in two days in a ravine outside Kiev.
Germany surrounds Leningrad; about a million die in a siege of nearly nine hundred days.
Reinhard Heydrich takes charge of the protectorate and begins mass arrests and executions.
Jews from Prague and Brno are deported to Lodz and Terezin.
Japan attacks Hong Kong, Malaya and Pearl Harbor in a day.
The Soviets stop the Germans before Moscow in the cold and counterattack.
The fortress town of Terezin becomes a ghetto and transit camp for the Jews of Bohemia and Moravia.
The house reading has an Arcanum member smuggle out drawings from Terezin, and some of them show things no child should know.
Nazi officials meet at a villa by the Wannsee to plan the murder of Europe's Jews.
Britain surrenders Singapore with eighty thousand troops, the worst defeat in its history.
Czechoslovak paratroopers Gabcik and Kubis ambush Heydrich in a Prague street; Heydrich dies a week later.
In revenge the Germans shoot the men of Lidice, send the women and children to camps, and raze the village.
The Germans destroy the hamlet of Lezaky and kill its people.

items.t: The church of St Cyril and Methodius
items.x: The paratroopers die fighting in the crypt of a Prague church.
The house reading has the dead of Lidice refuse the Hierarchy and haunt the empty fields as a Circle.
Japan loses four carriers at Midway in the Pacific.
The Germans reach the Volga at Stalingrad, and the city becomes a battle of streets and cellars.
Montgomery's Eighth Army breaks Rommel's lines at El Alamein.
The camps of Auschwitz, Treblinka, Sobibor and Belzec murder millions of Jews, Roma and others.
The house reading has the Garou of Europe find the camps the deepest wounds the Wyrm has made in their age.
Japan marches American and Filipino prisoners to camps; thousands die on the road.
The frozen remnant of the German Sixth Army surrenders at Stalingrad; ninety thousand men go into captivity.
The Jews of the Warsaw ghetto fight the Germans for a month.
The greatest tank battle in history is fought at Kursk, and Germany loses the east.
Allied bombing creates a firestorm in Hamburg that kills about forty thousand.
Famine kills perhaps three million in Bengal while rice is shipped elsewhere.
The house reading has the Technocracy work quietly on both the radar and the bomb, and Traditions fight to keep magic out of the war.
Allied armies land on five beaches in Normandy, and the liberation of western Europe begins.
The Polish Home Army rises in Warsaw; the Soviets wait across the river while the Germans destroy the city.
Slovaks rise against the Germans and their own regime; the rising is crushed in two months.
Allied bombers strike Brno's factories and rail yards; hundreds of civilians die.
Soviet and Czechoslovak troops fight their way through the Dukla Pass into Slovakia.
The British and Indians stop the Japanese invasion of India at Imphal and Kohima.
The house reading has the Toreador of Paris return from hiding and quarrel over who collaborated.
Soviet troops reach Auschwitz and find seven thousand prisoners left behind by the death marches.
Allied bombers destroy the old city of Dresden in a firestorm that kills some twenty-five thousand.
Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin meet at Yalta to shape postwar Europe.
The Red Army takes Brno after a week of fighting.
Soviet and Czechoslovak troops take Ostrava after weeks of fighting.
Prague rises against the Germans; the Vlasov army changes sides and helps.
Hitler is dead in the Berlin bunker, and Germany surrenders on 8 May; Prague is still fighting.
Some twenty thousand German-speaking people of Brno are driven toward the Austrian border; thousands die on the road.
Czechoslovakia begins expelling its three million Germans; many are killed in the first wild months.
American atomic bombs destroy Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and Japan surrenders.
The house reading has the bombs tear holes in the Shroud, and the Dark Kingdom of Jade shaken to its depths.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin of Japan hide from the sun the bombs made, and many never return.
The house reading has the Technocracy see the bomb as proof that its paradigm has won the war.
