The Allies agree how to run Germany and approve the expulsion of Germans from the east.
Ho Chi Minh declares an independent Vietnam in Hanoi.
Korea is divided at the thirty-eighth parallel between Soviet and American zones.
The house reading has the Kindred who fled Brno return to a city of Soviet soldiers and missing German elders.
The Nazi leaders are tried and many are hanged.
The Communists come first in the free election of 1946.
Jewish militants of the Irgun bomb the British headquarters in Jerusalem's King David Hotel and kill ninety-one.
Riots between Hindus and Muslims in Calcutta kill thousands in four days and foreshadow partition.
The house reading has the dead of the Brno march haunt the road south, and the Moravian Hierarchy argue about whose they are.
India and Pakistan become independent; millions flee and perhaps a million die.
A Bedouin shepherd finds ancient scrolls in a cave near Qumran.
The house reading has the Celestial Chorus and the Society of Leopold both send scholars to the scrolls.
The Communists take power in Czechoslovakia when the democratic ministers resign and Benes gives way.
The foreign minister Jan Masaryk is found dead below his window.
Ben-Gurion declares the state of Israel in Tel Aviv, and the armies of its Arab neighbours invade.
Some seven hundred thousand Palestinians flee or are driven from their homes.
The Soviets blockade West Berlin, and the Allies fly in its food for a year.
A Hindu nationalist shoots Gandhi at a prayer meeting in Delhi.
Mao proclaims the People's Republic of China from the Gate of Heavenly Peace, and Chiang flees to Taiwan.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin courts of China driven underground by the new state.
America, Canada and ten European states found the North Atlantic alliance against the Soviet bloc.
North Korea invades the south, and American and United Nations troops are drawn in, then China.
The Chinese army enters Tibet and defeats its small army at Chamdo.
The house reading has the Akashic Brotherhood carry treasures out of Tibet.
Prime Minister Mossadegh nationalises Iran's oil, and Britain blockades Iranian exports.
Nasser's Free Officers overthrow King Farouk, and Egypt becomes a republic within a year.
Fourteen Communist leaders, most of them Jewish, are tried as traitors; eleven are hanged.
Stalin dies at his dacha after a stroke, and the camps begin slowly to empty.
A currency reform wipes out savings, and workers in Plzen storm the town hall.
American and British agents help the army and the mobs overthrow Mossadegh, and the shah returns.
The fighting in Korea ends with the peninsula divided.

items.t: The Kindred in the show trials
items.x: The house reading has Prague's Kindred use the purges to settle their own accounts, and hunters among the secret police note odd deaths.
The Viet Minh crush the French at Dien Bien Phu.
The Soviet bloc forms its own military alliance in Warsaw in answer to NATO.
The four powers leave Austria, which becomes free and neutral; Vienna is no longer divided.
Asian and African leaders meet at Bandung in Java and found the movement of non-aligned nations.
Japan's conservatives merge into the Liberal Democratic Party, which will rule for decades.
Khrushchev denounces Stalin's crimes to a closed session of the party congress, and the speech leaks abroad.
Hungary rises against Soviet rule; Soviet tanks crush it within weeks.
Israel, Britain and France attack Egypt after Nasser takes the canal; America forces them out.
Poland wins a gentler communism under Gomulka after riots in Poznan.
The house reading has the Brujah of Budapest fight beside the students and the Tzimisce feed on the reprisals.
The Soviet Union puts the first satellite in orbit.
The house reading has the Void Engineers race to claim space for the Technocracy before the Traditions can dream it otherwise.
A nuclear waste tank explodes in the Urals and poisons a wide stretch of land; the Soviets keep it secret.
France, Germany, Italy and the Low Countries found the European Economic Community.
Officers overthrow Iraq's monarchy and kill the young king and his family in the palace courtyard.
Mao's Great Leap brings famine that kills tens of millions.
Czechoslovakia's pavilion and its Laterna Magika win the Brussels fair.
Tibet rises against China, and the Dalai Lama flees to India.

Tibet rises in March 1959 and the Dalai Lama flees to India. The Akashic Brotherhood's old refuge is now under Communist guns. Fits: The Akashics went back into Tibet after 1360 on the approved cards.
items.ref: Real history (1959); the Akashics are a house reading.

items.x: Czechoslovakia declares itself a socialist republic, the second in the bloc after the Soviet Union.
Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela found OPEC in Baghdad to take back control of oil prices.
Yuri Gagarin orbits the earth in Vostok 1, the first person in space.
East Germany builds a wall through Berlin overnight to stop its people from leaving.
The house reading follows canon in spirit: Berlin's Kindred divide like the city, and crossing becomes a matter for princes.
East Germany seals West Berlin on 13 August 1961. Gustav Breidenstein's Berlin is cut in two for 28 years. Fits: Ends with the Wall card of 1989.
items.ref: Real history (1961); Gustav from Berlin by Night.

items.x: Europe waits for nuclear war for thirteen days while America and the Soviets face off over missiles in Cuba.
China defeats India in a short war high in the Himalayas and keeps Aksai Chin.
The house reading has Liverpool's music pour Glamour into the Dreaming years before the Resurgence.
An earthquake destroys most of Skopje and kills over a thousand; the city is rebuilt to a Japanese plan.
A landslide into a dam reservoir in Italy sends a wave over the dam that kills two thousand.
Japan hosts the Olympics and opens the bullet train.
Reports of attacks on American destroyers in the Gulf of Tonkin let America widen its war in Vietnam.
China tests its first atomic bomb.
The army and militias kill half a million or more suspected communists.
India and Pakistan fight a three-week war over Kashmir that ends where it began.

items.t: The Sons of Ether and the space race
items.x: The house reading has the Sons of Ether launch their own etherships while the Void Engineers race the Soviets.
Mao unleashes the Red Guards against teachers, temples and party rivals.

items.t: The Red Guards and the shrines
items.x: The house reading has the Red Guards smash shrines the Kuei-jin had guarded for centuries; some courts are destroyed.
The Arno floods Florence, drowns its streets and damages thousands of paintings and books.
The Cultural Revolution, from 1966, smashes temples and the old learning. The Wu Lung lose more of their ground. Fits: Fits the Wu Lung card: weakened by Communist rule.
items.ref: Real history (1966 to 1976); the Wu Lung are a house reading.

items.x: Israel takes Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan.
Greek colonels seize power in a coup and rule Greece for seven years.
Alexander Dubcek begins socialism with a human face, and censorship lifts.
Communist forces attack cities across South Vietnam at the lunar new year; Hue is fought over for a month.
Students raise barricades in Paris, millions of workers strike, and France comes to a standstill.
Warsaw Pact troops invade Czechoslovakia; Brno's people stand in front of the tanks.
The house reading has Prague's Kindred split over the Spring; Ventrue loyal to Moscow help the invaders and the Anarchs pay for it.
American soldiers kill hundreds of villagers at My Lai.
The house reading has the StB open files on Brno's nightwalkers after the invasion, a knot later hunters will untangle.
The student Jan Palach sets fire to himself in Wenceslas Square in protest.
Czechoslovakia beats the Soviets twice at ice hockey, and crowds attack the Soviet airline office.
Apollo 11 lands on the Moon, and the world watches on television.
The house reading follows Changeling canon: the Moon landing reopens the Dreaming, and the sidhe return.
Husak's regime purges half a million party members and fires the reformers from universities, papers and theatres.
A cyclone kills perhaps half a million in East Pakistan.
Jordan's army fights the Palestinian guerrillas and drives them out to Lebanon.
Bangladesh breaks from Pakistan after a war and mass killings.
Palestinian gunmen kill eleven Israeli athletes at the Olympics.
Many of the Czech new-wave films are banned and their makers silenced.
Egypt and Syria attack Israel on the holiest day of the Jewish year and are thrown back after hard fighting.
Arab states cut oil to the West, prices quadruple, and Europe has car-free Sundays.
Turkey invades Cyprus after a Greek-backed coup, and the island is divided by a green line.
North Vietnamese tanks break into the presidential palace in Saigon; the last Americans leave by helicopter.
The Soviet bloc signs a promise to respect human rights.
Lebanon falls into fifteen years of civil war among its faiths, the Palestinians and foreign armies.
The Khmer Rouge empty Phnom Penh into the countryside; in four years perhaps two million Cambodians die.
The house reading has the Yama Kings' servants grow strong on Cambodia's dead, and the Kuei-jin of Angkor go to war against them.
An earthquake destroys Tangshan and kills a quarter of a million.
The rock band Plastic People of the Universe is jailed.
Dissidents sign Charter 77 asking the state to keep its own human rights laws.
The house reading has a few signers of Charter 77 Embraced in later years, so that some Kindred of Prague still carry the Charter's grudge.
Deng Xiaoping opens China's economy to markets and foreign money after Mao's death.
Karol Wojtyla of Krakow becomes Pope John Paul II, the first pope from beyond Italy in four centuries.
The shah flees, and Ayatollah Khomeini returns from exile to found an Islamic republic.
Armed militants seize the Grand Mosque in Mecca and hold it for two weeks.
Soviet troops enter Afghanistan to prop up a communist government and fight a ten-year war.
The house reading has the Garou of the Hindu Kush fight the Soviets' shadow in the Umbra.
Shipyard workers in Gdansk strike under Lech Walesa and found Solidarity, the first free union in the bloc.
Iraq invades Iran, and eight years of trench war and gas follow along the Shatt al-Arab.
General Jaruzelski declares martial law and jails Solidarity's leaders.
Soldiers shoot President Sadat at a military parade.
Lebanese militias kill hundreds of Palestinians in the Sabra and Shatila camps while Israeli troops ring them.
Syria crushes a rising in Hama and kills thousands.
Truck bombs kill American and French peacekeepers in Beirut.
A gas leak from a pesticide plant kills thousands.
Indian troops storm the Golden Temple, and Indira Gandhi is killed by bodyguards.
Mikhail Gorbachev takes power and begins glasnost and perestroika.
A reactor explodes at Chernobyl and spreads fallout across Europe.
The house reading follows Werewolf canon in spirit: the Black Spiral Dancers claim the poisoned zone.
The house reading has the New World Order help the Soviets hide the scale of the disaster.
Reactor four at Chernobyl explodes on 26 April 1986. The Garou of the region speak of a wound in the Umbra that will not close. Fits: No clash.
items.ref: Real history (1986); the Garou are a house reading.

items.x: Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank rise against Israeli occupation.
Iraq attacks the Kurdish town of Halabja with poison gas and kills thousands.
An earthquake in northern Armenia kills twenty-five thousand and levels Spitak.
A bomb destroys an airliner over Lockerbie in Scotland.
The army clears Tiananmen Square of protesters and kills hundreds or more.
A muddled announcement opens the border, and East Germans pour through the Berlin Wall.
Students beaten in Prague start the Velvet Revolution, and the communists give way within weeks.
Crowds fill Freedom Square in Brno as the regime collapses.
Romania rises against Ceausescu, who is caught, tried in an hour and shot on Christmas Day.
The playwright Vaclav Havel, jailed a year before, is elected president by the old parliament.
The house reading has the Camarilla rush into the old bloc as the Sabbat and the old bloc's princes scramble.
The house reading has the Velvet Revolution light the Dreaming of Prague, and the Kithain of Brno dance on Freedom Square.

appr.x: Masaryk University is founded in Brno in January 1919. Land reform breaks up the great estates in the years after.
On 30 September 1938 the Munich agreement hands the German-speaking borderlands to Germany. Families and Kindred alike decide where they will be when the border moves.
On 15 March 1939 German troops occupy what is left of Bohemia and Moravia. The Gestapo keep files; files are dangerous to the Masquerade.
After Heydrich is attacked in Prague on 27 May 1942, reprisals follow, among them the destruction of Lidice on 10 June.
Brno is freed in April 1945. In the months after, Germans are driven out of the country; the heirs of the valley's German council lose their houses. The old Moravian families stay.
The Communist Party takes power in February 1948. Land, shops and workshops are taken by the state over the next years.
In April 1950 the state closes the monasteries in one night. The Church's hunters lose their houses and go underground with the rest of the faithful.
In 1968 the reforms of the Prague Spring open the country; on the night of 20 to 21 August Warsaw Pact armies end them.
At the Resurgence the old crossroads trod opens again for a few nights. Fae of the old families remember who they were.
The secret police keep an informer in every block. Kindred of the march learn to feed only where no one writes things down.
On 17 November 1989 police beat students in Prague; within six weeks the regime has fallen.
In the 1920s and 1930s Doran learned of a Syndicate of mages in southern Louisiana. Huey Long worked with other Technomancers in the north of the state and was killed by yet another group of mages.
Once Lily Thorne, an American silent film actress who fell into a river while filming in the Black Forest in the late 1920s and was Embraced underwater by the Gangrel Methuselah Brunhilde.

Insight Investments is a fast-growing Chicago investment house; the Marsh Institute goes back to a telepathic financier who made a fortune in 1920s real estate and was warned of the crash by a precognitive rival.
The clan's ties to the Gambino crime family go back to 1921, when the Giovanni supplied Joe Masseria with fresh talent for a cut of the racket.
In 1923 Professor Donald Richardson claimed that a relic from the reign of Thothmes I described a secret society of Sacred Artisans, writing in a script only the Enlightened could read.
In 1930 the Council of Seven forbade any study of Akhu, then allowed it again in 1973, persuaded by the Pontifex of Antioch, who argued the clan had to know the Serpents' magic to defend against it.
The Technocracy, the Japanese invasion of the 1930s and Communist rule have left the Wu Lung greatly weakened.

A Scot who dug shelters in London in the late 1930s for the Ventrue Gotsdam, who had the family build fortified havens across England and later sent Dylan to France with the British Expeditionary Force.
The Special Affairs Department is thought to date from the end of the Truman years, but its roots go back to the 1930s.
In 1931 an Anacreon of the Silent Legion in Boston resigned, protesting that Stygia ignored the Shadowlands beyond its borders while the mortal crisis stretched local Legions past their limits.
Since Japan invaded China in 1937, Shanghai and the provinces under the Flesh Court have fought a nightly war against Japanese akuma, and its rule has decayed into a loose oligarchy.
On the night of October 10, 1940, bombs fell across more than 50 districts of London, while Dylan Bee sheltered in a trench by the Thames.
In June 1943 ghouls of Don Sebastian drove into Venice and beat up anarchs who had fled the Mexican Sabbat; the police arrested the victims. The anarchs struck back at the Don's thugs the next night.
A Tzimisce of the Tenth Generation, Embraced in 1943 by Efrain Sortano, once a medical professor.
Anarchs drive the Camarilla out of California and declare the Anarch Free State.
Don Sebastian had Jeremy MacNeil seized and beaten in 1944. MacNeil urged six weeks of patience, and on 21 December 1944 armed anarchs struck the elders in their havens before dawn.

By the end of the Revolt's second night every Los Angeles elder had been destroyed, driven off or forced into hiding, and just before dawn on 22 December 1944 Jeremy MacNeil proclaimed the Anarch Free States.
The Revolutionary Council, the leaders of the 1944 Revolt, wrote the Status Perfectus, the 'Perfect State', setting out how the Free States would govern themselves rather than be ruled.
The bombs tear the Tempest open. Gorool rises, and Charon is lost fighting it.
By the end of February 1945 the Free States ran from the Mexican border north to San Jose, and from the Pacific to within 50 miles of Nevada.
Most Nephandi were driven past the Horizon in 1945, leaving centuries of building behind; a few strongholds were found and burned, but most never were.
A short wartime alliance with the Technocracy crushed a rising Nephandi threat and was disowned in 1946, when the Council marked its renewal with Reconciliation Day.
A spacecraft crashed near Roswell in 1947, hidden by the Void Engineers and New World Order.

Hong Kong was the Triad capital from 1949 until the 1997 handover, which sent many societies overseas and drew Western attention to them for the first time; their roots lie in old Chinese secret societies.
Four founders (Philip Marshall, Enrico Sagunto, Ginerva Salamanca and Gregory Winter) started it in the 1950s to help ghouls who escaped or were abandoned by their domitors.
They rose after the Sabbat civil war of the late 1950s, when the clanless Joseph Pander led them against the Moderates at the urging of Lasombra and Tzimisce elders, and won formal recognition.
A Tremere of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1950 by Duke Traska; a decorated Second World War soldier who later worked for an unnamed intelligence agency.
In the 1950s Simcoe and other Syndicate members formed the Dominion Gaming Group, later DCG Ltd.
Founded in the 1950s among early liberation theologians of Central America, it sets out to bring justice and mercy to those denied both.
By one Sabbat veteran's count, New York in the late 1950s held perhaps 300 Cainites, half of them Lasombra and Tzimisce.
Genegineers were called Mutagenic Engineers until 1954.
Born in England in 1957, Dane felt called to the Lord's work young and sought to join the Jesuits in 1980.
Any Kindred who hears the call may attend, and young vampires may speak. In 1957 a switch of venue from Rotterdam to Brussels left visiting American elders to walk into the Sabbat.
A Lasombra of the Eighth Generation, Embraced in 1957 by Tobias Smith as part of a Sabbat campaign.

The Mariana Trench, the deepest point of the planet's surface, holds the ocean's strongest Grotto; Void Engineer explorers first reached it in 1960, and a few squads and two Tradition cabals have gone down since.
As the largest Camarilla city in the United States, Chicago turned into the main battleground of the 1960s War of Ages against the anarchs.

A pestilent, ratlike creature that the Sabbat take for a werewolf has been seen in the city's sewers since the 1960s. To lure it out, packs lower mortal bait on a rope into the sewers, and something below always kills it.
Many of the Patient Deed stood down when True Silverheels called for the camps to end, remembering protests of the 1960s that had gone badly.

The Free State survived a Sabbat attack in 1965 and a war with a mortal gang in 1992, but the Cathayan invasion of 1998 broke it. Anarchs briefly held San Francisco before Cathayans drove them out in mid-1998.
During the 1966 riots in Los Angeles, after the Sabbat siege of the city, a nomad Sabbat pack watched a mortal gang led by a young drug-fuelled man named Angelo burn building after building.
After the anarchs were crushed in 1968, Lodin outlawed the Embrace across the metropolitan area, and for the most part the ban was obeyed.

The war ended at the 1968 Democratic convention. With the Ventrue justicar's leave, Lodin sent police and elders against the protesters, and archons and elders fell on the anarchs out of sight of the cameras. More than 100 vampires vanished that night.
The name Takeouji comes from a 1968 manifesto by Burakumin, which called the old ways hopelessly outdated and asked for a new breed of Kuei-jin with all the virtues of bamboo.
As people watch the first steps on the Moon, Dreaming floods back into the world and some of the lost fae return.
Sidhe came back out of Arcadia at the Resurgence, when the gates opened again in 1969.
The gates to Arcadia opened again on July 20, 1969.
Liam and Scathach nobles took the Changeling Way rather than flee, and greeted the returning sidhe in 1969.

appr.t: Ailil and the right of demesne
appr.x: When the noble houses returned in 1969, Seelie houses seized every freehold they could and drove out the commoners who had kept them; Ailil says many of those freeholds were once its own and refuses to honor the new holders.
In 1969 the group broke into a restricted hangar, and it keeps the devices it found hidden in abandoned warehouses.
Born in Bergen in 1970, Svein rose in the Norwegian black metal scene of the early 1990s and was Embraced in 1991 by Brynjar, a Follower of Set of the 12th Generation.
Edgardo took work from mortals and Kindred alike, and in the 1970s grew close to the Baader-Meinhof Group.
After a string of financial mistakes in the 1970s, MacLaren was urged to leave and became Prince of Kingston, Ontario.

appr.t: The Zaibatsu and the Elemental Dragons
appr.x: Other Asian Technocratic bodies kept silent too; in the late 1970s a few Taiping Tianguo agents admitted aiding North Vietnamese forces on Syndicate orders.
The Institute was never just about computers, though its close work with the Virtual Adepts through the 1970s and 1980s led many to think so.

Several old vampires gained sway over major local businesses, including forestry firms, while Richard Daly, a rich and influential businessman who leads the Glass Walkers, became a key figure of Garou Vancouver from the early 1970s.
Opened in the mid-19th century, Highgate has always had ties to the supernatural, including talk of a Vampire of Highgate in the 1970s and 1980s.
Black Tooth, a Simba from Zululand, gathered a pride in the ivory wars of the late 1970s and struck at all European intruders, supernatural or mundane.
While building Atlanta's subway in the late 1970s, MARTA crews failed again and again to blast through one stretch of granite that geologists could find nothing wrong with.
In 1974 the French Tremere won over Madame Yacine, a Malkavian practitioner living among the Algerian community of Lyon.
A Brujah of the 11th Generation, Embraced in 1974 by Fat Ciaran; ambushed and staked on a farm truck bound for London in 1976, then left in torpor three years.
Cordoned off since the Turkish invasion of 1974, Varosha is frozen in time, its shops still hung with clothes untouched for decades.
Training of new Qutbs began in Isfahan in October 1979.
In 1979 the Shah's government fell and Technocratic agents were driven out of Iran, a turn the Batini call the Reprieve.
DiMatto, child of a Giovanni cousin, was Embraced in 1980 after a youthful fascination with the darker side of the family.

Few Restless gathered in Atlantic City until gambling was made legal there in 1980; before that its dead were mostly Enfants and old wraiths bound to happier summers, ignored by Hierarchy and Heretic alike.
In 1982 Dane destroyed a neonate in Washington, D.C., and in that moment was flooded with names, faces and scenes, sure of a calling to hunt vampires.
In 1985 the Council sought a normal footing with the Camarilla against unnamed threats; in 1990 all contact stopped, then all contact with any Kindred in Russia, and Tremere spying there failed.
The quake of 19 September 1985 damaged over 4,000 buildings and killed more than 9,000 people.
In 1986, in return for Annabelle's support against the anarch leader Maldavis, Lodin had to let Annabelle make two childer and to attend the primogen in Elysium on the first Monday of every month.
Procet, a member of the council, vanished in the Thanksgiving Massacre of 1986, when Lodin's mortal servants staked anarchs in their havens by day.
Its resident, Kathryn Green, made a fortune in the 1987 stock market crash by buying while others sold.

appr.t: Baba Yaga and the Fall of the Wall
appr.x: Even Gustav was caught off guard when the crossing points opened on November 9, 1989; hoping to win back lost ground, the prince let the Wall come down from June 13, 1990.
A Malkavian of the 10th Generation, Embraced in 1989 by Colin McAllister; each night the delusion of being the Black Dragon Princess, heir of the Yellow Emperor, grows stronger.
Old Clan Tzimisce of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1989 by Janek Ritka; dissident parents were arrested in Prague under Gustav Husak.

name: Modern and the Time of Judgment

items.x: Soviet troops storm Baku after pogroms against Armenians and kill over a hundred civilians.
Lithuania declares independence from the Soviet Union, the first republic to do so.
Czechs and Slovaks quarrel over the country's new name and settle on the Czech and Slovak Federative Republic.
Czechoslovakia's first free election in forty-four years gives Civic Forum a landslide; Moravian regional parties win seats.
An earthquake in northern Iran kills over thirty-five thousand.
Saddam Hussein's army overruns Kuwait in a day.
East Germany joins the Federal Republic, and Germany is one state again.
Western tourists flood Prague, and the old town fills with exchange booths and beer.
The house reading has Camarilla envoys reach Prague within weeks of the revolution, offering protection to the eastern Kindred who survived.
The house reading has the old prince of Brno rise from the Spilberk to claim the city again, and find younger Kindred who never knew the prince existed.
Miners brought to Bucharest by the government beat students and opposition protesters.
Hunger strikes in Ulaanbaatar end one-party rule in Mongolia.
Property taken by the communists is handed back to former owners and the Church, and Brno's old families return.
Ostrava's deep coal mines begin to shut, one after another, and the black city starts to change.
Slovak nationalists march in Bratislava for an independent state.
The Afghan communist government outlasts the Soviet withdrawal and holds the cities.
Tokyo's stock market falls by a third, and Japan's lost decade begins.
Insurgency breaks out in the Kashmir valley, and Kashmiri Pandits flee.
The house reading has the ghosts of those shot at the Berlin Wall at last cross freely, and many move on.
The house reading has Prague's Hermetic chantry reopen its rooms near the castle after forty years in hiding.
An American-led coalition bombs Iraq for six weeks and drives its army from Kuwait in four days.
Soviet troops kill fourteen unarmed people defending the television tower in Vilnius.
Retreating Iraqi troops set hundreds of Kuwaiti oil wells on fire, and black smoke covers the Gulf for months.
Shia in the south and Kurds in the north rise against Saddam and are crushed; Kurds flee into the mountains.
A cyclone and storm surge kill some hundred and forty thousand in Bangladesh.
Slovenia and Croatia declare independence, and the Yugoslav army attacks.
Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines erupts and cools the world for two years.
The last Soviet troops leave Czechoslovakia after twenty-three years.
Hardliners try to depose Gorbachev; Yeltsin stands on a tank, and the coup collapses in three days.
The house reading has Moscow's Brujah split as the Soviet dream fails, and Baba Yaga's servants watch from the forests.
Vukovar falls after an eighty-seven-day siege, and Serb forces kill some two hundred wounded and prisoners.
The Soviet Union dissolves into fifteen states, and Gorbachev resigns.
Israel, its neighbours and the Palestinians meet face to face for the first time.
lk: The Difference Engineers and New Madrid

items.x: The house reading has the New World Order lose its grip on the Soviet apparatus, and Russian Traditions come out of hiding.
The house reading has the Black Spiral Dancers breed in the Chernobyl zone, and the Shadow Lords of Kiev raid them.
Czechs buy vouchers to own shares in state firms; clever funds gather them up and many vanish.
Bosnia's peoples arm as the Yugoslav wars spread south.
A Tamil Tiger suicide bomber kills Rajiv Gandhi at an election rally.
The Cambodian factions sign a peace, and the UN takes over the country for an election.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin courts send envoys back into Cambodia to reckon with what fed on the killing fields.
A coalition drives Iraq out of Kuwait in January and February 1991. Fits: No clash. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.
items.ref: Real history (1991).

items.x: Armenia and Azerbaijan fight openly over Nagorno-Karabakh.
The European Community becomes the European Union.
Bosnian Serb forces besiege Sarajevo; the siege lasts nearly four years.
Election results set Klaus's Czech right against Meciar's Slovak nationalists, and the two agree to divide the country.
Rioters set fire to a hostel for asylum seekers in Rostock while crowds cheer.
Hindu nationalists tear down the mosque at Ayodhya, and riots kill two thousand.
The communist government falls, and the mujahideen factions shell Kabul into ruins.
The house reading has Sarajevo's dead crowd its Shadowlands, and Spectres prowl the sniper alleys.
The house reading has old Tzimisce of the Balkans feed on the war and play the factions against each other.
Brno's theatres and the Janacek Opera draw audiences from Vienna once again.
South Korea and China establish relations.
The army cancels an election the Islamists would win, and a decade of killing follows.
The house reading has the Shadow Lords and Silver Fangs of the Balkans fight each other as well as the Wyrm.
The motorcycle Grand Prix returns to the Masaryk circuit, and two hundred thousand fans camp in the woods.

Yugoslavia breaks apart in war from 1991; Sarajevo is besieged from 1992 to 1996, and Srebrenica falls in July 1995. Margrave Konietzko directs the Garou against the Wyrm's forces in Serbia from the Sept of the Night Sky. Fits: No clash. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.
items.ref: Real history (1991 to 1995); Konietzko from Tribe Novel: Silent Striders & Black Furies p. 32; the timing is a house reading.

items.x: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully at midnight, and Moravia becomes part of the Czech Republic.
The house reading has the Kindred of Moravia and Slovakia redraw their domains, and the Bratislava prince loses havens east of the Morava.
A series of bombs kills over two hundred and fifty in Bombay.
Rabin and Arafat shake hands on the Oslo Accords, and Palestinian self-rule begins in Gaza and Jericho.
An earthquake in Maharashtra kills nearly ten thousand villagers asleep.
Yeltsin's tanks shell the parliament building in Moscow.
Croat artillery destroys the sixteenth-century bridge at Mostar.
Sarajevo digs a tunnel under the airport to bring in food and arms.
The house reading has the Kithain of Prague grow strong on the tourist crowds, and Banality fights back through the souvenir shops.
Slovakia becomes an independent state.
The Czech crown replaces the Czechoslovak one.
Hamas begins suicide bombings inside Israel.
The house reading has the Arcanum put its library onto computers and fear what the networks will reveal.
A mortar shell kills sixty-eight people in a Sarajevo market.
An Israeli settler shoots twenty-nine Muslims at prayer in Hebron.
North Korea's founder dies, and his son Kim Jong-il succeeds.
The ferry Estonia sinks in a storm in the Baltic; over eight hundred die.
Russia invades Chechnya, and Grozny is bombed to ruins.
Plague breaks out in Surat in India, and hundreds of thousands flee.
The tunnel under the Channel opens.
The house reading has the Garou of the Caucasus fight the Wyrm's servants in the Chechen ruins.
The MMM pyramid scheme collapses and ruins millions of Russians.
Israel and Jordan make peace.
Aum Shinrikyo releases sarin in a quiet street in Matsumoto, killing eight; police suspect the wrong man.
The house reading has a Sabbat pack test Brno's borders from Slovakia and leave three dead ghouls in the Svratka.
Kosice's old town is restored as Slovakia's second city finds its feet.
An earthquake destroys much of Kobe and kills over six thousand.
Aum Shinrikyo releases sarin on the Tokyo subway and kills thirteen.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin of Tokyo find Aum's leaders drawing on a power that was not theirs.
Bosnian Serb forces murder over eight thousand Bosniak men and boys at Srebrenica.
The house reading has the Srebrenica dead form a vast Circle that will not leave the valley.
Croatia retakes Krajina, and two hundred thousand Serbs flee.
An Israeli extremist shoots Prime Minister Rabin at a peace rally.
The Dayton agreement ends the Bosnian war.
The Czech Constitutional Court and supreme courts sit in Brno, which becomes the country's judicial capital.
Austria, Finland and Sweden join the European Union.
China takes the boy named Panchen Lama by the Dalai Lama and puts its own choice in his place.
Turkey's army fights the PKK in the south-east, and thousands of Kurdish villages are emptied.
The house reading has young changelings find Glamour in the early web, and the elders do not understand it.
Vineyards around Mikulov and the Palava hills open to tourists from Austria and beyond.
The Taliban take Kabul and hang the former president.
Britain admits a link between mad cow disease and a new human brain disease.
Israeli shells kill over a hundred refugees in a UN compound at Qana.
The house reading has the Kindred of London worry about the blood of the infected, and the Tremere study it.
Russia withdraws from Chechnya.
Serbs march through Belgrade's winter for three months against vote rigging.
The Czech Senate is elected for the first time.
The Taliban ban music, kites and girls' schooling in Kabul.
A truck bomb kills nineteen American airmen in Saudi Arabia.
The house reading has the Kuei-jin of Hong Kong bargain with mainland courts ahead of the handover.
lk: The sleeping dragons of Hong Kong
Necropolis Hong Kong and the Midnight Express

items.x: The archbishop's palace and gardens at Kromeriz are put on the World Heritage list two years later.
Pyramid schemes swallow the savings of half of Albania, the state collapses, and armouries are looted.
Deng Xiaoping, architect of China's opening, dies at ninety-two.
The reformer Mohammad Khatami wins Iran's presidency by a landslide.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China at midnight in the rain.
lk: The sleeping dragons of Hong Kong
Necropolis Hong Kong and the Midnight Express

items.x: The Thai baht collapses, and the crisis spreads to Indonesia, Korea and Malaysia.
The Morava and the Oder burst their banks; Olomouc, Otrokovice and Troubky drown, and fifty die in Moravia.
The house reading has the Garou of the Morava read the flood as the river's anger at the dams and drainage of the plain.
The house reading has the flood stir old drowned wraiths of the Morava, some dead since the Thirty Years War.
Diana, Princess of Wales, dies in a car crash in a Paris underpass.
Gunmen kill sixty-two people, most of them tourists, at the temple of Hatshepsut.
The house reading has the Reborn of Thebes swear to find whoever guided the killers to Hatshepsut's temple.
The house reading follows Vampire canon in spirit: the Gangrel begin to quit the Camarilla, and their justicar walks out.
The house reading has the Traditions' chantries in Europe prepare for a Technocratic push after the bloc's fall.
A party funding scandal and a currency crisis bring down Klaus's government.
South Korea takes an IMF rescue, and Koreans give gold to the state.
The house reading has the Olomouc flood uncover a sealed cellar, and a parish priest asks the Arcanum for help.
Czech hockey players win Olympic gold at Nagano, and Prague celebrates in the streets.
Northern Ireland's parties agree to share power.
India tests five nuclear bombs, and Pakistan answers within weeks.
Riots in Jakarta kill a thousand, many of them Chinese Indonesians, and Suharto resigns after thirty-two years.
Russia defaults on its debts, and the rouble loses two thirds of its value.
A car bomb kills twenty-nine in the Northern Irish town of Omagh.
Serbian forces fight the Kosovo Liberation Army and drive villagers from their homes.
The house reading follows Mage canon: the great Hermetic Horizon chantry of Doissetep tears itself apart in a war of its own masters.
The house reading has old secret police files on Brno's night-walkers sold to a private collector, and hunters learn of them.
Zeman's Social Democrats rule with Klaus's support.
Brno begins its fireworks festival on the Brno dam.
American missiles strike training camps in Afghanistan after embassy bombings.
America and Britain bomb Iraq for four days.
The house reading has the Tremere of Vienna fear a breach in their own pyramid, and the Prague chantry is purged.
The Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary join NATO.
NATO bombs Serbia for seventy-eight days to end the Kosovo campaign.
Some eight hundred thousand Kosovar Albanians flee to Albania and Macedonia.
India and Pakistan fight on the icy heights of Kargil.
The house reading follows canon: the Ravnos Antediluvian wakes in India, and Kuei-jin, Garou and Kindred fight it for a week of storms and madness.
The house reading follows canon: Technocratic satellites burn the Ravnos Antediluvian with sunlight focused from orbit.
The house reading follows Wraith canon: the Antediluvian's death sends the Sixth Great Maelstrom through the Underworld, and Stygia falls into ruin.
lk: Stygia and the other Dark Kingdoms

items.x: The house reading follows Mage canon: an Avatar Storm closes the Umbra to Mages, and Horizon Realms are cut off.
The house reading has the Ravnos of Prague go mad in a week, and the clan is nearly gone by summer's end.
A total eclipse crosses Europe from Cornwall to Romania; millions watch.
An earthquake in north-western Turkey kills seventeen thousand.
Bombs destroy apartment blocks in Moscow and other cities; Russia blames Chechens and goes to war again.
East Timor votes for independence, and militias backed by the army burn Dili.
An earthquake in central Taiwan kills over two thousand.
The house reading follows Hunter canon: ordinary people across Europe hear the Messengers and begin to see what walks among them.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The house reading follows Demon canon: the Maelstrom cracks the Abyss, and fallen angels slip into the bodies of the dying.
The house reading has the Maelstrom reach the Duat, and the Reborn of Egypt lose their path to the Underworld for a time.
Russia invades Chechnya again and levels Grozny.
Yeltsin resigns on the last day of the year and leaves Vladimir Putin as acting president.
The euro begins as a currency for banks and markets.
An Indian airliner is hijacked to Kandahar.
King Hussein of Jordan dies, and his son Abdullah succeeds.
Morocco's king dies and his son takes the throne.
The house reading has the Garou of India count their dead after the Week of Nightmares; whole septs are gone.
The house reading has the Maelstrom's echo shake the Dreaming, and the Kithain dream of a red star.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The house reading follows Werewolf canon: a red star appears in the Umbral sky, and the Garou fear the Apocalypse is near.
lk: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

items.x: The baroque plague column of Olomouc is added to the World Heritage list.
A dam at a gold mine in Romania breaks, and cyanide kills the fish of the Tisza and the Danube.
A Concorde crashes on take-off at Paris and kills a hundred and thirteen.
The Russian submarine Kursk sinks after an explosion; all a hundred and eighteen die.
A visit to the Temple Mount sets off the second intifada.
Protesters fight police at the IMF and World Bank meeting in Prague.
Crowds storm the parliament in Belgrade, and Milosevic gives up power.
The Czech nuclear plant at Temelin begins its first reactor, and Austria protests at the border.
The house reading has the Technocracy run Temelin's start quietly, while a Brno Verbena reads the land's unease.
The Czech lands are divided into regions, and Brno becomes the seat of the South Moravian Region.
