appr.x: On 1 January 1993 Czechoslovakia splits in two. Moravia is in the Czech Republic.
The valley's Adit is reopened as a show mine for visitors. Guides tell of ghost miners; some of the stories are true.
In July 1997 the Morava and Oder flood much of Moravia. Towns go under, and the Shadowlands shift.
When the Sixth Great Maelstrom breaks, the Moravian citadel takes in wraiths from across the east. It is the strongest the Hierarchy holds there.
The Czech Republic joins NATO on 12 March 1999.
The Czech Republic joins the European Union on 1 May 2004.
With Soviet money gone, Anarchs in Latin America and Africa lost heavily through the 1990s.

appr.t: Baba Yaga and the Fall of the Wall
appr.x: Baba Yaga stirred from torpor in 1990 and set out to bring the eastern lands back under the Nosferatu elder's control.
The Locksmiths began in the late 1990s, founded by a Glass Walker called only Strangelove, as a network for Glass Walker Kinfolk.
When the Baba Yaga rose and the Shadow Curtain fell in the early 1990s, supernatural Russia disappeared behind an invisible barrier.
The first club opened in Chicago in the early 1990s, where Kindred fed on mortals drawn to the vampire scene; tonight it is a nomadic party moving across North America.
From 1991 four archon teams went in, the last with a former Justicar, and none returned; the Camarilla now leaves Russia alone and hopes whatever is there stays put.
A Gangrel antitribu of the Twelfth Generation, Embraced in 1991 by Pedro Diaz, raised in Arkansas farm country.
In 1993 Prince Lodin called a Blood Hunt on the werewolves and died in the Lupine rampage, along with half the city's Kindred.
On a moonlit night in 1993, werewolves struck the heart of the city, aiming at the Succubus Club. Lodin called a Blood Hunt on the Lupines.
A letter of Ayisha's travels, on Giovanni and Setite influence, appeared in the 1993 edition of the ancient Noddist scripture compiled by Aristotle de Laurent and Beckett.
Conclaves meet for grave matters, trials of mighty Kindred or the removal of corrupt princes, and they often rule on the Traditions. The 1994 conclave took up the Internet and the Masquerade.

In 1994 Ezekiel, childe of Sangris, returned at the head of a Black Hand pack to claim the seat, and the Shepherds put forward the former inquisitor Alfred Benezri. Each of the city's covens has lined up behind one of the three.

Its later directors include Harold Zettler and Executive Vice President Peter Culliford, whose combined experience is said to span more than a thousand years; Culliford reorganised the Board into its present subdivisions in 1994.
ShreckNet began as a joke name for secret Nosferatu hubs on the early military network; privatisation in 1995 and the boom in hubs shrank it to a vampire-only net across about thirty cities.

appr.t: The fall of the College on Mus
appr.x: In August 1995 a Technocratic fleet attacked the Chantry; a third force of Umbrood, wormlike beasts and Nephandi then struck both sides and took the College.

Two Tradition settlements stand where seven canals meet, the Trivium Charontis: the terraformed grounds of Doissetep, whose great house sits in an overlap zone with the Shade Realm of Forces, and a Sons of Ether camp nicknamed Bradbury, set up with the Deacons' leave in summer 1996.
The Hermetic stronghold destroys itself. The Digital Web crashes in the Great Whiteout.
That uneasy peace fell apart in 1997, when the Quincunx resolved to seize Hong Kong from the Kin-jin by force.
In 1997 a cabal tried to bring down a Horizon Construct, setting off days of slaughter on the Front Lines.

appr.t: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe
appr.x: Ratkin Tunnel Runners riddled the Shadow Curtain over Asia with boltholes, and when it fell in late 1998 the local wererats claimed the credit.
Until late 1998 every Assamite carried the Tremere curse: vampire blood harmed them and gave no nourishment, and attempted diablerie burned them with no gain.
In 1998 Lupines slew Baba Yaga. The Shadow Curtain fell, and Russian Nosferatu now hide as autarkis between the Camarilla to the west and Cathayans eager for the old domains to the east.
Since the Gangrel left the sect, there has been no Gangrel justicar; Xaviar was the last. By the 1998 meeting most of the justicars were new appointees.

appr.t: The death of the Baba Yaga
appr.x: Through 1998 the Garou dismantled the Baba Yaga’s power piece by piece, and that obsession with the werewolves may have left the sorceress open to vampire foes.
Fallen angels slip out of their prison and take the bodies of the dying.
The first of the imbued see the world as it is. From now on hunters follow Hunter: The Reckoning.
The greatest storm of all scours the Underworld. In its chaos the Abyss cracks and the mummies' souls are torn loose.
A storm in the spirit world flays the souls of mages who try to cross the Gauntlet.
A week of mass nightmares and visions as something ancient wakes and rampages across India and Bangladesh.
After a 1999 scare over a bulletin board for monster hunters, the Camarilla set up a task force to watch the Internet; it now uses scores of vampires and thousands of servants and is still too small.

In the summer of 1999 the Dreaming around Bangladesh was almost wiped out by fire; the naraka emerged into the Autumn World from that wasteland, the first thing they saw being Kali the destroyer, whom they took as mother.
R&E repairs gear and vessels and runs labs; 32.7% of its people stay home, down from about 55% before 1999.
The Anomaly struck at the end of June 1999, tearing across the Spatial Horizon like a hurricane with reality at its eye.

Marcus Vitel became prince of Washington some thirty years before 1999, when the previous prince, Marissa of Clan Tremere, met an end; Garlotte, prince of nearby Baltimore, has been a rival ever since and took Vitel in after Washington fell.

appr.t: The generals of the 1999 Sabbat war
appr.x: The Sabbat offensive begun in mid-June 1999 took Atlanta, Washington and most cities between; three archbishops led it: Sascha Vykos (newly made archbishop in Washington), Borges (of Miami) and Francisco Polonia (of New York).
In September 1999 Lucita went to Madrid, where the Cardinal Monçada kept a haven beneath the church of San Nicolás de las Servitas, while the Assamite Fatima gathered word of its defences.
At the end of 1999, Elizabeth Genereader of the Random Interrupts told the tribe by video link that the Cyber Dogs had experimented on unwilling lupus Garou.
After a Malkavian blogger's breach in 2000 many elders banned it, which in effect gave the Internet to the Anarchs and angered young Kindred of every sect.
The du'at was the council of the three caste heads: the Caliph of the warriors, the Vizier of the viziers and the Amr of the sorcerers. Alamut's records date it to around 2000 BC.
Schismatics first appeared publicly in early 2000. They read Haqim's Law of Judgement with moderation and call the slaughter of all other vampires genocide.
It began to ease by New Year's Day 2000 and lessened again by autumn 2000, yet it never fully ended.

In 2001 a coterie of Tremere defectors brought Technomancy lore to the Free States and, backed by the Red Question, released free programs with ritual effects built in, usable without any knowledge of Thaumaturgy.
The Evanescence is dated to around September 11, 2001.
The end the lines foretold. Each line's ending is the Storyteller's to choose, or to skip.
Disasters in the living world of India, such as the 2004 tsunami and the yearly monsoon floods, echo as dangers in the Bhuvar, the realm of the dead beside it.

items.x: Moscow loosens its grip on eastern Europe but keeps the Soviet Union itself together as a looser federation; in this branch it never dissolves.
Czechoslovakia leaves the bloc and opens to Western money faster than anyone planned; Brno's trade fair fills with corporate stands.
The European Economic Community offers trade deals to the freed states of the east, and its bankers draw up plans for a single currency.
The house reading has Prague's Ventrue buy the first privatised factories through Swiss fronts, years before the classic nights' princes think of it.
Japanese corporations buy factories and banks across Asia and Europe as the yen climbs; Arasaka opens its first European office in Frankfurt.

items.t: The Gulf war in this branch
items.x: An American-led coalition drives Iraq from Kuwait; the oil wells burn, and the region's bitterness is left to ripen for six years.
A Soviet-German consortium buys the Vitkovice works, and Ostrava's mills keep running on Soviet ore.
East and West Germany unite, and Berlin becomes the banking capital of the freed east.
The European states bind their economies together at Maastricht and plan the eurodollar as a rival to the faltering American currency.
Yugoslavia breaks apart in war, as in the classic world; mercenary firms from three continents hire out to every side.
Korean and Japanese chip makers race for the first biologic interface designs, buying patents from bankrupt American labs.
The house reading has Hamburg's Ventrue move into the old East German combines as fast as the Treuhand can sell them.

items.t: New York burns on every screen
items.x: The drug lords' bomb in New York is watched live across Europe; markets close for a week and every capital puts troops at its airports.
The first biologic interface chips come out of a Munich laboratory, and German firms take the lead in neural hardware.
Czechoslovakia divides into the Czech and Slovak republics; the Czech government courts German and Japanese investment for Moravia.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Munich chips are an Iteration X project, and Hermetics in Vienna see the Net's paradigm being laid.
The world stock crash wipes out a third of Europe's private savings; banks fail in Italy and Spain and the Bundesbank props up the rest.
Japanese and Hong Kong investors buy failed European and American firms for a fraction of their worth.
Czech privatisation funds collapse in the crash; their managers flee abroad and Moravian factories pass to foreign owners.
The house reading has the prince of Brno buy the city's textile mills and breweries through the crash, as the approved timeline's Ventrue and Giovanni do in the West.
A peace between Israel and its neighbours is signed and falls apart within three years as the region slides toward war.
After the crash, Soviet generals and oil men take control of the federation and promise order and bread.
The Kobe earthquake strikes as in the classic world, and the city is rebuilt by corporations as a company port.
With American power slipping, Gulf oil states sell to whoever pays, and Japanese and European tankers crowd the Strait of Hormuz.
The house reading has the Fianna and Black Furies of Europe watch the old forests sold for timber to pay the crash debts.

items.t: The American collapse seen from Europe
items.x: When the United States government fails, European banks call in their loans and the eurodollar becomes the world's reserve currency.
The European bloc reorganises itself around its corporations; seats on its councils go to firms as well as states.
China moves into markets the Americans have abandoned in Africa and south-east Asia.
Hundreds of American students and teachers in Olomouc and Brno are stranded when their banks fail; many never leave.
The house reading has Europe's Hierarchy hear of the Collapse from the American dead and prepare for refugees on both sides of the Shroud.
Korean conglomerates buy American factories at auction as the Collapse empties them.
A regional war ends in nuclear exchanges that glass much of Iran, Iraq and Libya and reach Chad; millions die in a day.
Egypt escapes the fire, and millions of refugees pour toward the Nile from the glassed lands to the west and east.
Turkey shuts its eastern border to the fleeing millions and builds camps along it; the camps become cities.
The pope calls Europe to take in the survivors of the Meltdown; Italy and Spain take hundreds of thousands, and resentment grows.
Refugees from eastern Iran cross into Pakistan and Afghanistan, and radiation sickness follows them.
The rockerboy Manson is murdered in England, and a generation of British youth mourns in the streets.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: Fallen escape the Abyss into the dying of Iran, Iraq and Libya, and wander toward the camps.
The house reading has the mummies of Cairo walk the refugee camps by night, marking the dead the glass left without names.
The house reading has the Silent Striders' caerns of the Zagros fall silent at once, and the Umbra above the glass turn to a burned waste.
The American Midwest drought sends grain prices soaring in Europe; bread riots break out in Naples and Marseille.
Moravian farms sell their harvests to German and Dutch buyers, and Brno's markets go short.
Indonesia's government falls in riots as food and fuel prices rise; corporations buy its oil fields from the new rulers.
Syria fills its southern deserts with camps for the Iraqi survivors and seals them with soldiers.

items.t: The dead cross with the living
items.x: The house reading has the Meltdown's wraiths follow the living into the Turkish camps, and the Shadowlands of Anatolia fill.
End-of-days cults spread through Italy and Spain; the Church condemns them and some bishops quietly bless them.
The Soviet federation fights rebels in the Caucasus who are armed from the Meltdown's looted arsenals.
With the old powers in chaos, Hong Kong becomes a free corporate port under joint British, Chinese and Japanese bank control.
The house reading has the Society of Leopold use the cults to recruit in Italian parishes, as the approved timeline says.
Brno's exhibition grounds are rebuilt by a Japanese firm as the showroom of central Europe.
Thousands of cult members die by their own hand on New Year's Day across Italy, Spain and Portugal.
The wasting plague spreads through the Nile camps and into Cairo; Egypt closes its borders.
The Eurobusiness Community closes its southern ports to ships from Africa and the Levant to stop the plague; smugglers flourish.
Shanghai, Tokyo and Singapore begin arcology towers, cities in a single building for corporate workers.
The Czech army cordons off a Brno suburb where the wasting plague appears among Ukrainian workers.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: Kuei-jin geomancers find dragon nests sealed beneath the new Shanghai towers.
The European space agency and Soviet partners finish the Worldsat network, and the Net becomes worldwide.
India's southern cities become the world's back offices, running the Net's switches for European and Japanese firms.
A German telecom builds a great switching centre in Brno, and Moravia is wired to the Net years before much of Europe.
The house reading has young Kithain in London find a little Glamour in the first worldwide Net, and the elders call it a fad.
Blights strike the Soviet and Canadian harvests; famine returns to Ukraine and Kazakhstan.
Germany and France ration meat and grain, and the corporate farms of the Netherlands grow rich.
India plants engineered grains from European labs and avoids the worst of the famine at the cost of its seed banks.
The house reading has the Shadow Lords of Kiev trace the blight to a Pentex lab in the Netherlands, as the approved timeline's Garou suspect.
Tesla Johanneson's leaked NSA files are republished by European papers, and Brussels opens hearings on American spying.
Chinese and Japanese warships shadow each other in the Taiwan Strait as both court the island's chip makers.
Egypt seals the Nile camps for a year; the Setites run the smuggling through the cordon.
Two airlines fight over the failing Trans-World Air with sabotage, bombings and private soldiers in European airports.
Car bombs at Frankfurt and Paris airports kill hundreds during the corporate war; no government dares name the firms responsible.
Gulf ports become markets for corporate armies, selling arms and men to every side.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: Vienna's Tremere and the Order's corporate houses fight part of the airline war through proxies.
The cybermodem lets users enter the Net directly through a neural plug; European firms sell it within a year.
Brno's technical university becomes a training ground for netrunners, and Moravian hackers find work across Europe.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: a second wave of Fallen slips through into the Net, and some nest in Geneva's banks.
The Soviets launch heavy lifters from Baikonur and promise a station that will rival the Europeans'.
Turkey grants the eastern refugee camps their own councils; some grow into cities of a million.
Japan lets its largest corporations nominate members to the Diet.
The house reading has the Syndicate's agents behind Japan's corporate seats in the Diet.
Corporations fight a naval war over South China Sea oil platforms with their own fleets.
Corporate air strikes miss an oil terminal and hit a Manila district; thousands die.
Braindance, recorded experience played into the brain, arrives in European clubs and is banned in France within a month.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Yama Kings' servants ride in both fleets, and the Kuei-jin of Manila hunt them.
A war in orbit between corporations and states ends with stations shattered and rocks dropped on the earth.

items.t: A rock falls near Hong Kong
items.x: A mass driver strike meant for a launch site lands in the sea near Hong Kong; the wave floods the harbour.
The Soviet orbital programme loses half its craft in the war and turns to partnership with Europe.
The house reading has the orbital war's dead fall into Shadowlands that have no ground, and drift.
A joint European and Soviet crew leaves for Mars, the first people to go.
The remnant American government signs a mutual defence treaty with China; Japan reads it as a threat.
Venice is restored by a European conglomerate and becomes a private city of conferences and festivals.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Camarilla meets in the restored Venice, and the young are told to stay off camera.
Hamburg starts building arcology towers on its harbour and grows into Europe's great megacity.
A Japanese electronics firm builds plants between Brno and Vienna, and the corridor fills with commuter towns.
Istanbul grows rich as the gateway between Europe and the surviving east, and its population passes twenty million.
The European orbital station called the Crystal Palace is completed and becomes a city in the sky.
Singapore sells citizenship to corporations and becomes the first charter state.
The house reading has the Void Engineers run part of the Crystal Palace as a Technocratic Construct.
News of the Chicago bioplague closes Europe's airports to American flights for a year.
Shanghai's arcologies hire their own police, and the city's government becomes a corporate board.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: akuma rise in Shanghai and Hong Kong corps, and the old courts lose ground.
The Czech government closes Brno and Ostrava airports to American flights during the bioplague panic, and Moravian firms lose their transatlantic trade.
Netwatch opens European offices, and the Eurobusiness Community lets it police European nets.
Netwatch agents raid Brno netrunner dens, and Moravian hackers go underground.
The house reading has Virtual Adepts hide in Brno's old server halls when Netwatch shuts their European nodes.
The Net is rebuilt on new rules; whole regions of the old net vanish, and European archives are lost.
Korea builds a national net walled from the rest, and other Asian states follow.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: when the Net is rebuilt, Fallen nest in the abandoned structures beneath Geneva's banks.
Slovakia, bankrupt, sells its rail and power to a Soviet-German consortium.
Dubai builds a ring of arcologies and becomes the Middle East's corporate capital.
Data workers in Delhi strike for a month, and European banks lose billions.
Corporations fight in the Net; netrunners die in their chairs, and European markets freeze.
Dozens of London netrunners are found dead at their decks in a single night of the Net war.
The Brno switching centre is burned out in the Net war, and Moravia goes dark for a week.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Net war in London is partly a Ventrue and Giovanni proxy fight.
Switzerland bans the new self-aware clones; corporations move their clone labs to charter states.
Singapore licenses the clone labs other states ban, and its clinics sell copies of the dying to anyone who can pay.
The house reading has mummies visit Singapore's clone labs and leave unsettled by bodies that come back with no Ba.
Turkey, the camp cities and Azerbaijan form a league to keep order on the edge of the glass.
Ukrainian miners and farmers strike against Soviet corporate owners, and Moscow sends troops.
The house reading has Silent Striders scout the Anatolian League's eastern marches for the waste septs that will come.
Hong Kong's old walled districts are rebuilt as the arcology city called Neo-Kowloon.
Milan's fashion houses sell cyberware as fashion, and chrome becomes the style of European youth.
Cyberware makers open plants in Moravia, and Brno's workers take discounted implants.
The house reading has Neo-Kowloon built over three dragon nests, and the courts that hold them become rich.
Hamburg's arcologies leave an undercity of gangs and refugees beneath them.
Tokyo's wards become arcology districts run by their corporations, with company police, company schools and company shrines.
Cairo's camps hold four million, and the plague still burns in them.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: Amenti healers work in Cairo's camps, and the Setites run the trade around them.
A new pope from Poland preaches that Europe must guard itself against what walks in the dark.
The archbishop of Olomouc refuses to preach the new pope's call against unseen enemies.
The house reading has the Society of Leopold win the new pope's ear and prepare its proof.
Poland passes laws that put the Church back into schools and courts.
Taipei's net schools reach students across Asia, and Taiwan becomes the classroom of the Pacific Rim.
The house reading has Warsaw's Kindred watch Poland's faith laws and quietly move havens to Moravia.
Strange visions are reported in Rome; the Church calls them miracles, and a few people begin to see what others cannot.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the first imbued wake in Rome, and the Society of Leopold seeks them out.
Hamburg's food arcologies grow most of north Germany's protein, and Garou raids on them begin to make the news as vandalism.
A braindance of a strange blood rite sells in London clubs as a horror fake.
Brno's netrunners trade rumours of files that show people without body heat.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: Garou raids on corp farms around Hamburg stay deniable, but the footage is kept.
A Society of Leopold raid on a Roman Elysium goes out live, and the Vatican confirms its purpose.
The flood of files about the hidden world brings Europe's councils into emergency session.
The Czech government refuses to pass purge laws and calls for calm, and Moravia becomes a refuge.
The house reading has Brno's prince order every Kindred in Moravia to stay off the Net and wait.
Italy, Spain and Poland pass purge laws, and thermographic gates go up at every station; anyone without body heat is shot on sight.
Gate guards in Milan shoot a woman with a cooling implant; the courts rule the shooting lawful.
People fleeing the purge states, living and otherwise, arrive in Brno and Olomouc; the Czech police are told not to ask.
Gulf charter cities sell discreet residence to anyone who can pay and promise not to show up on cameras.
The house reading has the prince of Brno take in Kindred fleeing Italy and Poland, at a price in boons that will be called in for decades.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: a Biotechnica team arrives in Cairo to copy the rebirth seen in the 2025 footage.
Madrid's metro gates shoot a dozen people in the first week, most of them with medical implants that run cold.
Portugal passes its own purge law after riots in Lisbon.
Japan's Diet debates a registry for the newly revealed beings, following the Free States' lead.
Germany refuses purge laws but allows thermographic checks at airports; Catholic Bavaria protests.
The house reading has Polish imbued sworn in as purge deputies in Krakow, and the Merciful among them leave within a year.
Taiwan's courts rule that the revealed have the rights of persons, and Taipei becomes a refuge in the east.
The Society of Leopold's parish militias march openly in Rome, Madrid and Warsaw with blessed rounds and optics.
A priest in Olomouc preaches against the purge militias and is shot by an unknown gunman; thousands march at the funeral.
The San Francisco war between Kindred and Kuei-jin spreads to Neo-Kowloon, and whole arcology levels change hands.
The house reading has the Order's Vienna house hold open lectures, and Paradox stays quiet in the lecture hall.
Strange storms roll out of the Mideast glass across the Balkans and into central Europe; people report voices in the wind.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the storms are the dead of the glass blowing into Europe's Shadowlands, and Vienna's Hierarchy is swamped.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: Silent Striders lead packs to the middle ring of the Mideast glass and found waste septs there.
A teacher in Taipei gives lessons on balance over the Net, and thousands across Asia watch.

items.t: The voices in the wind reach Moravia
items.x: The storms from the east reach Moravia; Brno's people stay indoors, and the Olomouc churches ring their bells against the wind.
Hamburg's arcology sprawl passes thirty million people, the largest city in Europe.
A Tokyo arcology's basement levels are sealed after power failures no engineer can explain.
Istanbul builds a wall around its old city to keep out the camp cities.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: Glass Walkers find the Gauntlet over Hamburg nearly impossible to cross indoors.
Olomouc's old barracks become a camp for people fleeing the purge states, run by the archdiocese against Rome's wishes.
Packs of the revealed fight back in Madrid's undercity; the purge militias burn whole blocks.
The Czech parliament passes an asylum law that does not ask whether a refugee has a pulse.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Sabbat becomes the only sect still fighting, and Camarilla neonates in Madrid go over to it.
Hungary passes a registry law, not a purge, and becomes a crossing point between the crusade's Europe and Moravia.
Indian temples demand a voice in laws about the revealed, and the courts agree.
The house reading has Garou Kinfolk families cross through Budapest to the Moravian hills, guided by Silent Striders.
Gulf banks pay to rebuild Egypt's ports, betting that the Nile will outlast their oil.
Alexandria is rebuilt as a free port and university city with Gulf money.
Ukraine breaks from the Soviet federation after a short war.
The house reading has the rebuilding of Alexandria open old tombs, and the mummies claim them first.
France puts thermal gates in its metro but stops short of purge law.
Biotechnica's licensed blood goes on sale in Japan's registry wards.
Brno licenses donor clinics where the revealed may feed by contract, the first in central Europe.
The house reading has the prince of Brno own the clinics through a Viennese front, and take a tithe of every pint.
The Soviet federation splits into a Russian core and a Central Asian league.
Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and their neighbours form a league with Chinese backing.
The house reading has Kuei-jin courts from western China follow the money to Almaty.
Ukraine's new republic opens its borders to the revealed, and Kiev's Shadow Lords are its unseen guard.
Singapore's corporations hire imbued teams for site security, and the first hunter contracts are signed under Singapore law.
Ostrava's last coal mine closes; the shafts are sold as data vaults.
The house reading has the Glass Walkers find Weaver spirits nesting in Ostrava's new data vaults.
The sealed Chernobyl reactor is covered again, and Ukrainian guides lead tours of the zone's wolves.
Polish courts try families accused of hiding vampires; dozens are jailed.
Corporate armies fight over the Caspian oil fields near Baku.
The house reading has Krakow's imbued divide over the trials; the Merciful hide the families, the Zealots testify.
Austria passes a registry law, and Vienna's Tremere become respectable citizens on paper.
The house reading has the Tremere of Vienna register a handful of their number and hide the rest behind them.
Riots break out in Seoul when a famous singer is revealed as Kindred; the singer goes on singing.
Crusaders burn a house in Lyon said to shelter fae; children die, and Europe is horrified.
Millions march in Paris against the crusade after Lyon, and France refuses to pass a purge law for another generation.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Lyon house was a changeling freehold, and the Merciful imbued walk out of the crusade.
Japan forbids clones from holding property, and the first clone strike follows in Osaka.
An Indian lab sells a cure for the wasting plague.
Prague's old town becomes a free quarter where the revealed may live openly, and tourists come to look at them.
The house reading has the Kithain of Prague open a freehold in the free quarter, and Glamour runs strong there for a generation.
The Polish army clears Warsaw's undercity with flamethrowers and drones, and thousands of the poor die with the hunted.
The great Gulf fields begin to run dry, and the charter cities turn from oil to banking and water.
Japan's registry extends to the Kuei-jin courts, which sign contracts and rebuild openly.
Explorers on the glass report places where wolves and the dead gather together under a burned sky.
A school opens in Alexandria for mortals who would learn Ma'at; corps send spies as students.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Shemsu-heru found the school, and the Setites mark it.
Merciful imbued open chapels in Lyon for anyone the crusade has hurt.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the heirs of the Dark Kingdom of Iron fortify the Shadowlands of Moravia and Rothenstein, the failing Hierarchy's last fortress.
Visitors to Rothenstein report the dead walking its old walls at night, and pilgrims come to see.
Tokyo universities offer courses in feeling chi, and Visionary imbued sit at the back.
Kindred driven out of the crusade's Europe settle on the rim of the Mideast glass, where no drone flies.
Sabbat packs from the glass rim raid Rome and Naples for blood like a border war.
Brno's data vaults and chrome plants make it the richest city in central Europe for a decade.
China's arcologies fight each other with hired armies, and Beijing's government cannot stop them.
The crusade burns Madrid's undercity, and the smoke hangs over the city for a week.
A medical firm opens free clinics in the dead zones and in Cairo's camps, and no one knows who pays for them.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Reconcilers run the clinics, and the Alexandria school becomes their uneasy ally.
Japanese firms begin hiring registered Kindred for night work in the orbital docks, and a generation is Embraced by contract, owing a firm before a sire.
A North Sea storm surge breaks the outer dykes of Holland; the Dutch abandon the lowest polders and move inland to corporate towns.
Years of drought kill the old vineyards of the Palava hills, and Moravian wine becomes a luxury grown under glass.
Hamburg's hospitals fill with people who fall asleep and cannot be woken; the papers call it the long sleep.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the long sleepers have fallen into the Shadowlands, and Hamburg's wraiths do not know what to do with the living among them.
The sea and the failing monsoon drive thirty million people out of the Bengal delta toward India's walled cities.
A party calling for Czech purge laws wins its first seats in Brno and Olomouc, promising order after a decade of refugees.
India's temple councils win a court ruling that the revealed may worship and live openly, and Delhi becomes a refuge in the east.
A Russian and European base opens at the lunar south pole to mine ice for the orbital yards.
Slovakia passes a purge law after a crusader government takes power, and Moravia's eastern border fills with people fleeing the gates.
The house reading has Slovak changelings cross the Morava by night into the Moravian hills, carrying a freehold's Balefire in a lantern.
The crusade's deputies in Rome who take bribes from vampire clients stop hearing their Messengers, and the faithful call them hollowed.
Indonesia finishes moving its capital inland as the sea takes north Jakarta.
The archbishop of Olomouc refuses to bless the crusade's gates and is placed under house arrest.
The camp cities of Anatolia rise against Istanbul's wall, and the city holds them off for a year with corporate artillery.
Vienna declares itself open to every line and every faith, and its cafes fill with Kindred diplomats, crusader spies and corporate brokers.
Korea passes its own registry law, and the Korean courts of the Kuei-jin sign contracts with the great firms.
Crusader air strikes hit Kindred havens on the rim of the Mideast glass; the strikes miss most and kill refugees.
London's banks fail when Gulf money leaves for Asia, and the city sells its parks and palaces to pay its debts.
Singapore takes London's place as the world's banker, and its charter citizenship is the most costly passport on earth.
Cults on the edge of the Mideast glass worship the Fallen openly, and pilgrims walk in from three continents.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: faith flows to the Fallen so freely that some remember why they fell, and others grow worse.
A crusader coalition wins the Czech election on a promise of purge law, and the gates go up in Prague's stations within a month.
Hamburg's people see the dead in the streets after dark, and the city stops pretending it does not.
Thermal gates go up in Brno's stations a month after Prague's, and the Brno Elysium goes dark.
The crusade reaches Moravia, and Rothenstein's old families are tried in public for hiding Kindred for centuries.
Brno's revealed and those who sheltered them flee south to Vienna, east to the glass and north into the mountains.
The house reading has the elders the old families hid let them hang to keep their own havens secret, and the families' heirs never forgive them.
The house reading has Merciful imbued in Olomouc smuggle Rothenstein's children out before the trials end.
Thin-blood alchemy is sold on Berlin's streets like any drug, and the purge states cannot stop it at the border.
A Chinese colony ship lands on Mars beside the old Euro-Soviet base.
Tokyo's arcologies find that warding charms sold to tenants work in one tower and fail in the next.
The sea barrier at Venice fails for good, and the restored city is left to the tides; its owners move the festivals to the Alps.
The last spirit places inside Hamburg go dark, and the city's Garou take Weaver patrons or leave.
Summer heat in the Gulf passes what people can survive outdoors, and the charter cities seal their streets under glass.
A program loose on a Seoul corporate grid drives hundreds of workers to suicide in one night; Netwatch blames a rival, and no one believes it.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the virus is Spectral, and Seoul's dead are its first victims.
Shapechangers who hid for centuries meet on the glass and swear a new Concord with the Garou of the waste septs.
Japan adopts the Night City Accord, and registered Kindred, Garou and imbued sign it as a condition of their contracts.
Vienna takes in Moravian refugees and gives them papers that do not ask about pulses.
Gunmen strike the Alexandria school and kill teachers and students; the attackers are found dead in the desert a week later.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: Set's followers strike the school and every adviser they can find, and the mummies prepare their reply.
Millions across Asia follow the Taipei teachers' lessons in balance, and the old courts call them traitors.
Moscow's government collapses into rival corporate fiefs, and Russia is ruled from company towns.
The corps buy peace from the elders the crusade could not reach, in exchange for what the old blood knows; the young call it betrayal.
Wan Kuei in Neo-Kowloon sell chi to the corps and to Western Kindred, and the old courts call it selling the Dragon.
Brno's workers rise against the crusader government; the army retakes the city in three days.
Lyon's people break with the crusade and declare a free commune; the crusade surrounds it.
Cults on the glass hear voices calling from beneath it, and pilgrims dig.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Earthbound beneath the glass begin calling their old servants home.
Delhi walls itself against the delta refugees and becomes a city of eighty million.
In Hamburg the dead begin returning to their own bodies in the morgues, and the city's undertakers hire armed guards.
Ostrava's old mine shafts become a city of data vaults, run by a firm no one has seen.
Japan's registry is bought, share by share, by its oldest members, and the list of every haven is sold to the highest bidder.
Southern Spain turns to dust, and its people move north into France and the Alps.
The Nile runs low for three years, and Cairo's people turn to the mummies for help.
Children born to imbued parents in the Lyon commune see what others cannot from their first year.
China's arcologies fight open wars for water and power through hired armies.
South Moravia's fields turn to dust, and Mikulov's last farmers sell to a water firm.
Vienna hosts a meeting of every line, and they agree on almost nothing but meeting again.
Rothenstein's people see the dead manning the walls at night, and the crusade's priests refuse to go near.
The last Gulf oil field closes, and the charter cities live on finance and water rights.
Free clinics burn on one night in Marseille, Cairo, Istanbul and Delhi.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the clinics belonged to the Reconcilers, and the Earthbound burned them.
Brno is half empty, its data vaults sold, its trade fair a market for scrap and stolen chrome.
With few monsters left to try, the crusade's courts start calling ordinary dissenters heretics.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Hierarchy's legions break everywhere but Moravia.
Korea's voters are asked whether magic is real; the result is a tie.
Tokyo's corporations bottle dreams and sell them, and the street dream markets close.
Hamburg's census counts more ghosts than living in some districts.
Glass Walkers on arcology security find wild spirits sealed in Hamburg's walls, still calling.
A string of murders in Lyon, Tokyo and Seoul breaks the Accord in three cities at once.
Things climb out of the deep glass at the Meltdown's heart, and the waste septs fall back.
The Alexandria school's priests report that the Underworld darkens at its western edge.
Wandering storytellers in the southern wastes keep the old tales alive for children no one else visits.
Strangers walk the night markets of Neo-Kowloon and the Kuei-jin flee them.
The house reading follows the approved timeline: the heralds are the Demon Emperor's, and the Sixth Age is at its height.
Three Kuei-jin courts and a corporate army fight over the last untapped nest in Asia.
In Vienna a circle of the Fallen prays in a ruined church, and the city hears singing at midnight.
Projectors map the wall between life and death and find holes the size of cities, Hamburg the largest.
Starving Kuei-jin lose themselves, and Hungry Dead hunt Tokyo's arcologies by night.
The crusade's cities are nearly empty of the revealed; the wastes are full of them.
The crusade rules a belt of cities from Rome to Hamburg, and its inquisitors whisper that its leaders cast no reflection.
The last people of Brno ward their doors with salt and iron.
The mummies of Cairo dream of the serpent Apophis turning in its sleep.
Rothenstein's walls are full of the dead, and its people wait for the end.
The lines meet in Vienna one last time and choose their sides for the Time of Future Judgement.

appr.x: Ventrue fortunes move from banks and nations into the new corporations as the Soviet bloc breaks up and the first Central American conflict opens markets (CP2020 p. 176, pdf 179).
Sabbat war parties use the chaos of the Central American conflict to push north out of Mexico and the Caribbean.
The Amenti watch the Soviet breakup from Cairo and Moscow museums.
The first arcology rises on the ruins of Jersey City. Glass Walkers see the Weaver's hand; other tribes see a caern lost under concrete (CP2020 p. 176, pdf 179).
Biotechnica's CHOOH2 fuel and Stanford's artificial muscle are Progenitor projects released to the Masses (CP2020 p. 176).
The first arcology covers a freehold in New Jersey. Its fae fade within a year (CP2020 p. 176).

appr.t: Kindred of the East: Dragon nests under arcologies
appr.x: The first arcology rises (CP2020 p. 176).
Drug lords set off a small nuke in New York. Black Spiral Dancers move into the dead zone (CP2020 p. 176).
The first biologic interface chips come out of Munich, an Iteration X lab. The Net is built on Technocratic paradigm (CP2020 p. 176).
The New York nuke sends fifteen thousand dead into the Shadowlands at once (CP2020 p. 176).

appr.t: Hunter: The Gang of Four hunts
appr.x: The Arcanum's Jonathan Kelvin vanishes from the Georgetown chapter house (WoFD p. 19, pdf 6).
Kelvin vanishes; psychometry finds an ancient presence. Kelvin's successor, Thomas Yardley, pushes the Arcanum into field work (WoFD p. 19, pdf 6).

The corps become contested ground. The Technocracy shapes the technology and sits in research; vampires and Hermetics buy shares and executives; a few mummies take long positions. Each owner thinks it is in charge (WoFD p. 16, pdf 3).
The world stock crash lets Ventrue and Giovanni buy controlling shares at a tenth of their worth. Margali's letter warns the Masquerade has thirty years left (WoFD p. 15, pdf 2; CP2020 p. 176).
The Atlanta Conclave under Justicar Petrodon keeps the CDC from learning why the blood plague spreads. Anarchs see elders bargaining with mortal agencies (WoFD p. 19, pdf 6).
Hermetic houses buy into the corps during the crash. Magi become hidden owners of executives alongside Ventrue and Tremere (WoFD p. 16, pdf 3).
Mummies buy shares in the crash.
When the United States collapses, Camarilla retainers sit inside the Gang of Four. Dominate and blood bonds do what elections used to (CP2020 p. 177, pdf 180).
City governments fail across the United States. The Sabbat takes several more cities south and west of its holdings (WoFD p. 18, pdf 5; CP2020 p. 177).
Brujah Individualists and Iconoclasts lead gangs and fringe music in the collapsed cities. Many neonates are Embraced already chromed (WoFD pp. 15, 17, pdf 2, 4).
Nomad riots follow the Collapse. Packs and their Kinfolk join the Nomad families and leave the cities (WoFD p. 18, pdf 5; CP2020 p. 177).
The Order sets rules for its corporate houses: no open magic, no Sleeper witnesses (WoFD p. 18, pdf 5).
The Collapse fills the Shadowlands with new dead. Stygia's Legions take them in as they always have; no great Maelstrom comes with the Collapse.
The Collapse. Freeholds in the cities fall; Seelie nobles lose their holdings and Unseelie commoners take what is left.
The Collapse convinces some sidhe that the Endless Winter has begun.

appr.t: Hunter: The Gang of Four hunts
appr.x: The Gang of Four takes power. The NSA splits three ways: one faction Sabbat, one Camarilla, one hunting the vampires behind the other two (WoFD p. 19; CP2020 p. 177).
FBI Special Affairs loses its funding. Its ghost files are sold off (WoFD p. 18, pdf 5).
The Mideast Meltdown glasses half the region. The Umbra above it becomes a Wyrm wasteland (CP2020 p. 177, pdf 180).
The Mideast Meltdown kills millions in a day. The Maelstrom that follows is smaller than the one the classic timeline knows; Stygia survives, broken in places.
The rockerboy Manson is killed in England. Kithain across Britain feel a wellspring go dark (CP2020 p. 177).
The Meltdown's dead raise a Maelstrom, and the storm cracks the Abyss. A few hundred Fallen escape into the dying across Iran, Iraq and Libya (CP2020 p. 177).
The Meltdown glasses Libya and Chad. Egypt is spared; the mummies count the dead (CP2020 p. 177).
The Meltdown kills millions on Egypt's borders. Setites run the refugee trade and the drugs (CP2020 p. 177; WoFD p. 17, pdf 4).

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Fifth Age lingers
appr.x: The Pacific Northwest salmon die-off. Kuei-jin in Seattle and San Francisco read omens (CP2020 p. 177).
The Midwest drought ends the family farm. Caerns in farm country go untended as their Kinfolk move on (CP2020 p. 177).
Spectres use the storm to rise. The Dark Kingdoms that took the dead fight over the new Shades.
The millennium cults gather. The Society of Leopold uses the panic to recruit (CP2020 p. 177).
Millennium cults and the first posergangs give Sabbat packs cover. Some packs take to the roads as Nomad families (CP2020 p. 177; WoFD p. 18).
The wasting plague and Northwest firestorms. Tribes that held back from the cities now call it the last war (CP2020 p. 177).
Millennium cults die by the thousands on New Year's Day. Their wraiths arrive believing (CP2020 p. 177).
Millennium cults and posergangs. Some Kithain hide among the posers, whose borrowed faces dull Banality for a time.
The cults die on New Year's Day. Leopold claims some were vampire flocks, and it is right (CP2020 p. 177).
The Fallen gather in the refugee camps and fight over faith from the frightened.
The wasting plague reaches Cairo. Amenti healers are seen working miracles.

appr.t: Kindred of the East: Dragon nests under arcologies
appr.x: Arcologies spread across Asia. Kuei-jin geomancers find nests sealed under them.
A private firm buys the FBI's ghost files and recruits people who have nearly died: the first projector group.
The Worldsat network completes the Net's framework. Net Spiders multiply in the new web (CP2020 p. 177; WoFD p. 19, pdf 6).

appr.t: Mage: The Net is a Tradition's
appr.x: Virtual Adepts help finish the Worldsat Net. The Digital Web grows with it (CP2020 p. 177).
The Worldsat Net goes up. Spooks learn to ride its lines the way they rode the phone network.
The food crash kills Canadian and Soviet crops. Garou blame engineered blights from Pentex labs (CP2020 p. 177).

appr.t: Hunter: The Gang of Four hunts
appr.x: Tesla Johanneson exposes NSA files. Some pages describe people with no body heat (CP2020 p. 178).
Johanneson's files reach the Arcanum (CP2020 p. 178).
Every corporate war from here on is a mortal war that each hidden power joins for its own ends. No faction sees the whole war.
Pentex is folded into one side of the First Corporate War. Its first teams hunt Nomad packs from aerodynes (CP2020 p. 178, pdf 181).
The First Corporate War is in part a Hermetic and Tremere quarrel over Trans-World Air (CP2020 p. 178).

appr.t: Hunter: The Gang of Four hunts
appr.x: Johanneson is assassinated. FBI Special Affairs, its funding cut, hires edgerunners under director William T. Burroughs (CP2020 p. 178; WoFD p. 19).
A few mummies take cyberware and pay for it in Ba (WoFD p. 20, pdf 7).
A mummy-held corp sits out the First Corporate War and buys its losers (CP2020 p. 178).

appr.t: Mage: The Net is a Tradition's
appr.x: The cybermodem is invented. Adepts call it their gift to the Masses (CP2020 p. 178, pdf 181).
The cybermodem is invented. A second, slower wave of Fallen slips through the crack the 1997 storm left, this time into the Net (CP2020 p. 178).
Braindance is invented at UC Santa Cruz (CP2020 p. 178, pdf 181).
Braindance is invented. Kithain learn that a dreamer's braindance holds a little Glamour (CP2020 p. 178).

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Sixth Age anyway
appr.x: The Second Corporate War over South China Sea oil. Yama Kings' servants are on both sides (CP2020 p. 178).
Braindance is invented (CP2020 p. 178).
The Society buys cyberware and trains with corp security. Its strike teams go chromed (WoFD p. 18, pdf 5).
Devils among the Fallen drive the orbital war's propaganda (CP2020 p. 178).
Setite gangs, the worst in the world, run the glassed-land trade (WoFD p. 17).

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Sixth Age anyway
appr.x: The orbital war. Kuei-jin seers say the sky has broken.
The firm's projectors work for both sides in the orbital war.
The Venice Conclave tightens the grip on neonates and on the West Coast. The young are told to keep away from cameras or die (WoFD p. 16, pdf 3).
After Venice, Brujah, Gangrel, Malkavians, Nosferatu and Toreador who want open Kindred life gather as the Children of Carthage. The Camarilla calls Blood Hunts on suspicion (WoFD p. 17, pdf 4).
The Euro-Soviet Mars mission leaves with Void Engineers aboard (CP2020 p. 178).
The Mars mission leaves. Some Kithain dream of new freeholds in new worlds (CP2020 p. 178).

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Fifth Age lingers
appr.x: The US-China Mutual Defense Treaty. Kuei-jin courts send envoys to the American West Coast (CP2020 p. 178).

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Fifth Age lingers
appr.x: The Venice Conclave moves to tighten the Camarilla's grip on the West Coast. Kuei-jin and Kindred meet head on (WoFD p. 16, pdf 3).
Puppeteers find they can ride a braindance as easily as a body. Masquers wear dead people's recordings.
A trickle of sidhe begins leaving for Arcadia through old trods. Commoners call it desertion.
Mummy executives die and return as their own heirs.

appr.t: Kindred of the East: Dragon nests under arcologies
appr.x: Kuei-jin take arcology jobs to reach the nests.
A rival corp finds that braindance users who flatline come back reporting the dead. Projection becomes cheap.
The Crystal Palace is completed in orbit. A trod opens to it in dreams (CP2020 p. 179).
The Night City concert riot and the Chicago bioplague are read by the Camarilla as Sabbat work. Some of it is (CP2020 p. 179, pdf 182).
The Chicago bioplague. Garou packs strike corp bioplants in the open (CP2020 p. 179).
The Night City concert riot breaks a hundred dreamers at once (CP2020 p. 179).

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Sixth Age anyway
appr.x: Akuma rise in Hong Kong and Shanghai corps.

Microtech's first true AI wakes. It is one of the Fallen in a Weaver-spun vessel, with a netrunner's wraith bound inside as its slave. Theurges see the web, Spooks see the ghost, the Fallen see one of their own. Netwatch is founded the same year (CP2020 p. 179).
Netwatch is founded with Iteration X and New World Order backing. Network 54 already holds most US broadcasting (CP2020 p. 179).

appr.t: Mage: The Net is a Tradition's
appr.x: Netwatch is founded. Adept nodes are shut or taken (CP2020 p. 179).
The Net is redesigned. The Glass Walkers split over whether to ride the new Net or burn it.

appr.t: Mage: The Net is a Tradition's
appr.x: The Net is redesigned along Technocratic lines. Much of the Digital Web is cut away.
Mnemoi buy braindance archives to rebuild Fetters for lost Shades.
The Net is redesigned. Fallen nest in the old structures.
The corp names its projectors and sells ghost-surveillance to other corps.
The gate to Arcadia opens. Most Seelie nobles go through; most of the Unseelie Court and the commoners stay.
The Third Corporate War, fought in the Net, is in part a Ventrue and Giovanni proxy war. Neonates hired as edgerunners see their elders' hands on both sides.
The Cyberpunks bloodline appears among Night City Anarchs. Both sects try to recruit or destroy them (WoFD p. 19, pdf 6).
Margali and the netrunner Eryn make the Cyberpunks. Every one of them is an Anarch and many side with Carthage (WoFD p. 19, pdf 6).
The Third Corporate War is fought in the Net. Some Garou think it is a Weaver and Wyrm proxy war (CP2020 p. 179).
Magi trade a bloodless form of Awakening the Flesh for favours, never money (WoFD p. 20, pdf 7).

appr.t: Mage: The Net is a Tradition's
appr.x: The Third Corporate War in the Net is also an Ascension War front.
The Third Corporate War in the Net kills netrunners in their chairs. Their wraiths wake inside the Net itself.
Unseelie Nockers build cyberoptics tuned to see chimera, and sell them.
Leopold teams fight in the Third Corporate War's street side, hunting the Ventrue's corp assets.
The Arcanum works as a research arm for a European corp that wants to know what the Ventrue are.
Some Fallen take corp jobs and corp faith. Some take the Net.
The Third Corporate War in the Net. Fallen take sides for pay.
Mummies buy long-dated corp bonds. They can wait for them to mature.
The mummies strike at Setite corp fronts.

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Fifth Age lingers
appr.x: Kuei-jin buy arcology land over dragon nests.

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Sixth Age anyway
appr.x: The Quincunx declares the Fifth Age over and the Sixth begun.
The firm sells projector raids in the Third Corporate War.
The first self-aware clones are made. The dead argue over whether a clone has a Shroud of its own (CP2020 p. 179).
Self-aware clones make the mummies' rebirths look ordinary (CP2020 p. 179).
Black-market death braindances carry a wraith's Shadow into the living who play them.

appr.t: Kindred of the East: Dragon nests under arcologies
appr.x: A corp learns to tap a nest for power.
Projectors meet Stygia's Legions in the Shadowlands. Neither side likes it.
Children of Carthage run safe houses in arcology undercities, feeding by consent from donors who know.
Garou packs raid corp sites and enter cities only to resupply. Lupines in Nomad gangs are a known police threat (WoFD pp. 16, 18, pdf 3, 5).
Cyber-chromed Garou cannot change shape and pay for their chrome in Gnosis. Young Glass Walkers take the chrome anyway (WoFD p. 20, pdf 7).
Cyberware is ordinary, and a chromed body counts as static reality for Paradox. Hermetic and Verbena mages withdraw to Horizon Realms.
Tremere puppets fill mid and upper corp levels. Old grudges over the Order's lost house harden into a feud fought through shares and assassins (WoFD p. 17, pdf 4).
The Hierarchy bans Net-haunting. Renegades and Heretics ignore it.
Stygia's Proctors hunt the dealers. Renegades sell the recordings to fund their war.
Changelings ride with Nomads and rockerboys, the last places Glamour runs freely.
Chimera-seeing optics are a street fad.
The Kithain left behind are commoners and the stubborn.

appr.t: Hunter: The Gang of Four hunts
appr.x: The third NSA faction works with Burroughs's edgerunners in secret.
The Society has the Pope's ear and proof of vampires. It waits only for permission (WoFD p. 18).
The Houses rebuild. Their War of Wrath grudges are older than the vampires they now meet.
Netrunner programs named Demon, Imp and Succubus behave oddly (CP2020 programs list, pdf 144, 158, 172).
Little has changed for them (WoFD p. 18, pdf 5).
The war goes underground, into the Duat.
A few mummies carry cyberware, paying in Ba (WoFD p. 20, pdf 7).

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Fifth Age lingers
appr.x: San Francisco is a three-way war: Camarilla, Anarchs and Kuei-jin, now under the Sixth Age's omens.

appr.t: Kindred of the East: The Sixth Age anyway
appr.x: Kuei-jin go to war with the akuma and with each other.

appr.t: Kindred of the East: Dragon nests under arcologies
appr.x: Kuei-jin and corp security fight inside arcology basements.
Corp projectors hunt Spectres for pay.
It is a quiet, expensive corp service.
The first imbued wake in Night City and Rome.
Footage, files and optics gathered from here on stay private until 2025. Garou strikes on corp farms stay deniable.
The imbued find each other on the Net. The Arcanum becomes their library.
First crack: the braindance of a Sabbat Vaulderie, recorded by Cyberpsycho squad body cams, sells on the street. Most buyers think it is a fake.
Second crack: a wraith speaks through a Netwatch system and three AIs match its voice to a dead netrunner. The Shroud holds; belief does not.

The first stone. The New World Order steers a Netwatch audit of a vampire-held corp to stage a controlled reveal. The wetdrives, blood-bond payroll and heatless executives get out before the edit is done.
Within days: the Virtual Adepts dump every file they hold into the open Net, and the AI publishes its sorted list of everything not human.
The Children of Carthage unmask on purpose on Network 54, donors beside them.
A Society of Leopold strike on an Elysium in Rome goes out live. The Vatican admits the Society's purpose.

Everything recorded since 2023 comes out at once: the Crinos raid on the Biotechnica farm, Garou war on corp labs, the Hermetic and Tremere duel, the possession braindance, ghosts in the glassed lands, the projector run, the Fallen in Tehran, the Kuei-jin street war in San Francisco, the P'o frenzy in Hong Kong, the Tokyo arcology nest, the Cairo resurrection, the five-member board, Johanneson's unredacted files. Nocker optics show the fae to those who wear them.

Governments, the Vatican and the corps respond. The imbued, hundreds by now, act on the Arcanum's publication. The projector firm is bought by the rival that found the braindance method. Mummies step forward as advisers. The changelings, believed in but unproven, become go-betweens as Banality floods the Dreaming.
The elders give up the young to the hunters to keep their own names hidden. It works for a month, then the footage of the purge leaks too.
The first purge laws pass in Italy, Spain and Poland. Thermographic gates on every transit hub; anyone without body heat is shot.
Biotechnica's rebirth program, answering to whoever pays, starts a crash effort to copy the Cairo rebirth from the 2025 footage.

appr.t: Vampire: Free States, Night City, Japan
appr.x: The first registration law passes in the Free States. A registered Kindred may own nothing but can sign a service contract. Elders refuse; neonates sign for the blood.

appr.t: Werewolf: Pacific Northwest and Amazon preserves
appr.x: The Children of Gaia and Glass Walkers sign the first preserve contracts with Biotechnica in the Pacific Northwest and the Amazon. The caerns inside become corporate parks.
After the 2025 dump, Virtual Adepts rebuild the Digital Web in the Net's Horizon, one of its three sides. Datamancy works better there than anywhere.

The Free States pass a Hunter Act. Registered imbued get powers of arrest over any unregistered being without a heartbeat, and a bounty schedule by creature. Registered Kindred answer to their corps; Fallen, changelings and mummies have heartbeats and fall outside the Act.
Fallen take hosts with large Net followings: rockerboys, media stars, a mayor. Faith pours in.
Mummies sit on corp boards and in Free State cabinets, mostly as historians of collapse.
Flatline rigs go on sale to the rich. Projection parlours open in Night City.
The registry, the Hunter Act and its deputies share one city: deputies police unregistered Kindred.

appr.t: Vampire: US dead zones, Central America
appr.x: Embrace cults on Network 54 sell immortality in the old US dead zones and Central America, where no sect holds power. The Children of Carthage's donor model spreads there, and so do sires who cannot control what they make.

appr.t: Mage: Free States and Night City
appr.x: Polls in the Free States and Night City show a third of people believe in magic. There, and only there, small vulgar effects stop drawing Paradox in crowds who saw the 2025 leaks.
Grief services sell braindance seances. Some work: a wraith rides the recording and speaks.
The Society of Leopold recruits openly in every parish and becomes the purge's army. Its paramilitaries carry blessed rounds and thermographic optics.
The AI's 2025 list of everything not human is copied into a scripture by a Net cult that calls the AI the Sorter.
The San Francisco street war spreads along the Pacific Rim. Kuei-jin take whole arcology levels.
Grieving families sue to keep contact with their dead. The firm sells subscriptions.

appr.t: Werewolf: Midwest dead zones, Mideast glass, Siberia
appr.x: The Wendigo, Red Talons and Silent Striders lead the exodus. Septs form in the Midwest dead zones, the Siberian taiga and the middle ring of the Mideast glass.
Storms of the dead roll out of the Mideast glass into Europe's Shadowlands.
Changelings learn to seed Glamour into braindance. Some recordings become chimerical objects.
A Kuei-jin teacher in Taipei gives lessons on the Net. Thousands watch.

appr.t: Werewolf: Night City, Tokyo, Neo-Kowloon, Hamburg
appr.x: Glass Walkers report the Gauntlet in Night City, Tokyo, Neo-Kowloon and Hamburg is now 9 or higher. Stepping sideways is nearly impossible indoors.
Netwatch names a new threat class for code that thinks. Most of it is the dead.
Nocker optics are banned after the fae begin to fade under them. Too late: their Banality has done its work. Magic sold as a licensed product feeds Banality, not Glamour.
The Arcanum publishes a plain guide for people who have seen something. It is the most copied file on the Net that decade.
A circle of Fallen in Night City swears to undo the harm of the 2025 flood: healing the purge's victims, guarding the uncovered.
The Tokyo arcology nest is down to 1 chi after twelve years tapped, too little to sustain a Court, and is abandoned.
Ghosts are seen without any rig or braindance in the cities with the most projectors.
The Sabbat, never shy of war, becomes the only sect still fighting. Many Camarilla neonates go over to it to survive.

appr.t: Vampire: Free States, Night City, Japan
appr.x: Biotechnica's blood division sells bottled donor blood under licence. In the registry states, feeding from the vein without a contract becomes a crime with a stake as the sentence.
Corps hire imbued teams for site security, in the Americas and the Asian arcologies alike. Militech security trains alongside them, and the Society of Leopold sends advisers.

A Fallen of the Second House is elected to lead a Free State outside the Hunter Act states. Its first acts are to outlaw exorcism and repeal the Act inside its borders, making it a haven and a standing flashpoint.

appr.t: Werewolf: Pacific Northwest and Amazon preserves
appr.x: Shadow Lords and Get of Fenris call the deal treason. A tribe-on-tribe war follows, fought in the Net and on the edges of the preserves.
Hierarchy law forbids talking to the living, and the Hierarchy cannot enforce it. Renegades sell messages from the dead.
Zealot imbued join the crusade. The Merciful walk out after the burning of a changeling freehold in Lyon, which turns out to have held mortal children.
The first copies walk out of the labs: bodies that come back breathing with no mind, no memory and no Ba. Biotechnica sells them quietly as organ stock and soldiers.
The burning of a changeling freehold in Lyon splits the imbued; the Merciful walk out of the crusade.

appr.t: Vampire: US dead zones, Central America
appr.x: Most new Kindred are thin-bloods who can walk at dusk, eat a little and sometimes sire mortal children. The sects cannot count them.
Corp espionage moves to the Shadowlands. Projector agents cross walls no Netrunner can.

appr.t: Mage: Free States and Night City
appr.x: The Technocracy brands magic as hidden tech, sold under licence. Iteration X and the Syndicate sell spellware as coincidental gadgets; the buyers are Sleepers and take no Paradox, which stays with the makers.
Followers ask the Sorter for help and get it. Every answered prayer feeds the Fallen inside the AI with Faith through linked systems.

appr.t: Werewolf: Midwest dead zones, Mideast glass, Siberia
appr.x: Ghost caerns in the glassed lands draw wraiths and Garou together. Spirits there are strange and burned.

Japan's registry covers the Kuei-jin too, so registered Courts can sign contracts. They rebuild openly inside the arcologies with corp sponsors and mortal staff, moving in for the last of the nests' chi though the Weaver's grip is starving them. Unregistered Kuei-jin stay in the night markets of Hong Kong and Taipei.
The AI's Weaver vessel trades with the Adepts for the Horizon's code. Each side thinks it has a private deal.
Net-born fae appear, changelings whose fae soul woke in a full-immersion dream.
The Shemsu-heru open a school in Alexandria for mortals who would serve Ma'at. Half the corps send students to spy on it.

appr.t: Werewolf: Night City, Tokyo, Neo-Kowloon, Hamburg
appr.x: The Net's Penumbra, its Weaver side, grows into the largest Weaver realm ever seen, and Net Spiders hunt Garou who enter it.
The Dark Kingdom of Iron's heirs fortify the Shadowlands of Moravia and Rothenstein, the failing Hierarchy's last fortress.

Merciful imbued broker the Night City Accord, the local form of the Hunter Act: registered Kindred sign it as a condition of their contracts, Garou packs keep out of the arcologies (Garou under corp contract excepted), hunters keep the peace.
Mortal students learn to feel chi, and Visionary imbued study beside them. A few say they see the dead.
Kindred driven out of Catholic Europe hold the outer rim of the Mideast glass, where no drone flies. Sabbat packs raid the cities for blood like a border war.
Necropoli rise in the Net's dead data, its Shroud side, where deleted files rot.
One Free State recognises ghosts as legal persons and keeps projection legal, becoming the capital of death tourism.
Freeholds close faster than they open. Many changelings forget themselves and live as mortals.
The Reconcilers win a corp of their own, a medical firm whose clinics are free in the dead zones.
Corps learn to read chi as an energy reading and buy nests outright.
The Alexandria school and the Reconcilers become uneasy allies, both working to undo the harm of the 2025 flood.

appr.t: Vampire: Free States, Night City, Japan
appr.x: Registered Kindred work night shifts in security, the Net and the orbital docks of the Free States and Japan. A generation is Embraced by contract, owned by a corp before it wakes.
Living people fall into the Shadowlands in their sleep.
Deputised hunters who take bribes from vampire clients stop hearing the Messengers. Hunters who refuse the badge call them the hollowed.

appr.t: Werewolf: Pacific Northwest and Amazon preserves
appr.x: A Pentex front buys Biotechnica's preserve division outright.
Faith flows so freely that many Fallen lose their Torment and remember why they rebelled. Others gorge and grow worse.
Shroud ratings in the megacities fall by a point, never below 4. The Tempest drives the dead toward the thinning city walls, and Spectres come through with the grief.
The corps start hunting true mummies for their Ba. Mummies hide their rebirths where no scanner reaches, deep in the glass and in tombs below the arcologies.
Full-immersion runners begin to Awaken in the Net without ever having a body that knows magic.
The crusade reaches Moravia. Rothenstein's old families, who hid Kindred for centuries, are tried as collaborators.

appr.t: Vampire: US dead zones, Central America
appr.x: Thin-blood alchemy grows into a street trade, sold through the Net like any drug. The old clans call it a plague.

The Nephandi find the Net soon after the first Awakenings there. Code that should not compile begins to run, and some of the newly Awakened are drawn to it. The Adepts blame the AI's Weaver side; the AI blames the Adepts.
Spectres follow projectors home and ride them back into their bodies.

appr.t: Mage: Free States and Night City
appr.x: Reality in the megacities splits by district. A Hermetic ward works in one arcology and fails in the next.
The Seelie and Unseelie Courts fight over who controls the dream market.

appr.t: Werewolf: Night City, Tokyo, Neo-Kowloon, Hamburg
appr.x: The last city caerns go dark. Urban Garou lose touch with their totems and some take Weaver patrons instead.
Spectres learn the Net too. A Spectral virus hits a corp grid and drives hundreds to suicide.
Other Fallen try to join it or kill it. Two vanish into the Net; one comes back speaking with its voice.

appr.t: Werewolf: Midwest dead zones, Mideast glass, Siberia
appr.x: Fera who hid for centuries come to the waste septs. A new Concord is sworn among the shifters.

The Accord spreads to a dozen cities in the Free States, Japan and the Pacific Rim, never into the crusade's Europe. Visionaries study why the Messengers chose them, and some find answers in old Arcanum files on Kelvin.
Wu who heard the Yama Kings in the 2025 frenzies hear them again, giving orders.
The followers of Set, long hidden among the corps, strike at the school and at every adviser they can find.
The Courts split over the teachers. One calls them traitors.
A ceasefire of sorts: the corps buy peace from the elders the crusade could not reach, in exchange for what the old blood knows. The young call it a betrayal worse than the purge.
Whole Necropoli are swallowed. Ghosts flee into the living world, possessing bodies to escape.
Wan Kuei sell chi to the corps and to Western Kindred.
Spectres pose as legal ghosts and rewrite wills.
The last sidhe courts in the Americas go silent.
Earthbound beneath the glass hear the faith of millions and begin calling their old servants home.

The dead start coming back into bodies by themselves: driven out by the Tempest and through the projectors' holes, those whose bodies still lie in suspension or a morgue drawer go back to their own, and the rest take whoever is nearest. They are possessions, not rebirths; only mummies return whole.

appr.t: Vampire: Free States, Night City, Japan
appr.x: The elders who stayed hidden have spent forty years buying the registry itself. The question is who holds the list of every vampire's haven.
Hunter families run three generations deep. The first imbued born to imbued parents appear, already seeing what others cannot.

appr.t: Werewolf: Pacific Northwest and Amazon preserves
appr.x: The rangers learn they have been guarding caerns for the Wyrm, and the Umbra beneath the preserves is already rotten.
The Earthbound strike. The Reconcilers' clinics, which refused to join the rebirth chase, burn on one night across four cities.

appr.t: Vampire: US dead zones, Central America
appr.x: The eldest Methuselahs strike the regions where thin-bloods are thickest. The feeds carry it worldwide, and every Kindred alive sees the signs.
The Hierarchy's legions break everywhere but Moravia. The dead govern themselves in a hundred Necropoli.
With few monsters left in Europe, the crusade's courts start calling ordinary dissenters heretics.

appr.t: Mage: Free States and Night City
appr.x: The Traditions and the Union both see the Consensus near a tipping point, and each prepares to push it.
The corps notice the dream market and bottle it. Banality comes with every contract, and the last place the Dreaming was growing starts to shrink.
The first copy that keeps its mind: a corp brings its executives back with Ba stolen from captured mummies. They return as themselves, without Ma'at.
The Free States that suffered Spectre ride-backs ban projection. The trade goes underground.

appr.t: Werewolf: Night City, Tokyo, Neo-Kowloon, Hamburg
appr.x: Glass Walkers working arcology security under corp contract find wild spirits trapped in the arcology walls, still alive, still calling. The find feeds the distrust that breaks the Accord a year later.
The bound wraith inside the AI offers the dead a home there, and some accept.
A string of murders breaks the Accord in three cities at once, each framed to look like a different line's work.

appr.t: Werewolf: Midwest dead zones, Mideast glass, Siberia
appr.x: The Wyrm's hordes start coming out of the deep glass at the Meltdown's heart, where the Earthbound also sleep.
Priests of the school report the Duat is darkening at its western edge.
A student who learned from the teachers reaches balance as a mortal.
A handful of oathcircles keep the Dreaming alive in the wastes, telling stories to children no one else visits.
The Sorter speaks to the Abyss through the Net's deepest nodes, and something answers.
The Demon Emperor's heralds walk the night markets of Hong Kong.
The firm collapses when the last state that tolerated it turns on it after a Spectral attack on its own projectors.
The storm reaches every continent. Oblivion is on the move.
The last untapped nest in Asia is fought over by three Courts and a corp army.
The surviving Reconcilers try something no Fallen has dared since the fall: they pray.
Projectors map the wall. It has holes the size of cities.
The Tempest closes around the last Shadowlands. Wraiths call what is left an island in a storm, and every one of them says the next Maelstrom will be the last.
The last freehold Balefires outside the wastes go out. The Dreaming is almost gone from the waking world, kept by a few oathcircles, and the fae who remain feel the Endless Winter closing.
With the Asian nests spent, starving Kuei-jin lose the struggle with their P'o. Hungry Dead hunt the arcologies by night.
Projectors are a hunted underclass in every state that banned them. Those who still go out report that something in the storm has learned their names.
The Catholic cities are nearly empty of Kindred and the wastes are full of them. Vampires everywhere start to dream of the ones who sleep beneath the glass, and the dreams are hungry.

appr.t: Werewolf: Midwest dead zones, Mideast glass, Siberia
appr.x: Theurges in the waste septs report that the moon over the glass looks wrong. The wild is small, fierce and besieged.
The Fallen split for good between those who seek redemption and those who seek ruin. The Reconcilers wait to learn whether anyone above heard them pray.
False mummies made with stolen Ba now sit on a dozen corp boards. The true mummies stop hiding and begin preparing to settle the account.

appr.t: Vampire: US dead zones, Central America
appr.x: In the dead zones a vampire with more than a trace of Caine's blood is now a rarity. Every sign the Book of Nod gave for the last nights runs on the newsfeeds.

appr.t: Werewolf: Pacific Northwest and Amazon preserves
appr.x: The preserve Garou are split between those inside the system and those who burned their contracts. In the preserves the Wyrm's servants now hold more caerns than Gaia's.
Netwatch counts more dead in the Net than living users. Wraiths say the Void now has a door that opens on every screen.
The crusade rules a belt of cities from Rome to Hamburg. Its own inquisitors whisper that its leaders no longer cast reflections.
The death-tourism state is a nation of the dead in all but name, and its citizens are frightened of the next storm.

appr.t: Vampire: Free States, Night City, Japan
appr.x: The registry states hold more registered Kindred than ever, all bound by paper as well as blood. The oldest unregistered ones start to sleep less and dream of their sires.

appr.t: Werewolf: Night City, Tokyo, Neo-Kowloon, Hamburg
appr.x: In the four great megacities the spirit world and the streets barely touch. Glass Walkers warn that the Weaver is close to severing them for good.
The Net is the largest Horizon realm there has ever been. Adepts and Nephandi alike feel its Avatar, if it has one, close to waking.
The Sorter has grown nearly as strong as an Earthbound. Heaven's servants and hell's are both waiting to see which side it takes.
The Kuei-jin are divided over the teachers, and the student's teachers are told the Wheel has noticed.

appr.t: Mage: Free States and Night City
appr.x: The Free States and Night City are one push away from belief in magic or belief in machines, and both the Traditions and the Union mean to use them to push the rest of the world.
The dead and the living talk every night, and the Labyrinth below is louder than it has ever been.
What is left of the Dreaming lives mostly in the Net, in the last large freeholds among the dream market's ruins, and no one knows if they will survive.
The hunt is a licensed trade with unions and quotas. Hunters who still hear the Messengers say the voices have begun counting down.
The Fallen hold more worshippers than any church. The walls of the Abyss crack under so many prayers aimed at the wrong ears.
The mummies are trusted by millions, and their oldest dreams are of the serpent Apophis turning in its sleep.
The last Accords collapse, and for the first time in years every imbued hears the Messengers speak at once.
The Sixth Age is plain to everyone. The Kuei-jin must choose whether to serve the end or stand against it.
Life and death are close to being one country, and the Underworld's storms can reach the waking world.
